News.title: Miami Airport didn’t install safety feature before deadly plane crash as expert warns landing ‘should’ve been aborted’
News.content:
MIAMI Airport was missing a critical safety feature which could have saved five victims of the horror Amazon plane crash, officials say.

The cargo jet barrelled off the runway at 129mph on Sunday before smashing into several cars – in what one expert has called a “complete dog’s breakfast” of a landing.



The Federal Aviation Administration today confirmed the airport lacked a vital safety system which prevents planes from sliding off runways.

The Engineered Material Arresting System (EMAS) uses crushable material at the end of a runway to help an aircraft stop in case of emergency.



Aviation expert Terry Tozer told Sam Homewood at The Sun’s new studio in the heart of the newsroom: “It looks as if this started going wrong a long way from the airport.”

He added: “If you look at all the data, it [the jet] landed halfway down the runway. I mean, you just don’t do that.”

read more world news CRASH HEARTBREAK Flight instructor mum and two sons, 10 & 13, killed in horror plane crash

EMAS systems have been installed at more than 120 airports nationwide and despite being one of the country’s busiest hubs, Miami International Airport does not have one.

While not compulsory, aviation authorities have warned for years that the safety system should be always be installed.



They say it has helped save at least 497 lives so far.

Commenting on the botched landing, Tozer said “extreme weather” meant the pilots should have tweaked their landing technique.

He also said they could have attempted to restart their approach by going back around and coming towards the runway again.



But a “trend” of pressure to land planes no matter the cost may have impacted their decision-making, Tozer added.

He said: “Unfortunately, there is a trend in certain areas to be like ‘we must get the job done’.”

The expert said the pilots “could have just aborted” the landing instead of touching down halfway through the runway.

Tozer added: “On the face of it, it looks like a complete mess.

“Quite honestly, unless they were dealing with some other malfunction that had completely distracted them on the flight gate, this looks like a complete dog’s breakfast of an approach from a long way out.”



The Amazon plane overran the tarmac just before 2pm on Sunday after arriving from San Juan, Puerto Rico.

It ploughed across a road used by warehouse workers and other businesses that surround the airport.

Concrete barriers designed to keep cars out of the secure area crumbled as the jet, weighing more than 100 tons, headed straight for the four-lane road.

Five people died, three were critically injured and two others were hospitalised with less severe injuries, officials said.

It is understood people were pinned inside their cars when the plane struck them, Miami-Dade County fire chief Ray Jadallah told reporters.



Harrowing emergency audio heard crews desperately trying to reach the burning Boeing 767 after it crashed to the tarmac.

In audio obtained by the Miami Herald, one crew member said: “The plane is on fire. The plane is on fire.

“Put your game faces on guys.”

Multiple fires broke out on and around the aircraft after the plane dragged vehicles across concrete before grinding to a halt.

Firefighters raced to get hoses close enough to the aircraft to douse the heavy flames and smoke pouring from the wreckage but as the plane’s engine was still running the operation was made near-impossible.



The live engine prevented firefighters from safely entering the aircraft to search for anyone trapped inside.

Firefighters were forced to flood the engine with water in an attempt to disable it.

Striking footage later shows emergency workers scaling a ladder to make their way into the cockpit of the charred Boeing 767-300.

It is understood, the pilot and co-pilot were trapped in the cockpit.

An investigation has been launched to understand why the cargo plane overran.



Kelly Nantel, Amazon spokesperson said: “We’re heartbroken to learn that five people lost their lives in today’s incident at Miami International Airport.

“Our deepest sympathies go out to the families, loved ones, and all those affected by this devastating loss.

“The airplane, which was operated by 21 Air, was attempting to land when this incident occurred.

“We’re working closely with local authorities and officials to learn more and will cooperate fully with any investigation.”

The catastrophe left Miami’s airport operating with just two of its normal four runways on a busy Labor Day.

News.title: Fears of a second mass ‘invasion’ as Ceuta border force on high alert over calls for march to ‘liberate enclave’
News.content:
FEARS of a second mass “invasion” are mounting in Ceuta after Spanish intelligence chiefs went on high alert over calls of a march to “liberate” the enclave.

National security forces are scrambling to monitor a Moroccan social media campaign urging crowds to descend on the Spanish territory on September 20.



The fresh threat comes as the last border breach on July 30 was also fuelled by a wave of social media messages calling on migrants to head for Ceuta.

Posters and messages written in Moroccan Arabic have began spreading online earlier this month, calling for a “march of anger” against Ceuta, Melilla and Spanish-held islands off the North African coast.



Campaigners are rallying supporters to “recover” the territories they claim are occupied by Spain.

The mobilisation is planned just days before Morocco’s legislative elections on September 23, with messages urging followers to take advantage of police being tied up at polling stations.



Moroccan journalist Mustapha El Asri has helped amplify the incendiary campaign, sharing posters calling for the recovery of “occupied” territories.

One message reads: “To recover Ceuta and Melilla and all the occupied territories.”

El Asri has also shared a video showing fans of MAS Fez displaying a banner declaring: “Ceuta and Melilla, two cities, one homeland: Morocco”.

Spanish intelligence agencies are now watching the online frenzy to establish whether it will remain a digital campaign or spill onto the border.



The National Intelligence Centre (CNI) and military intelligence agency CIFAS are both monitoring the threat.

Intelligence sources told Spanish newspaper El Español they are “on top of the issue” and working to contain the danger.

But the absence of an official organiser has left authorities facing a chilling question over how the September 20 mobilisation could unfold.



The poster gives no route or meeting point, raising fears the protest could suddenly mutate into an attempt to breach the border.

It comes just weeks after a huge influx into Ceuta which Spanish authorities later described as a planned operation rather than a spontaneous migration crisis.

A report by Spain’s National Centre for Immigration and Borders (CENIF), prepared at the request of the National Court, described the July 30 and 31 entry as “planned”.

The report also pointed to the presence and actions of Moroccan security forces, including what it described as the “active guidance” of migrant flows towards crossing points.

Now authorities are desperately watching for signs that the latest online calls are turning into concrete instructions, movements or fresh attempts to overwhelm the border.



The latest scare comes as thousands of migrants are still believed to be in Ceuta after the chaotic July breach.

Around 5,000 are estimated to remain in the enclave, with some sleeping on beaches, in parks, squares and on the streets.

The crisis has already triggered fury among residents, protests and a major security operation.



Spain has responded by deploying 500 additional Civil Guard officers to its 1,100-strong force in the enclave.

Tensions have also boiled over into violence.

More than 20 migrants were arrested after allegedly hurling rocks at a military patrol on Trampolín beach.

Police said a fight broke out before a group allegedly began pelting a nearby military patrol with stones.

Civil Guard officers were called in for support and were also reportedly targeted.



Just days earlier, two Moroccan nationals, aged 20 and 30, were arrested after allegedly attacking law enforcement officers trying to break up a violent fight on the same beach.

The crisis has also been linked to a string of shocking allegations, with Spanish prosecutors saying 23 sexual assaults have been reported in Ceuta since the end of July.

Nine of the alleged victims were children, while both local women and migrant girls have reportedly been among those targeted.

Several arrests have been made, with Ceuta chief prosecutor Silvia Rojas saying the majority of suspects were Moroccan or Spanish.

One man was also accused of breaking into a woman’s flat and creeping into her bed wearing only his underwear.



Meanwhile, horrific scenes on Trampolín beach have sparked outrage after a baby dolphin was allegedly dragged from the sea and beaten to death.



Footage reportedly shows migrants surrounding the distressed calf after it was pulled onto the rocks.

One man allegedly dragged the animal by its face before lifting it above his head as others gathered around.

A high-vis worker reportedly pleaded with him to put the dolphin down.

Local reports said the animal was allegedly struck on the head with a stick before it later died.

The incident prompted an online petition demanding those responsible be identified and prosecuted for animal cruelty.



It has added another explosive flashpoint to a crisis that has already left Ceuta residents fearing their city is spiralling out of control.

The July influx saw tens of thousands cross into the Spanish enclave, with migrants arriving on foot via the breakwater and swimming across Tarajal beach.

At least 145 migrants reportedly died during the crossing, triggering panic across the territory.

Many of those who entered later returned to Morocco, while others were rounded up by the army and placed in makeshift camps.

Those camps subsequently became targets of furious protests, with some set alight as residents demanded the authorities restore order.



The crisis has also ignited a political storm across Spain.

Mass rallies have been held across the country, with more than 200 cities reportedly hosting demonstrations over the government’s handling of the chaos.

The biggest crowds gathered in Madrid and Barcelona, where protesters waved Spanish flags and brandished anti-government signs.

PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo claimed more than 50,000 people packed into Madrid.

At the Madrid rally, Feijóo accused Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez of abandoning Ceuta, declaring: “A Spanish city has been invaded, occupied and, unfortunately, this happened with the knowledge of the Government of Spain.”



Vox leader Santiago Abascal meanwhile accused Sánchez of acting like “a lackey of the Moroccan regime”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Spanish Government has repeatedly rejected claims that it failed to respond quickly enough to the July crisis.

But with a fresh mobilisation now being whipped up online, authorities face a tense countdown to September 20.

News.title: I’ve been ‘banned’ from gardening outside my home after row with ‘petty’ housing chiefs over 1ft fence & flower bed
News.content:
FENCE OFF I’ve been ‘banned’ from gardening outside my home after row with ‘petty’ housing chiefs over 1ft fence & flower bed

A PENSIONER has claimed he has been banned from gardening outside his home after a row over his flower bed and a miniature 1ft fence.

Julian Phillips, 80, transformed what he described as a “mud field” outside his block of flats into a well-groomed lawn and colourful flower garden.



But he soon wound up in a feud with housing group Orbit, who branded his ankle-high picket fence a “trip hazard” and told him to stop tending the area.

“I can’t see what the problem is because people living here have complimented my work,” said Julian.



“All I do is try my best to make the garden look lovely for everyone who lives here.”

The group allegedly confiscated his lawnmower and asked him not to store it in the communal garage – a claim they deny.



The row first erupted two months ago, after green-fingered Julian decided to inject some life into the grounds surrounding the 31-flat development.

Julian laid down fresh turf, planted colourful flowers and installed a 1ft high fence to stop cars from driving over the garden.

However, Orbit promptly objected, insisting he take it down.

The housing association told him his workmanship raised “safety concerns” and failed to meet the “required specifications and standards”.

The group initially said they would remove the fence within seven days, but sent workmen three weeks later to rip it out.



They have further advised residents not to garden the area themselves as the area is already looked after by a contractor.

Frustrated by the ban, Julian claims he has not received any complaints about the garden from residents.

A spokesman for the housing association said: “We appreciate customers taking pride in where they live and wanting to help make communal

spaces look their best.

“However, the gardens at Helgate Court are a shared area for all

residents.

“Mr Philips’ concern relates to a separate fence, which was added without the agreement and support of other customers, who have told us they are worried about the fence when parking, as well as the safety of neighbours who use walking aids or mobility scooters.



“We can confirm that Mr Philips’ lawn mower has remained in his possession throughout.

“We will continue to work with all customers at Helgate Court to make sure the communal areas are safe, well maintained and enjoyable for everyone.”

News.title: Putin plotting ‘silent mobilisation’ for worst winter blitz yet… only Churchill grit can save Ukraine, says ex-general
News.content:
VLADIMIR Putin is plotting a “silent mobilisation” as Russia prepares to launch its deadliest winter blitz on Ukraine so far, an ex-general has said.

As the Kremlin’s full-scale war grinds into its fifth year, Putin is reportedly gearing up to unleash a 500,000-troop assault to “break the backbone” of the Ukrainian forces and “strike deep into Kyiv”.



The people of Ukraine have “no other option” but to prepare for the coming horrors, MEP and retired general Pekka Juhani Toveri said.

Toveri told The Sun: “Putin knows that the war isn’t going well.



“The frontline is basically frozen – there’s been very little movement this year.

“The challenge is to break the stalemate.”

Ukraine has spent the summer blitzing oil depots with state-of-the-art drones, before shifting its crosshairs to a series of strikes that have crippled Russia’s largest e-commerce platform.

The attacks have tanked Russia’s already reeling economy – wiping out businesses, suffocating trade and sparking nationwide fuel shortages.

Toveri said: “There’s a lot of pressure within the Russian society to end the war.

“So Putin will probably throw in everything he has this winter.”



Ukrainian Leader Volodymyr Zelensky has said Putin is planning to draft over 300,000 new recruits to help pummel Ukraine’s defences and take the rest of Donetsk.

Toveri said: “He will probably get about half a million guys, enough to break the backbone of the Ukrainian army.



“And at the same time they will hit Ukraine with deep strikes.”

Earlier this week Putin said Russia’s military had been “ordered to prepare and carry out mass strikes” on Ukraine’s energy facilities.

Russia will “likely” engage in a sustained bombing of electricity, water and heating systems in Kyiv this winter, Toveri said.

He added: “About 80% of the Ukrainian energy industry has taken hits through the war.



“Russia will try to cause a humanitarian crisis. Make the big Ukrainian cities inhabitable by cutting the energy, heat and water from those cities.”

And as Russia steps up its production of ballistic missiles – now at a rate of more than 100 a month – Kyiv’s supplies of interceptors have tumbled.

Ukraine is trying to get an additional 300 Patriot missiles from partners this winter, but there is no guarantee.

The Kremlin has denied the mobilization rumor for months – a decision that would pose a risk for Putin ahead of elections in September.

But Toveri said: “He will conduct some kind of mobilisation, probably not announced public mobilisation, but silent.”



Hundreds of thousands of people fled Russia after Putin decreed a partial mobilisation in 2022.

Since then, Russia has sustained 1.4 million casualties.

It comes amid reports of increasingly aggressive recruitment efforts in Penza – 388 miles southeast of Moscow.



Since June there have been reports of fighting-age men being forced into vehicles and taken to recruitment centres where they are then beaten or threatened into signing a military contract.

Putin is also making a series of strategic developments within his own armed forces to bolster Russia’s attack potential.

In early August, Denis Lyamin was announced as the head of Russia’s new Unmanned Systems forces.

The newly established military branch will be responsible for drone warfare.

Moscow has started to deploy a high-speed jet variant of its Iranian Shahed drone model – capable of reaching targets almost 620 miles away.



Named Geran-4 and Geran-5, the UAVs can evade air defence systems while carrying a 90kg payload, according to Ukrainian government documents leaked online.

These will now be launched alongside another 10,000 cheap Banderol cruise missiles during 2027, boosting Russia’s ability to bomb Ukraine’s infrastructure.

Civilian casualties have been rising as long-range attacks increase.



According to the UN, 437 civilians were killed and 2,610 injured in Ukraine in July – the highest since March 2022.

Toveri said: “It’s very clear that the challenge is to break their defensive lines.

“And they can break the backbone of Ukraine so that by next spring Ukraine would have to basically surrender and create the peace negotiations on Russian terms.”

Putin has shown no signs of backing down from his territorial demands despite successive US attempts to broker peace talks.

It comes after a weekend of peace talks saw Trump’s top aides visit both Moscow and Kyiv within 24 hours.



Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv on Sunday after holding “constructive and useful” talks with Putin in Moscow on Saturday.

Hopes for peace were thrown into doubt after Putin’s forces unleashed strikes across Kyiv on Friday night.

“No peace initiatives can help when you are fighting monsters whose goal is not peace, but the genocide of your people”, war commentator Denys Kazanskyi said.

It comes after a Russian drone struck the headquarters of Ukraine’s state security service (SBU) on Friday.

Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called the attack a “major escalation” that laid bare Russia’s “true trajectory of diplomacy”.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Toveri said: “There’s only one thing which is needed – the political will.

“And that, of course, is a problem in the West where we have a lot of politicians, but very few statemen and statewomen like Churchill, who dared to go and tell people that ‘now we are facing hard times, but we don’t have any other, any other option’.”

News.title: Man, 21, charged with murder after 19-year-old woman found with fatal gunshot wounds at home in London
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

MURDER PROBE Man, 21, charged with murder after 19-year-old woman found with fatal gunshot wounds at home in London

A 21-YEAR-OLD man has been charged with murder after a woman, 19, was shot and killed at a home in London.

Emergency services were called to a property in Finchley, at around 12.15am on June 8 where the teenager was pronounced dead at the scene.



A full investigation was launched by the Metropolitan Police following the death.

Police had initially responded to reports of gunshots – though the victim’s cause of death has not been confirmed with a post mortem set to take place.



Jamie Duncan has now been charged with murder and three counts of possession of a firearm.

He was arrested on Sunday, August 23, in Spain.

This followed a police appeal for Jamie’s whereabouts, with CCTV footage of the man being shared online.

Duncan appeared at the Old Bailey on Tuesday, September 1, where he was remanded into custody.

A trial is scheduled to begin at the Old Bailey on Monday, 7 June 2027.

Anyone with information has been urged to contact police via 101, quoting reference 34/8JUN or call Crimestoppers anonymously.

News.title: Dozens of explosives found near German power grid after mystery fire & ‘rocket’ attack in spiralling sabotage campaign
News.content:
DOZENS of explosives and homemade bombs have been discovered near German power grids in a mysterious series of suspected sabotage attacks.

Fires have broken out and rockets have hit energy facilities in recent days – as authorities probe the spiralling campaign of what is feared to be Russian shadow warfare.

At least 21 explosive devices have been uncovered across the Nato nation as part of Berlin’s probe so far.



This includes nine homemade bombs which were found over the weekend near high voltage power lines in Goerlitz.



Earlier today, an inferno broke out at a construction site in Berlin’s Mitte district before spreading to an energy substation.

Hours earlier, cops found “irregularities” at the Niederrhein substation, including a hole cut in one of its security fences, reports say.



Fears are mounting that Moscow could be behind several of these alleged explosive schemes – especially due to the Leipzig drone plot which has been directly linked to Russia.

Putin was accused of orchestrating the plan on August 4 which saw a bomb-rigged drone found near a fleet of jets and another UAV striking a plane mid-air.

Germany is even planning to create a protective shield to prevent attacks like the failed assault on Leipzig.



It could include vehicles and helicopters with specialists ready to defuse and intercept explosive devices, authorities say.

Authorities haven’t confirmed if Putin was behind the botched power grid attacks or not – and one left-wing activist has claimed to be behind some of them.

Daniel V, 48, reportedly admitted to several of the bomb ordeals in a letter.



Cops found what appeared to be explosives at his home after a raid but he is still at large.

A helicopter was scrambled between Remscheid-Lüttringhausen and Wuppertal-Ronsdorf on Monday morning.

And a 60-strong team of officers is investigating the letters in which he claimed responsibility for the schemes.



It comes after a worrying wave of suspected sabotage attacks last week.

On Tuesday morning, multiple explosives fitted to what appeared to be fireworks were found at a substation near the Jaenschwalde coal-fired power plant in Brandenburg.

Separately on the same day, a short circuit caused several power lines to go out of service at the Bergheim power substation near Cologne.

Both cases are being treated as deliberate attacks, local police said, and the probe came just one day after Berlin pointed the finger at Moscow for the botched Leipzig attack.

On Thursday, police also discovered a number of homemade rocket launchers at a substation in Dormagen.



The plots were uncovered amid concerns Europe is losing the growing “hybrid” war with Russia.

Nato allies have been warned they must come up with new methods to prevent the attacks, defence sources told the Financial Times.

One official said: “‘It is completely clear that we aren’t doing enough to deter sub-Article 5 provocations.

“We are providing enough deterrence to prevent Russian conventional and nuclear escalation… but we really need to rethink our approach to hybrid.”

The letter confessing to the plots allegedly written by Daniel V reportedly said his motivation was to protest Germany‘s growing reliance on fossil fuels.



The letter bizarrely contained both his name and address.

When officers stormed Daniel V’s home in Gevelsberg, North Rhine-Westphalia, on Friday, he was not there.

His lorry was found close by and about 100 cops searched a nearby forest with drones and search dogs.

Police released photographs of Daniel V on Saturday, as part of a public appeal for information.

News.title: Royal Navy sailor, 38, ‘took own life with assault rifle on warship after sex assault charge and marriage broke down’
News.content:
NAVY TRAGEDY Royal Navy sailor, 38, ‘took own life with assault rifle on warship after sex assault charge and marriage broke down’

A ROYAL Navy sailor took his own life on a warship after he was charged with sex assault allegations, an inquest heard.

Petty Officer Jon Errington Paxton suffered a fatal gunshot wound from an assault rifle on the HMS Cattistock while it was docked in Portsmouth.



The hearing was told PO Paxton, 38, had recently gone through a divorce with his partner and he had been accused of sexual assault.

He also had debts of up to £25,000 and told his partner at the time that “everybody would be better off without him”, it was said.



Area Coroner for Hampshire, Portsmouth, and Southampton, Jason Pegg, concluded that PO Paxton had taken his own life.

He said he had fired two rounds of ammunition, using an assault rifle on the ship.

The inquest was told in December 2022, PO Paxton had been arrested and charged with sexual assault while he was at home on medical unit discharge.

He had pleaded not guilty to the charges, but the trial had not yet taken place.

PO Paxton suffered from depression and anxiety and he was deemed medically unfit for several months, the court heard.

His brother Ross said he had struggled with his marriage breakdown and that he had said to him the “one thing he couldn’t live with was another man living in his own house with his kids”.



How to get help EVERY 90 minutes in the UK a life is lost to suicide It doesn’t discriminate, touching the lives of people in every corner of society – from the homeless and unemployed to builders and doctors, reality stars and footballers. It’s the biggest killer of people under the age of 35, more deadly than cancer and car crashes. And men are three times more likely to take their own life than women. Yet it’s rarely spoken of, a taboo that threatens to continue its deadly rampage unless we all stop and take notice, now. On April 19, 2023, Royal Navy Clearance Diver Matthew Moreton, who shared a cabin with PO Paxton, said he had gone to sleep with the keys to the weapons storage on his belt.

He told the court he was called to the weapons storage the following day, where a rifle was missing, along with ammunition.

The diver later found PO Paxton dead in the showers, it was said.

His death came 12 years after Samuel “Ricky” Hatton, 20, shot himself on the same warship at Portsmouth Naval Base.



The engineering technician had been affected by the death of Matthew “Spider” Webster, who died on board HMS Hurworth in Faslane, Argyll and Bute, in February that year.

Paying tribute to PO Paxton, his mother, Linda said: “I absolutely loved him. He had a great sense of humour. A really good lad.

“He loved his kids, loved being a dad. He loved his job, absolutely loved it. He joined up when he was 19.”

News.title: Lindsay Clancy jury’s hellish 6-week trial as 12 put lives on hold for 28 days before a single holdout led to mistrial
News.content:
THEY were plucked from a pool of ordinary residents and asked to put their lives on hold to sit through one of the most harrowing murder trials in America.

For six weeks, the jurors tasked with deciding Lindsay Clancy’s fate repeatedly returned to Plymouth Superior Court in Massachusetts to hear gut-wrenching evidence about the deaths of her three young children.



In total, 18 jurors sat through the same 21 days of disturbing testimony and evidence, not knowing who among them would ultimately be tasked with deciding the case.

It was only before deliberations began that six, three men and three women, were randomly designated as alternates, leaving a final jury of nine women and three men.



The alternates remained on standby and under the same restrictions in case one of the final 12 became unable to continue.

But after seven days of painstaking deliberations, the marathon trial ended in a mistrial on Friday when the jury failed to reach a unanimous verdict, with defense attorney Kevin Reddington blaming a lone male holdout.



Reddington claimed the jury was split 11 to 1 in favor of finding her not guilty by reason of lack of criminal responsibility, accusing the sole holdout of refusing to properly apply the law on reasonable doubt.

Clancy, 36, had pleaded not guilty to murdering Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and eight-month-old Callan, who were strangled with exercise bands inside the family’s Duxbury home in January 2023.

Reddington did not dispute that she killed the children, but argued she was not criminally responsible because she was suffering from postpartum psychosis.

Prosecutors fiercely disputed that account, arguing Clancy knew right from wrong and that the killings were premeditated.



The jurors listened to more than 80 witnesses, were confronted with hundreds of exhibits and endured deeply disturbing evidence, including autopsy photographs and the desperate 911 call made by Clancy’s then-husband Patrick.

The distressing recording captured the moments after Patrick returned to the family home on January 24, 2023, and discovered his wife badly injured outside after she had jumped from a second-floor window.

Jurors then heard his frantic search for the children after Clancy told him they were in the basement.

Patrick could be heard screaming as he discovered Cora, Dawson and Callan, before desperately attempting CPR as the dispatcher tried to guide him through efforts to save them.

Protester Kimberly Souza, 58, was in court when the recording, which was blocked from public release, was played.



She confirmed that some jurors were moved to tears as Patrick’s guttural screams echoed across the courtroom.

“It was absolutely heartbreaking,” Souza told The U.S. Sun. “You could hear Patrick screaming, and you could see how much it affected some of the jurors. Some of them were crying.”

The jurors were not sequestered and were allowed to return home each night, but were under strict orders not to read or watch news coverage, research the case online or discuss it with anyone throughout the trial.



Not a single juror dropped out or called in sick, something Reddington specifically praised, describing them as “very, very attentive.”

On one day, they were served food at around 1pm and chose to continue deliberating while they ate, rather than taking a full break.

Weeks later, the emotion was again etched across the jury’s faces as their mammoth task ended without a verdict.

The U.S. Sun was in the courtroom as jurors appeared disappointed after Judge William Sullivan finally declared a mistrial, bringing their seven days of deliberations to an abrupt end.

Some shook their heads as they remained seated in the jury box, while Reddington later described them as looking “defeated.”



Speaking outside court afterward, he said, “They spent seven weeks of their life on this case, and they were robbed too.”

He also highlighted the meager compensation jurors received while being asked to absorb weeks of traumatic evidence.

“They give them $50 a day to sit there and go through this horrific stuff,” he said.

“And no, they don’t give them any counseling. They don’t give them any care. They don’t give them anything.

“They just say, ‘Thank you for your service and see you later.'”



Reddington also slammed the lone holdout juror.

“They know that they were robbed by one man, for whatever his agenda was, who stole seven weeks of the life of these other jurors that were so attentive, so beautiful, so wonderful,” he said.

“You could see how defeated they were sitting there.

“I got a funny feeling they would’ve gone on for another week if they had to. So I hope that guy can sleep well at night.”

The identities of the jurors, including the male holdout, are still being shielded from the public.



They entered and left the court through a separate entrance away from the media, with Sullivan issuing an order prohibiting anyone from filming or photographing them.

The tight security was highlighted when Clancy supporter Dawn Light, 56, was arrested after allegedly entering a restricted parking area and filming jurors as they left court.

She pleaded not guilty to a charge of witness intimidation and was later ordered to stay away from the courthouse and have no contact with jurors or witnesses.

Judge Sullivan ordered the official list identifying the empaneled jurors to be impounded for 14 days, citing the “significant and divisive attention” the case had attracted locally, nationally and internationally.

Unless Sullivan extends the order for “good cause,” it will expire two weeks after it was issued, meaning the names could then become publicly accessible through the court.



But the temporary order does not gag the jurors themselves.

Massachusetts’ official juror handbook states that jurors are no longer prohibited from talking about a trial once they have been dismissed, although it advises them to avoid revealing the identities of fellow jurors, how another juror voted or what was said during private deliberations.

However, that language is guidance rather than a blanket criminal prohibition.

If any of the Clancy jurors do decide to tell their story, they could potentially be paid for it.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

There is no blanket Massachusetts prohibition preventing a former juror from being paid for a media interview, documentary appearance or book about their own experience after their service has ended.



Were you a juror in the Lindsay Clancy case? If you want to share your experience following the mistrial, contact The U.S. Sun at exclusive@the-sun.com.

News.title: Hero lifeguard, 55, saves four Brit family members from drowning in Fuerteventura sea
News.content:
Hero lifeguard, 55, saves four Brit family members from drowning in Fuerteventura sea

The 55-year-old lifeguard was praised by other rescuers for being physically fit enough to reach the family, despite them being far out to sea, and keeping them afloat until help arrived

View 2 Images The British family got into difficulty at the Fuerteventura beach (Image: LightRocket via Getty Images)

A hero lifeguard, aged 55, has been praised after he saved four members of a British family from drowning in Fuerteventura.

‌



The lifeguard was praised for rescuing the Brits after they got into serious difficulty on the Spanish island's Grandes Playas de Corralejo. He reportedly spotted the four Brits struggling in the water a considerable distance away from shore at about 2.30pm (local time) on Friday.

‌



The lifeguard had been keeping watch in his tower when he spotted several people struggling a ways offshore. He immediately left his post, running down th ebeach before entering the sea to swim out toward the family.

‌



View 2 Images The lifeguard rescued the family of four (Image: LightRocket via Getty Images)

Survivors pulled alive from flooded Nepal tunnels after more than a week trapped READ MORE :

After reaching the holidaymakers the lifeguard was able to keep all four of them afloat as he waited for rescue teams to arrive. A rescue jet ski later arrived with two lifeguards on board, who helped bring the Brits back to shore.

When they arrived back on the beach, the rescuers found a teenager under the age of 18 was showing signs of suffering a non-fatal drowning, reports the Canarian Weekly. The lifeguards treated the child and alerted the Canary Islands Emergency Service.

‌



Paramedics arrived at the beach a few minutes later and transported the teen to a hospital where they were treated further. They were admitted but according to reports are out of danger.

Other lifeguards praised the 55-year-old's fitness and believe his intervention prevented a tragedy. He was able to swim a considerable distance from the shore and kept the four people afloat until other rescuers arrived, both requiring significant displays of strenght and endurance.

His heroic efforts meant the Brits were able to stay above water for long enough to be reached by the rescue jet ski, which could bring them back to safety. Following the rescue, there have been calls for more information, warnings and restrictions to be displayued in multiple languages.

Article continues below

The lifeguards believe multilingual signs could help prevent tourists from misunderstanding warnings about dangerous conditions at sea as Fuerteventura attracts visitors from across Europe, and even further afield. They have argued that making sure beachgoers can easily understand safety instructions could help prevent fatal incidents, especially on beaches where currents and challenging sea conditions may not be immediately clear to inexperienced swimmers.

The rescue comes after a Brit died in Fuerteventura after suffering a cardiac arrest while being saved from the sea by helicopter earlier this year. The man was found by rescuers aboard the emergency rescue helicopter in June.

After being winched to safety, crews found he was in cardiac arrest an immediately began CPR while transporting him to a nearby landing site. Paramedics, a medical helicopter crew and staff from a local health centre attempted to resuscitate him on the ground, but he was pronounced dead at the scene. A second swimmer managed to reach the shore without assistance and was treated on the beach by paramedics.

News.title: Dad spent three weeks at wrong teen’s bedside before learning son, 18, had died
News.content:
Dad spent three weeks at wrong teen’s bedside before learning son, 18, had died

Joshua Johnson, 18, and Summer Louise Scott, 17, died when a Toyota Corolla left the road at Todwick, near Rotherham, while another passenger was initially misidentified as the male who had died.

View 3 Images Joshua Johnson, 18, died in the crash near Rotherham. (Image: Facebook)

A dad says “it felt like two deaths” after spending three weeks at the wrong teenager’s bedside before learning his son had died in a car crash, an inquest heard.

‌



Joshua Johnson, 18, and Summer Louise Scott, 17, died when a Toyota Corolla left Todwick Road, at Todwick, near Rotherham, and hit a tree in the early hours of December 13 last year, inquests in Doncaster heard on Monday.

‌



A previous hearing was told how police originally misidentified front seat passenger Trevor Wynn, then 17, as the male who had died in the crash, with Mr Wynn’s family believing he was dead until he came out of sedation three weeks later, on January 4.

‌



At the same time, Mr Johnson’s family sat at the bedside of seriously injured Mr Wynn, not realising their son was dead.

View 3 Images The mistake was discovered when Trevor Wynn came out of sedation (Image: Jonathan Stoner / SWNS)

A statement from Mr Johnson’s father, Lee Johnson, was read at Doncaster Coroner’s Court on Monday, where a coroner ruled his son was unlawfully killed.

‌



Mr Johnson explained how he and his wife spent weeks at the Royal Hallamshire Hospital, in Sheffield, believing they were sitting with their serious injured son, only to be told there had been a mistake.

He said: “This information came as a huge shock and I cannot comprehend it. It felt like, as a family, we had two deaths. I felt I had missed out on the initial grieving part of the process.”

Senior coroner Nicola Mundy read the statement of Detective Chief Inspector Andy Knowles, of South Yorkshire Police, who told the court in January how the mix-up began when a number of items of personal property were found at the scene, “though were not physically about the person of either of the males”.

‌



One of these items was a phone in a case, which also contained Joshua Johnson’s driving licence. A second phone nearby contained medical ID information in the name of Trevor Wynn, and a bank card in the same name was also attached.

View 3 Images Mr Johnson’s family described him a “gentle giant” (Image: South Yorkshire Police / SWNS)

Mr Knowles told the court earlier this year how an officer used this information to trace Trevor Wynn’s mother, who provided a college ID card, as well as a description of his build and footwear.

‌



The senior officer said: “That officer then took this ID card to Rotherham Mortuary where, at that time, the deceased victim of the collision was booked in as an unknown male.

“Upon considering the comparison between the male’s features against the ID, and also considering the descriptive details of build and clothing, the officer was satisfied that this was the body of Trevor Wynn.”

Mr Knowles said a second officer, with the surviving but sedated teenager, was told this person was Joshua Johnson by colleagues at the crash site, and was able to obtain a photograph from Mr Johnson’s driving licence.

‌



He said: “The officer liaised with medical staff and the photograph was compared against the casualty. Those present were then satisfied that this person was Joshua Johnson.”

Mr Knowles explained how he set out establishing the true identity of the deceased male with “no further reliance in this case on visual recognition as a form of ID” and this was done using dental records.

On Monday, separate inquests were held into the deaths of Mr Johnson and Miss Scott. Senior Rotherham Coroner Nicola Mundy heard how Miss Scott was was driving the Toyota and lost control as she approached a slight bend.

‌



The car went across a verge and hit a low wall which caused it to roll in the air before it struck a mature tree almost 50m from the road.

The inquests heard how police investigators used the tracking app Life360, which was on one of the phones in the car, to determine that the car was travelling at 95mph for about a kilometre before the crash happened, and had slowed to 86mph about 130m before the bend.

Forensic collision investigator Peter Gallagher said it was the first time his team had used this technique. Mr Gallagher said tests showed the maximum speed at which the bend could be safety negotiated was 68mph.

‌



The inquest heard how Miss Scott had a provisional driving licence but had not passed her test. Pc Joe Binley said two men were arrested who were in a car which was following the Toyota.

He said officers investigated whether the cars had been racing but evidence, including a Snapchat video of the crash filmed by someone in the second car, showed there was a distance between the vehicles and it was Miss Scott’s decision to drive in the way she did.

Miss Scott had told friends there was an issue with the brakes on her car but the inquest heard there were no defects found on the vehicle which would have contributed to the crash.

‌



The coroner heard that Miss Scott’s family described her as “loving, caring and very funny” but also “fierce and sassy”. They said she had a long-standing love of cars.

Mr Johnson’s family described him as a “gentle giant” with a “massive heart” who had a “bright future ahead that was tragically cut short”. The coroner concluded that Miss Scott died as a result of a road traffic collision and Mr Johnson was unlawfully killed.

Earlier this year, the police watchdog, which is investigating the misidentification error, said it was “clear something has gone very wrong”, leading to “awful consequences” for the two families.

Article continues below

A spokesman for the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said on Monday that the investigation was “at an advanced stage” and they hoped it would conclude “in the coming weeks”.

South Yorkshire Assistant Chief Constable Colin McFarlane said: “We recognise the shock and significant distress caused by the misidentification following the collision on Todwick Road, and the unimaginable consequences this had for the families involved. Only those involved can truly understand.”

Mr McFarlane said the force took immediate steps to review processes and will look at the findings of the IOPC, when it reports. He said work is ongoing to ensure all officers are confident following new guidance issued by the College of Policing in August.

News.title: Darren Lewis: 'Reform’s hate is turning elders into monsters'
News.content:
Have we misjudged the concern about radicalisation in plain sight? For so long we’ve worried about the impact of extremists on kids, teenagers and young men. And yet when you watch the footage from the Reform conference last week, of two female hecklers being attacked by senior citizens, your jaw will drop.

Because it leads you to ask whether sections of our British pensioners have been fanaticised by the corporate lobby group with just eight MPs. Older voters push back against extremists in France and Germany, despite Sunday’s success for the far right in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt.

But Reform’s xenophobes appear to have gained traction with sections of the UK’s senior citizens, judging by their conduct last week. The incidents, caught on camera and beamed around the world, leave you convinced that serious chats are needed around a few dinner tables among some extended families around the country.

View 3 Images Robert Jenrick, Reform's wannabe chancellor (Image: Victoria Jones/Shutterstock)

‌



At times the images looked like scenes from a zombie movie, where victims disappear under a sea of flailing arms. In one incident, for example, older men drag a young woman to the ground while one appeared to jab and strike her with a walking stick.

A man wearing a white, open-necked shirt and jeans then appeared to stamp on or kick the clearly terrified woman while another hand appeared from nowhere, gripping her on the back of her neck.

So much for Reform wanting to protect our young women and girls. Or for their claim to be protectors of free speech. The woman is also pushed to the ground and struck from behind with what appears to be a walking stick.

In another incident, a woman is manhandled by four or five men while an older lady is violently yanking her hair and a bespectacled man appears to be pulling at her face and mouth repeatedly and forcefully from behind.

‌



At least two female protesters have spoken out, detailing their fear, their ripped clothes and their injuries. The response of Reform would-be Chancellor, Robert Jenrick, to critics of the attendees’ conduct, said it all.

View 3 Images Reform UK party leader Nigel Farage reacts after a woman threw a drink over him, as he launches his election candidacy at Clacton Pier on June 4, 2024 (Image: Getty Images)

“Oh boo hoo,” he said. “You take your chances if you go to a party conference and you try to mess it up. We are now in a country where a far-left protester goes into a party conference, tries to wreck the leader’s speech, and cries foul if a pensioner knocks her over the head with a Zimmer frame. Come on, get a life.”

This was the same Jenrick who took to social media when Farage had a drink thrown at him and, rightly, deplored the act, demanding police action. To be fair to Reform chairman “30p” Lee Anderson, he did go on stage to claim he “does not condone” that behaviour.

‌



But given he also joked that a “whip round” was needed to buy a new walking stick for a man who used his cane to hit a protester, Anderson clearly appeared to be speaking out of both sides of his mouth.

And while the focus will be on the MPs, the bigger picture is frightening. We need to ask whether our older contingent have successfully been radicalised by the scare tactics and the xenophobes determined to divide us as a society.

That they would treat young women who could easily be their children or even grandchildren in the manner that they did at that conference is chilling. It shows a slavish devotion to the purveyors of hate reminiscent of the kind of thing we’ve seen in the movies.

As for those purveyors of hate – well, no man who responds to any woman being violently attacked with the words “boo hoo” should ever be remotely close to government.

News.title: Body exhumed in police probe into ‘unexplained’ death of woman in Telford
News.content:
Body exhumed in police probe into ‘unexplained’ death of woman in Telford

Police are investigating the death of a woman in Telford which is now being treated as "unexplained" after a man had been arrested on suspicion of murder

View 3 Images Police at Fenns Meadow Green Burial Ground, where a woman’s body was exhumed. (Image: Iconic Media Group / SWNS)

A body has been exhumed in an investigation into the "unexplained" death of a woman in Telford.

Officers from West Mercia Police went to Fenns Meadow Green Burial Ground near Whitchurch, Shropshire, early this morning (September 7) to recover the body of the woman, who died in 2022.

Images from the scene showed police in hazmat suits and forensic officers working behind a cordon, with blue tents also set up.

The investigation was launched after the force was contacted by Essex Police with information about the death of the woman earlier this year.

A 62-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of murder in May and has been bailed amid enquiries.

View 3 Images A body has been exhumed amid an investigation (Image: Iconic Media Group / SWNS)

Police said enquiries are continuing and the woman's death is now being treated as "unexplained".

Detective Chief Inspector Lee Holehouse, from the Major Investigations Unit, said police were unable to release further details while the investigation remained ongoing.

He explained: "On Wednesday 6 May 2026, we were contacted by Essex Police after information was given to them regarding the death of a 57-year-old woman in Telford in 2022.

View 3 Images An officer in a hazmat suit at the scene during the exhumation (Image: Iconic Media Group / SWNS)

"An investigation was then launched by West Mercia Police, and a 62-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of murder. He has since been released on police bail as enquiries continue.

"As part of the ongoing investigation, which is now being treated as an unexplained death, this morning (Monday 7 September) officers have completed the exhumation of a grave at Fenns Meadow Green Burial Ground near Whitchurch, Shropshire.

Article continues below

"The activity at the cemetery is unrelated to the burial ground, but we would like to thank Fenns Meadow Green for their cooperation and assistance while we carried out this complex operation.

"Due to the ongoing investigation we are unable to release further details at this time but will do so when we are able to."

News.title: Kelsey Parker shares heartbreaking message as she prepares to give birth
News.content:
Kelsey Parker shares heartbreaking message as she prepares to give birth

Widow Kelsey Parker, 36, is expecting a 'rainbow' baby less than a year after the tragic stillbirth of her son Phoenix, saying it feels like a 'gift from heaven'

View 4 Images Kelsey Parker shared a picture of her at a hospital appointment (Image: @being_kelsey/Instagram)

Kelsey Parker says she is ready to give birth to her 'rainbow' baby after years of unimaginable grief.

‌



The 36-year-old widow of The Wanted singer Tom revealed last June that the baby she was expecting with partner Will Lindsay – a son they had already named Phoenix – was stillborn at 39 weeks, compounding an already devastating few years of loss.

‌



The agony of the stillbirth happened some three years after Tom died of an inoperable brain tumour in March 2022, aged just 33, which left her to raise their two children, Aurelia and Bodhi, alone. And with the loss of Phoenix leaving another vast hole, she and Will have been tested in ways they could never have imagined.

‌



Now she is pregnant again and with the new arrival close to being welcomed into the world, Kelsey is in reflective mood.

4 View 4 Images She can't wait to meet her 'rainbow baby' soon (Image: @being_kelsey/Instagram) 4 View 4 Images She is 'excited' by what's ahead after a harrowing few years (Image: Alan West/Hogan Media/Shutterstock)

‌



The podcaster and actress says she is so excited despite her harrowing experience and shared her emotions as she took to social media to tell fans how she is feeling.

"This time last year I couldn’t imagine wanting anything again," she wrote in a lengthy post, which she uploaded alongside a snap on her in a hospital bed with kids Aurelia, 6, five-year-old Bodhi.

"I remember sitting at home and genuinely believing that was it. That the rest of my life was going to be something I got through rather than something I lived. "And now there’s a baby about to arrive. I want to be really honest about what that feels like, because I don’t think anyone says it out loud.

‌



"It doesn’t feel like the end of the grief. It feels like carrying two enormous things at once and hoping my arms hold. I am so excited. I am also missing Phoenix so much this week that it takes my breath away. Both. At the same time. Every single day.

View 4 Images Tragic Tom Parker died of an inoperable brain tumour in March, 2022 (Image: Dave Benett Library)

"If you’re waiting for one feeling to finish before the other one is allowed to start it doesn’t work like that. They just live together in the end. And somehow that’s alright. "If you needed to hear this today, save it and send it to someone who does."

‌



Confirming in June, she said: “A year ago next month, we lost our beautiful baby boy, Phoenix. And somehow, through all the heartbreak, it feels like Tom and Phoenix have sent us another little gift from heaven, our little rainbow baby.”

She had opened up to OK! about enduring yet more agony, while trying to remain upbeat for the sake of her family. “I’m doing better,” she says. “All you can do is look forward. Last year was really tough, but I’m still here, I’m still living. I still have two healthy children, so I think you can only move forward and look forward.”

At the time of Phoenix’s death, Kelsey posted a poignant poem online titled ‘Born Sleeping, Forever Loved’. It was accompanied by a caption that said, “Phoenix Parker-Lindsay, you will forever be loved.”

‌



At the time of his death, Kesley wrote a touching tribute on Instagram which said, “Our hearts are broken, Tom was the centre of our world and we can’t imagine life without his infectious smile and energetic presence.” She added, “We are truly thankful for the outpouring of love and support and ask that we all unite to ensure Tom’s light continues to shine for his beautiful children.”

She and Tom first met on a night out in 2009 before he found fame with The Wanted, and she once described their connection as “love at first sight.” After a two-year engagement, they married in Surrey in 2018, with Tom’s bandmates Max George and Jay McGuinness both there to witness them walk down the aisle.

In June 2019, Kelsey and Tom welcomed daughter Aurelia, now six, before Bodhi, five, arrived in October 2020. Today, Kelsey makes sure she keeps their dad’s memory alive through “happy” daily conversations with them both, as well as through discussions with Will.
