News.title: Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week
News.content:
At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

News.title: Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions
News.content:
This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his new club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

News.title: Antonelli walks on water while Hamilton rages from mountaintop
News.content:
The 20-year-old also benefited from a perfectly-timed (from his perspective at least) mid-race virtual safety car when Lance Stroll retired his Aston Martin, which allowed Antonelli a cheap stop to switch to fresh mediums while Russell stayed out on used hards. But at some point you just have to take your hat off to the youngster.

Antonelli was irresistible. He had already surged from 19th on the grid to 12th by the time the red flag came out at the end of lap 2. He was up to sixth a couple of laps after the race resumed. And by lap 18 of a 53-lap race, he had passed Russell for the lead for the first time. That is some going.

Having caught up to Russell, the two Mercedes drivers engaged in an entertaining battle for a few laps, the pair of them yo-yoing in and out of the lead before Russell got past Antonelli on lap 23 and managed to make it stick.

But the key moment of the race came on lap 27 when Stroll stopped at the first chicane and the VSC came out. For Antonelli, the decision to switch to fresh mediums was clear. He was going to struggle to make it to the end of the race. Far better to drop a few positions and fight back on fresh rubber.

For Russell, it was far trickier. He was in the lead of the race. He was on hard tyres which he knew could get to the end of the race. And he also had the problem of Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, who at the time he was struggling to shake off.

Mercedes chose to keep Russell out there. In hindsight, it may have been the wrong decision. Had he stopped at that point, he would at least have stayed ahead of Antonelli, and on the same tyres. By staying out, he kept the lead but found himself relentlessly hunted down by the Italian.

By lap 49, the Italian had caught up to him. Antonelli botched his first attempt at reclaiming the lead, going wide onto the gravel at the first chicane. But he made no mistake one lap later as Russell was once again left licking his wounds.

News.title: VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling
News.content:
“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just said he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

News.title: Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw
News.content:
A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

News.title: Relentless Springboks give All Blacks 15 minutes of hell to lead series
News.content:
There will be no repeat of the All Blacks historic Test series victory in South Africa 30 years ago, after the home side ruthlessly ensured they will lead 2-1 going into the concluding weekend.

And the manner in which the Springboks blew away their fierce rivals in the last 15 minutes made Rassie Eramus’s men overwhelming favourites to finish the job in America next Saturday.

However, there were passages of this brutal battle that suggested that Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry could still produce a finale worthy of the billing if New Zealand can learn the lessons from this brutal encounter at the FNB Stadium in Johannesburg.

There was a late Kiwi try to give the scoreboard a humdinger hue but Erasmus’s side were well deserving of their second victory in as many Saturdays over their fierce rivals, and credit to the South Africa coach for outwitting counterpart Dave Rennie without needing to change his starting XV just before the kick-off, like he did seven days before.

Amazing what one can do with a simple but chilling game plan. The old scoundrel knew that if he slowed it down and let his scrum walk round the All Blacks scrum that his backs would have the precious space.

Yet, however it might feel away from Springbok turf, New Zealand will still fancy their chances of levelling it, especially after matching their opponents’ haul of four tries. Their fly-half, Ruben Love, missed five simple-enough points and until that last quarter it was an even contest. Yet, as it tends to, South Africa’s physical intensity and their almighty scrum eventually prevailed.

News.title: Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of and qualifying for the Monza Grand Prix.

Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he said.

“It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”

Russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

However, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

Perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

Russell has not secured pole for the last four races, so a strong showing in qualifying might be the boost he needs ahead of Sunday’s race, while Norris is looking for a pole position hat-trick.

Sports.title: Forgotten Tottenham flop Serge Aurier to join seventh-tier minnows who conceded TEN at the weekend
Sports.content:
FORMER Tottenham player Serge Aurier is poised to plunge his career to new depths – by joining a SEVENTH-TIER club in France.

The Ivory Coast defender helped Spurs reach the 2019 Champions League final during a four-year stay in north London.



The £23milliion buy from Paris Saint-Germain made 110 club appearances, scoring eight goals, before leaving in 2021.

He later spent two years with Nottingham Forest.



Aurier, 33, has been a free agent since leaving Iranian giants Persepolis earlier this year.

The right-back is now in talks with French minnows Montigny-en-Gohelle, who are based eight miles east of Lens.

Playing in the second division of the Hauts-de-France regional league, they conceded TEN goals at the weekend to rivals Biache-Saint-Vaast.

Aurier’s deal is reportedly being held up due to delays with documents from the Iranian FA.

But sources close to the defender told local paper La Voix du Nord they expect him to get the green light to sign imminently.

Aurier began his career at Lens, coming through their academy and making his professional debut.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

He has recently been appointed the northern club’s Under-15 coach, but plans to keep his playing career alive with Montigny.

Aurier won 11 trophies with PSG, and has twice helped Ivory Coast lift the Africa Cup of Nations.

He has also played for Toulouse, Villarreal and Galatasaray – helping the Turkish side win the Super Lig title in 2024.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace under investigation over use of ILLEGAL sub during win at the weekend with refs also in firing line
Sports.content:
CRYSTAL PALACE have landed themselves in hot water after breaking Women’s Super League rules in their season-opening win.

The newly-promoted Eagles sealed a 1-0 victory over Everton thanks to Lexi Lloyd-Smith’s first half strike on Sunday.



But WSL chiefs have launched an investigation after Palace used four substitution windows during the showdown.

Competition rules state clubs can only make changes in a maximum of three stoppages in play.



And Palace are now at the centre of a probe which could result in being slapped with a severe punishment.

A WSL statement read: “We can confirm there was a breach of competition rules in the Crystal Palace versus Everton match.

“Crystal Palace used a fourth substitution opportunity during a fourth stoppage in play, when the rules permit a maximum of three substitution opportunities per match.

“We will now conduct an investigation alongside both clubs and Pro Ref and update in due course.”

The WSL does not have an automatic penalty for substitution rule breaches.

But Palace may be referred to an independent tribunal, which would have the power to impose a warning, fine, points deduction or other sporting sanctions including replaying the clash.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The Eagles breached WSL rules in the seventh minute of stoppage time, when Kirsty Howat replaced Shannon O’Brien.

Palace boss Jo Potter had already used three separate substitution windows to send on Abbie Larkin, Ashleigh Weerden and Allyson Swaby.

It has been confirmed the investigation will involve both clubs and referee body Pro Ref.

And the match officials for Palace’s win over Everton, including whistleblower Megan Wilson, have been stood down from the next round of fixtures after failing to comply with regulations.



Palace were promoted to the WSL last season after grabbing the runners-up spot in the second-tier.

The Eagles are facing a daunting task when they make the short trip to Arsenal on Sunday.

Sports.title: Flop Chelsea boss Liam Rosenior’s incredible ‘f*** that’ team-talk goes viral with minnows Paris FC flying in Ligue 1
Sports.content:
EX-CHELSEA flop manager Liam Rosenior is going viral for his team talk after Paris FC beat Nice 3-0 in Ligue 1 last week.

Paris are currently second in the league on seven points, and five above city rivals PSG.



New boss Rosenior has had a brilliant start to the season, with his side also shocking Marseille 3-2 this weekend.

He was mocked at Chelsea for his communication skills, but a fantastic video of him riling up his team last week is now doing the rounds.



After Paris beat Nice, he said: “Football is everything. You have to take care of that f*****g ball.

“I want us to either keep possession or enter the tackle. Stay concentrated. I do not want us to survive our way through the game and win 1-0. F*** that.



“That is not what we are here for. Play. Go and get the second goal. We scored and then went ‘ok. We are 1-0 up.’

“No, no no. Not now. Not now. The game is 0-0. Go and get the second goal.

“You do that by playing positively and using the space in behind their back line.”

Paris play Lyon next, and face a mega local derby against the European champions PSG in mid-December.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Rosenior joined Paris in July, just three months after leaving his role at Chelsea.

The Englishman only lasted three months as manager of the Blues, and has jumped straight back in to ensure that calamitous tenure does not define his managerial career.

Sports.title: Why Man Utd did not sign a defender despite up to SIX leaving next year as leaky backline costs them again at Everton
Sports.content:
SIX GOALS conceded in three games is bad enough for Manchester United. Worse yet, they did not even sign a defender in the summer.

United’s only defensive-minded signing – defensive midfielder Carlos Baleba – is recovering from an ankle injury. Two of their back four at Everton are in their 30s while full backs Diogo Dalot and Luke Shaw are the longest-serving members in the squad.



There will be a revamp of the defence next summer, but this season is not even a month old and United will have to get by.

Defence was never a priority for United as they have the manpower: nine senior defenders and almost all of them can play in a variety of roles. That is more than the average two players per position in a back four.



United were left with Kobbie Mainoo as the only senior and available central midfielder after Manuel Ugarte ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament. Mainoo has been joined by Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba.

The quantity of defenders was the main reason why United did not reinforce it. With five centre halves, there was no room for an addition.



And also no market. Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven, aged 20 and 19, joined only two seasons ago and are long-term investments. Harry Maguire signed a contract renewal in April.

Matthijs de Ligt is recovering from a back injury that has sidelined him since November, so was unsellable. There were never going to be any takers for the injury-prone Lisandro Martinez, considered a first-teamer when fit.

United did not receive any offers for right backs Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui, two experienced options they have settled for, or are saddled with, for a third successive season.

It is well-known that United wanted a new left back. Lewis Hall was their preferred choice and Myles Lewis-Skelly was available but for a steep fee in excess of £50million.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

United never got far down the line with Hall but Newcastle would have priced them out of a move for the £70m-rated left back. If Hall’s resale value does not drop, he could command a world record fee for a full back next summer.

In all likelihood, United will go back in for Hall in 12 months’ time. Shaw has entered the final year of his contract and could be released after 13 years at the club.

United could also let Maguire go next year. Martinez, whose contract is expected to be extended until 2028, is effectively on trial ahead of a definitive decision on his future.

With Martinez, Dalot, Mazraoui and Harry Amass all likely to have one year left on their deals next summer, United could get rid of up to six defenders if they wish to drastically dismantle their defence.



Maguire is the vice-captain and has started in all 18 games he has been available for under Carrick. His contract includes a one-year option that could be triggered, depending on his fitness and form over the coming months.

Amass, 19, has at least four months to cement himself as a worthy senior squad member.

But already Carrick has thrown on a centre back at right back (Yoro) and a right back at left back (Mazraoui) to the team’s detriment.

Hooking Shaw in the 91st minute with United 2-1 up at Everton had dire consequences. Yoro was narrow, Patrick Dorgu switched to the right wing to offset that, but went rogue with some pointless pressing.



Mazraoui, sent on in added time, attempted a panicky prod at the ball and it was swept in by Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

Sports.title: BBC pundit Ashley Williams lands first senior coaching role in major career change 6 years after retiring from football
Sports.content:
ASHLEY WILLIAMS has been appointed to Craig Bellamy’s backroom staff with Wales.

Ex-Dragons captain Williams played 86 times for his country and led Chris Coleman’s men on their incredible run to the Euro 2016 semi-finals.



The 42-year-old has been a Match of the Day pundit for the BBC and has also worked for talkSPORT.

Former Swansea and Everton centre-back Williams is a Uefa A Licence holder and has coached at Wales youth level but this is his first senior role as one of Bellamy’s assistant coaches.



Ex-Swans coach Alan Sheehan is also joining Bellamy’s staff as a No2 for the autumn Nations League matches, which start against Cristiano Ronaldo‘s Portugal on September 24.

The League A clash in Lisbon is followed by an away day in Denmark before home fixtures with Erling Haaland‘s Norway and the Danes in Cardiff.



Bellamy, who was set to join Burnley in the summer before the move collapsed at the 11th hour, has been on the hunt for new coaches.

The Wales boss lost both Piet Cremers and James Rowberry in recent months.

Cremers quit to take on the head coach role at Club Brugge’s youth academy in the Belgian second tier.

While Rowberry opted to focus on his day-to-day job as No2 to Mark Robins at Stoke.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Tottenham assistant Andrew Crofts, who joined Roberto De Zerbi from Brighton, will remain in his Welsh post as Bellamy’s right-hand man.

Bellamy is in the third year of his four-year contract with the Football Association of Wales (FAW) having failed to qualify for the World Cup.

He names his squad for the Nations League fixtures in Cardiff next Tuesday.

Sports.title: Harry Kane ‘amazed’ by ‘very silly’ feat last season that beats Cristiano Ronaldo and puts him second only to Messi
Sports.content:
EVEN Harry Kane is flabbergasted by his “very silly” haul of 73 goals last season.

The England captain’s outrageous campaign for Bayern Munich and his country is the second highest in history.



His staggering tally is behind only the 82 netted by footballing deity Lionel Messi for Barcelona and Argentina in the 2011-12 term.

Kane admitted his mind has been blown by his own achievement, which feels “surreal” given his 61 strikes for Bayern is 20 more than his best-ever campaign with old club Tottenham.



The 33-year-old told TNT: “Seventy-three goals is just a crazy number.

“If I was young and I was watching someone do that, I’d be like, “oh, my God”.

“I grew up watching Messi and (Cristiano) Ronaldo every night, dominating, dominating.

“Obviously, Messi is the only one to score more (with) 82.

“In some of the other seasons, Ronaldo’s highest was 69 – these are numbers that I just thought were just very silly, which they are.

“They are the greatest of our generation for sure and arguably of all-time.



“Seventy-three goals, even for me – I’m pretty amazed by that.”

Kane was ultra prolific at Spurs, becoming the North Londoners’ record scorer with 280 goals in 435 appearances, including two campaigns where he netted 30 in the Premier League.

But his net-busting exploits have reached another level in Bayern, whom he joined from Spurs in 2023, where he is now on 148 goals in 151 games.

Though, ironically, he is yet to get off the mark in two Bundesliga games so far this term – a relative drought for the super striker.

Speaking to ex-Bayern midfielder Owen Hargreaves, Kane continued: “It’s hard to process how many goals I’ve scored this year.



“Even my 31 goals for Spurs, 28 goals were great seasons. But then to almost double that it’s pretty surreal to see.

“Sometimes, I’d watch Bayern Munich play or Real Madrid play or these other big teams play and be like if, ‘I was there, I’d score 40 goals or 50 goals’.

“When the decision came to leave, that was a big part of it. It wasn’t just to win trophies. It was just to get the most out of my career. I knew I had levels that I could reach.

“I knew if I had the right environment and the players around me like I do now that I would score goals that Messi and Ronaldo in that era used to score.

“So the fact that I took that risk, it’s paid off for sure, makes me extremely proud.”



Kane has won back-to-back Bundesliga titles – ending the trophy drought he experienced at Spurs – but the big one he wants in club football is the Champions League.

Bayern lost to eventual winners Paris Saint-Germain 6-5 on aggregate in a thrilling semi-final last term.

The German giants kick off their new campaign at home to Norwegian side Bodo/Glimt on Thursday and Kane says the hunger in Vincent Kompany’s squad to win the competition is huge.

He added: “We’re really close. I think last year was the finest of margins – to go out to a team who has won the Champions League back to back. There’s no shame in that.

“We’re coming into this season now saying that it needs to be our year. We need to find a way to get it done.”

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi took off new £85m Tottenham signing Savio against Nottingham Forest due to new policy
Sports.content:
ROBERTO DE ZERBI’S decision to take off Savio and Destiny Udogie at the weekend was part of Tottenham’s new approach to injury prevention.

The pair were replaced in the 61st minute during Saturday’s 0-0 draw at Nottingham Forest because of medical advice ahead of the game.

Spurs have been hit by a crock crisis for both of the last two campaigns which have played a significant role in their back-to-back 17th-placed finishes.



The North Londoners launched an extensive review over the summer into why last term – which saw the club escape relegation on the final day – was so best with fitness problems.



It was led by performance director Dan Lewindon, who joined from the City Football Group in February.

SunSport understands one of the consequences of that review has been a far more cautious approach to using players who are not at 100 per cent, on the guidance of Lewindon and Ali James, the club’s new head of medical services.

That led to £85million new-boy Savio being left out against Newcastle last Saturday on doctors’ orders because of “muscle fatigue”.



De Zerbi then heeded the information given by the medical staff for Forest, taking off both the Brazilian winger and left-back Udogie – who has a history of hamstring issues – after the hour.

The Spurs boss has bought into the new policy.

Though he would prefer to have his best players out on the pitch for longer, he agrees that a strategy designed to keep players fit for the long term is better than risking injury just for the sake of another 15-20 minutes in a game.

While managing players’ fitness should be far easier this term given the deeper squad Spurs have following a mega-money transfer spend that surpassed £300million this summer.



De Zerbi confirmed in the post-match press conference: “Before the game, the plan was Savio and Udogie around 60 minutes, because it’s dangerous, no?

“Savio has not the best physical condition to play 90 minutes. He’s an important player for us, a crucial player. Destiny is another crucial player for us.

“I’m not happy when we have the plan, but it’s for my advantage, for my business, the management of the players after injuries.”

Tottenham currently have Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert out with serious knee injuries, while Dejan Kulusevski and James Maddison are still working their way back from long-term crocks.

Both last season and the campaign before, there were matches when Spurs’ injury list was into double figures.

Sports.title: David Raya insists title-winning season ‘doesn’t matter now’ with Arsenal determined to win Champions League this year
Sports.content:
DAVID RAYA says Arsenal are hungry to take the next step and become kings of Europe.

The Gunners suffered heartbreak in the Champions League final last season as Paris Saint-Germain beat them on penalties.

Mikel Arteta’s side are bidding to go one better this term and start their road to glory away to Napoli on Wednesday night.



The Premier League champions have made a perfect start to defending their crown with three wins on the spin and are full of confidence as attention turns to Europe.



Raya said: “We’ve been improving every single year in the Champions League, especially after so many years without playing it.

“Since we came back to the competition, we’ve been enjoying it – which is the most important thing.

“We just have to be ourselves, and enjoy the moment. Enjoy every single game, and we will see where we are at the end. So just try to be better than last year – that’s all.



“Of course, winning the league after that many years and after those years that you are so close, it gives you that relief and it gives you that extra confidence.

“The last season is gone. That’s gone. That doesn’t matter now. We have to be focused on this season.

“Just focus on ourselves, focus on the present, enjoy and play that type of competition, especially against a big rival like Napoli.”

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Arsenal are sweating on the fitness of Cristhian Mosquera ahead of their trip to Italy.



The defender was left out of the squad for Sunday’s 2-1 win over Chelsea at the Emirates.

Mosquera, 22, has been feeling some discomfort in his hamstring after he came off in a 1-0 victory at Aston Villa last week.

Sports.title: Harry Kane tipped to join 'exclusive little club' and end 25-year wait with Ballon d'Or win
Sports.content:
Harry Kane tipped to join 'exclusive little club' and end 25-year wait with Ballon d'Or win

Harry Kane is set to be bang in contention for the Ballon d'Or, with Michael Owen already tipping him to win the award ahead of the likes of Kylian Mbappe

View 2 Images Harry Kane smiles as he warms up ahead of the 2026 World Cup football tournament third-place match between France and England at the Miami Stadium in Miami on July 18, 2026. (Photo by ROBERTO SCHMIDT / AFP via Getty Images) (Image: Getty)

Harry Kane has been told he deserves to join an “exclusive little club” - and be crowned winner of the Ballon D’Or.

‌



England captain Kane, 33, will discover his rivals for the prestigious crown on Tuesday when the 30 name shortlist is unveiled for one of the biggest honours in football.

‌



Kane is the red-hot bookies’ favourite after his record-breaking season when he scored 73 goals for club and would be England’s first winner in a quarter of a century.

‌



Michael Owen was the last winner in 2001 and believes Kane - who will be up against the likes of Rodri, Kylian Mbappe and Lionel Messi - deserves to win the award which will be handed out in London on October 26.

The Former Liverpool striker insists that Kane has had a “phenomenal season” and is the “best finisher on the planet. Owen said: “Let's hope that all that means that you're going to get a huge shout of winning the Ballon D’Or. I would welcome you with open arms to join our exclusive little club.”

‌



The Ballon D’Or often goes to a player from the winning nation in World Cup year but there is not an outstanding candidate and there is a strong feeling it could - and should - be Kane’s year, especially after a hugely successful season with Bayern Munich.

Kane, in an interview with TNT Sports, said: “I'm here now, and I'm winning awards like the Golden Shoe. And the Ballon d’Or is the same. Of course, now it's out of my hands in terms of it's down to the voters and the people who decide it.

View 2 Images Kylian Mbappe also has his sights set on the prestigious award (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



“The season I had was my best season by far, and we have to wait and see this. It's a weird one because I'm already focussed on this season now and the next season and thinking how can I be better, how can I improve. But also I want to appreciate what I did. Time will tell.”

Real Madrid star Mbappe is also banging the drum for his own cause as he is dreaming of winning it for the first time even though he did not win any trophies.

Mbappe said: “I think when you play for Real Madrid, the best club in the world, people associate you with this award. There are many people that speak about me and the Ballon d'Or. Of course I've made history in the most important competition. Maybe it's a good year for this but people can vote according to what they think.”

Sports.title: Michael Carrick should not be 'disappointed' with Man Utd setback - he should be angry
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick should not be 'disappointed' with Man Utd setback - he should be angry

The Man Utd boss has come under fire for saying his team's start to the season has 'not been that bad' and needs to get on the front foot in the Champions League and Manchester derby

View 3 Images Michael Carrick saw victory snatched away at Everton

It was once accepted wisdom that if, as an elite football manager, you do not get too euphoric when things are going well or too despondent when things are going slightly awry, then it is a good trait to have. Not any more.

‌



That is why Michael Carrick was probably ill-advised to say Manchester United’s start to the Premier League season has ‘not been that bad.’ Even though it has, er, not been that bad.

‌



Carrick’s character is not going to change but, like it or not, perception is important in the modern managerial game. Supporters do not like a shrug of the shoulders.

‌



Carrick said he was ‘disappointed’ with the way the game ended at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Sunday. That does not cut it these days.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Arne Slot found that out last season. One of the Dutchman’s issues was that he became eminently reasonable in his dissection of unfavourable results.

‌



More often than not, Carrick quite reasonably said, Ainsley Maitland-Niles’ strike does not go in. In fact, that is a totally reasonable thing to say.

In 334 appearances in professional football, Maitland-Niles has now scored 12 goals. He has never scored a goal like that in his professional life - and will never score one like it again.

View 3 Images Benjamin Sesko thought he was the matchwinner at Hill Dickinson Stadium (Image: Getty Images)

‌



But what Carrick should have been saying is that he was angry United did not go for Everton’s jugular after Bryan Mbeumo’s goal early in the second half. He should have been saying that he was angry United did not create a chance in the 40 minutes that followed Mbeumo’s goal.

And you can bet he was angry. Yes, United were denied a win by two freakishly good hits, but they were also complacent. And while they might have finished a decent third in the Premier League last season, they have nothing to be complacent about.

Of course, it is way too early to read too much into the start of a season. Liverpool were the only team to record three wins from their opening three matches last season.

‌



In fact, Slot’s team won five out five to kick off their defence. We all know what happened after that. When he looks ahead to Thursday’s Champions League game against Sabah, Carrick should get on the front foot.

View 3 Images Matheus Cunha does not look like a natural number nine (Image: Getty Images)

No, he cannot change his character but he can be a bit more expressive. When he has watched the Everton game back, he will know it was a badly missed opportunity, regardless of the fact that only an unusually brilliant goal denied them all three points.

‌



And he will say that. He will demand a response in the Champions League and then against Manchester City at Old Trafford next Sunday.

The game against Sabah is a good opportunity for Carrick. The feeling from the Everton match and the statistics suggest that Benjamin Sesko should be given a starting chance as the central striker.

Matheus Cunha is, quite clearly, not a natural number nine. Sesko, quite clearly, is a natural number nine. He certainly brings an extra dimension when it comes to aggression. And that is what this United team needs. More aggression … from the top down.

Sports.title: Joey Barton to spend Christmas in prison after trial adjourned until next year
Sports.content:
Joey Barton to spend Christmas in prison after trial adjourned until next year

Joey Barton was charged with causing grievous bodily harm with intent, to which he pleaded not guilty, after an alleged serious assault near a golf club in March

View 4 Images Joey Barton (Image: PA)

Joey Barton is due to spend Christmas in prison at HMP Liverpool after a bail application on his behalf was refused. The former Premier League footballer was due to face trial at Liverpool Crown Court last week, but the case was adjourned until March 8 next year.

‌



Barton, 44, was charged with causing grievous bodily harm with intent in connection with an alleged serious assault in March. The alleged victim, Kevin Lynch, was taken to hospital in a serious but stable condition.

‌



He was said to have sustained injuries to his face and ribs. Barton has been refused bail since his arrest.

‌



View 4 Images Joey Barton was initially denied bail in March (Image: PA)

Defence counsel Tim Forte KC applied for bail on his behalf during an hour-long hearing this afternoon (Monday 7 October), but the bid was refused. Barton appeared via video link to HMP Liverpool, wearing a grey Columbia fleece and glasses.

He appeared in the dock of courtroom 42 on Wednesday (2 September), which was his 44th birthday, when the case was adjourned. That is when Judge David Potter further remanded him into custody while proceedings continue.

‌



Judge Potter said: "Mr Barton, your case will next be mentioned on December the 11th. In the meantime, you are remanded in custody through to the next date."

View 4 Images Police at Huyton and Prescot Golf Club following the alleged assault (Image: Liverpool Echo)

That date in December is when the pre-trial review is scheduled. The expectation is that Barton's trial will last for up to a fortnight.

‌



He therefore faces a year in custody after already spending six months inside, with another six-month wait following the case's adjournment to March 8. Barton was wearing glasses, a navy blue suit and tie with a blue shirt and sporting short, greying hair.

Judge Potter told him in the dock: "Mr Barton, I have now fixed your trial to take place on Monday, the 8th of March. In the meantime, you are remanded in custody."

View 4 Images Mr Lynch is the headteacher of an independent school set up for students with additional educational needs

Article continues below

The court previously heard Lynch, 51, had been socialising with Barton at Huyton and Prescot Golf Club on March 8 before the alleged assault. Lynch is a former non-league football manager and was said to have been found covered in blood on Fairway, close to the club's entrance.

He managed City of Liverpool, Marine and Prescot Cables, and, away from football, founded NexGen Academy in Dovecot. He is the headteacher of the school for children with additional needs.

Barton is from Huyton but is now of Fox Bank Close in Widnes. He most recently hosted a podcast.

Sports.title: Man Utd signing 'isn't the answer' as Michael Carrick treatment sums up problem
Sports.content:
Man Utd signing 'isn't the answer' as Michael Carrick treatment sums up problem

Manchester United frontman Benjamin Sesko has continued to be used as an impact player with Michael Carrick opting against using him from the start, which was also the case last season

View 2 Images Michael Carrick saw Man Utd concede late to drop points on Sunday

Tim Sherwood has claimed that Benjamin Sesko "isn't the answer" for Manchester United as he continues to be overlooked by Michael Carrick.

The Slovenian frontman came off the bench to score, what he thought was a winner at Everton on Sunday, but his 88th minute strike was only good enough for a point.

Sesko has come off the bench in each of United's opening three games despite being the only genuine No 9 at the club, bar Joshua Zirkzee, who almost left in the summer. At Everton, Matheus Cunha led the line from the start, even though the Brazilian is not naturally and out and out striker, yet continues to get the nod ahead of Sesko.

Even last season, when the former RB Leipzig man continued to score winning goals from the bench, he was only afforded a starting role on occasion. Sherwood maintains that if Sesko was truly world class, he would be starting games but his current role suggests there are doubts.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

He said on Sky Sports: "Where do you find that striker? Everyone is looking for it, Arsenal are looking for it. Sesko isn’t the answer because no one wants to play him. He comes on, he’s done alright, he’s come on and scored a few goals off the bench.

"But if he was top drawer, do you think Michael Carrick would be playing him? Of course he would. He wouldn’t be wanting to play someone else out of position."

Sesko has been recovering from a shin injury, which he was nursing during the summer, and that may well have impacted his standing within the squad across the opening weeks.

View 2 Images Benjamin Sesko came off the bench to score in the 88th minute on Sunday, before Everton's stoppage time equaliser

Carrick though has been vocal about the fact Sesko, still only 23, is ultimately maturing as a player and needs to further adapt to what is being asked of him.

The United boss said: "He’s made big strides last season and he’s still young, he’s still kind of adapting to a point and learning and developing here.

"So there’s loads more to come from Ben. So just being patient with him really and looking after him as well. And letting him grow into the season. Really happy with how he’s come back, so looking forward to seeing him on the pitch a little bit more."

Sports.title: Jadon Sancho 'in talks with two Premier League clubs' days after Man Utd flop’s return option
Sports.content:
Jadon Sancho 'in talks with two Premier League clubs' days after Man Utd flop’s return option

The attacker left Manchester United in the summer becoming a free agent following loan spells at Chelsea and Aston Villa

View 2 Images Jadon Sancho is still without a club (Image: James Marsh/Shutterstock)

Jadon Sancho's future remains unresolved, with talks said to be taking place with 'at least two' Premier League clubs. The 26‑year‑old left Manchester United in the summer upon the expiration of his contract, becoming a free agent.

‌



During his five‑year spell at Old Trafford, Sancho struggled to impress, leading to loan spells at Borussia Dortmund, Chelsea and Aston Villa - though none of those clubs chose to sign him permanently. Chelsea, who had an obligation to buy the winger at the time, even paid a £5million penalty to send him back to United.

‌



Following a season at Villa Park, Sancho returned to Manchester in the summer but the club chose not to offer him a contract extension.

‌



Speculation has intensified in recent weeks, with Sancho linked to several clubs, though no move has yet materialised. A return to Dortmund has not been ruled out either, according to German outlet Bild.

The Bundesliga side recently lost Giannis Konstantelias to a cruciate ligament injury and are seeking a replacement. As a result, Sancho is said to have become a topic of discussion once again, with the report claiming he would 'be willing to forgo a signing bonus and accept a heavily performance‑based contract.'

As a free agent, Dortmund would not need to pay a transfer fee, with Bild suggesting 'a return could be on the cards.' Sancho made 158 appearances for Dortmund over two spells.

‌



Sancho is also reported to have interest from the Premier League. Two unnamed English clubs are thought to have made fresh approaches in 'recent days,' according to TEAMtalk.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

View 2 Images Jadon Sancho previously spent time on loan at Aston Villa (Image: 2026 James Gill - Danehouse)

‌



Meanwhile, clubs in Turkey, the Saudi Pro League and the UAE are also exploring a deal for the winger. Sancho has also been offered the chance to join Arabian Falcons, the Dubai‑based side managed by former Liverpool midfielder Jonjo Shelvey, who is enjoying a winning start to the new campaign.

United signed Sancho for £73m in 2021 after he had established himself as one of Europe's most sought‑after young players. Clubs were queuing up for his signature, and it looked as though United had won a major race.

Five years on, however, United have not seen a return on that investment. Sancho scored just 12 goals and registered six assists in 83 appearances during a spell that never truly ignited.

Sports.title: Emi Martinez keeps avoiding problematic Chelsea star he thought club were wrong to sell
Sports.content:
Emi Martinez keeps avoiding problematic Chelsea star he thought club were wrong to sell

Emi Martinez moved to Chelsea this summer but narrowly missed out on linking up with a player he has previously praised

View 3 Images Martinez joined Chelsea this summer (Image: 2026 Chelsea FC)

Chelsea goalkeeper Emi Martinez may be a huge fan of Alejandro Garnacho, but the duo keep narrowly missing each other at club level. The pair have played together for Argentina and Martinez has previously praised his young international team-mate.

‌



The shot stopper, who joined Chelsea this summer, was unable to prevent the Blues from slipping to a 2-1 defeat to Arsenal on Sunday as he returned to the north London club, where he spent 10 years. His compatriot, Garnacho, who joined Aston Villa this summer on loan, came on with 15 minutes to go for his new side in a 0-0 draw with Hull City on Saturday.

‌



While Martinez is a big fan of Garnacho, who has had his issues at his previous clubs, their Premier League tale is one of passing ships in the night. Martinez, then at Villa, almost moved to United in the summer of 2025, only for a late change of heart to crush the move and for United to sign Belgian star Senne Lammens instead.

‌



That same summer, United sold Garnacho to Chelsea for £40million. After a tough year in west London, Garnacho joined Martinez at Villa this summer, promising a link-up for the duo.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Morgan Rogers speaks out on Arsenal defeat as Chelsea star teased by Arsenal fans READ MORE :

However, Martinez then headed the other way, moving to Stamford Bridge in a £7.5m deal last month. While they've never played together domestically, Martinez is a big fan of the young winger and will not have been happy that United sold their young prodigy.

‌



When Garnacho earned his first Argentina cap in June 2023, the goalkeeper lauded his new team-mate. He told TyC Sports: "He is a very humble guy. He came to work; he didn't talk a lot. He is very eager to play. The truth is that he's a little treasure and I hope we can mould him so that he gives us as much as Angel Di Maria."

View 3 Images Alejandro Garnacho and Emiliano Martinez have never lined up together in the same Premier League team (Image: Getty)

‌



Despite bursting onto the scene at Old Trafford, Garnacho ultimately fell out of favour at United and looked to have reignited his career with a move to Chelsea.

He lasted just a year at Stamford Bridge, however, scoring once in 24 Premier League appearances. He now has his sights set on raising his levels at Villa Park.

"This is an important club which is going up really quickly, so I can't wait to get started here," Garnacho said after his switch to Villa was announced. "I was looking for a club to get my confidence back, so I can try to become the player I was a few years ago in my first years at Manchester United."

‌



View 3 Images Garnacho is set to spend the season on loan with Aston Villa (Image: Getty Images)

However, Villa boss Emery believes Garnacho still needs time to adapt to his new club. The Argentine forward has made just three substitute appearances for Villa so far this season, while he has also fallen behind academy graduate George Hemmings in the pecking order.

Emery said: "We have other players who joined who need to adapt to us in training, playing matches, and Garnacho is in this way. We need their performance to try to add things, working and getting numbers. Garnacho is in this way. How he is responding."

Sports.title: Steve McManaman explains Trent Alexander-Arnold issues as Jose Mourinho mulls over change
Sports.content:
Steve McManaman explains Trent Alexander-Arnold issues as Jose Mourinho mulls over change

Former Liverpool star Trent Alexander-Arnold endured a very tricky start to life with Real Madrid and Steve McManaman believes he could be in line for better things this season

View 2 Images Trent Alexander-Arnold has already made three appearances this term (Image: Getty Images)

Steve McManaman believes Trent Alexander-Arnold’s injury issues have hampered him at Real Madrid - and he is now ready to shine. The England defender joined the Spanish giants on a free transfer last summer after letting his contract at Anfield run down.

‌



He made 30 appearances across his debut season, with just 22 of those being starts. Alexander-Arnold suffered two separate injuries last term - a hamstring injury seeing him miss five league games, while a muscle tear kept him sidelined for a further seven.

‌



Former Liverpool and Real Madrid star McManaman has now offered his take on the defender’s issues and believes the club will now start to see the best of him now he’s fit.

‌



Speaking to Sport, he said: “He’s fine. I speak to him, and he’s fine. He’s settled in well. The problem is that he had a lot of injuries last year. That was the problem.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“He had physical issues, and the team weren’t at their best either. I think he should be fine this year.

‌



“Although, again, it’s going to be tough against Barcelona. Barcelona have signed some good players. He played the other day and did very well. I don’t need to give Trent any advice.

“He knows what he has to do. He knows he has to learn the language, settle in and enjoy his life in Madrid. And he’s doing just that. He’s got good friends there. I don’t think he’ll have any problems.”

Alexander-Arnold might have found an excellent opportunity to break into the team over the coming days, with Real Madrid currently in the grips of a midfield crisis. Bernardo Silva is suspended alongside Arda Guler and Eduardo Camavinga for the Champions League clash with Inter Milan.

‌



View 2 Images Trent Alexander-Arnold endured a tricky first season at Real Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

Aurelien Tchouameni and Thiago Pitarch are also both ruled out through injury, which could see Jose Mourinho use Alexander-Arnold as an emergency midfielder. Discussing the defender, the Portuguese coach claimed that he is better playing alongside big money summer signing Yan Diomande as opposed to fellow arrival Denzel Dumfries.

"The team has always been good," Mourinho is quoted as saying by AS. "I haven't seen the stats, but we created a lot. We missed three or four clear chances and their goalkeeper made three or four impressive saves.

Article continues below

"I didn't make changes because I wasn't happy; they were to take off the players who had been booked. It's better to play with Trent and Yan Diomande than with Denzel Dumfries."

Sports.title: Paul Ince recalls horrifying Glenn Hoddle incident as fans urged to back heart campaign
Sports.content:
Paul Ince recalls horrifying Glenn Hoddle incident as fans urged to back heart campaign

The ex-Manchester United midfielder is part of a five-a-side team of former hard men to launch the latest phase of the long-running Sky Bet/British Heart Foundation project

View 3 Images Paul Ince is encouraging people to learn how to use a defibrillator

If you will forgive the pun, the campaign to equip football fans with lifesaving CPR and defibrillation skills is one that is close to Paul Ince’s heart. Just under eight years ago, Ince was working with Glenn Hoddle in a TV studio when his friend and old England boss suffered a heart attack.

‌



Ince held Hoddle in his arms after an employee at BT Sport - a quick-thinking sound engineer - had used continuous CPR and a defibrillator to revive him. Ince recalls: “It was Glenn’s birthday and it turned into probably the worst experience I’ve had in my life. I had his head in my hands trying to keep him awake, talking about the World Cup in '98 and our time together at Wolves.

‌



Michael Carrick fumes at Man Utd stars following late Everton nightmare READ MORE :

“But the fact that every time I speak to him now, he seems to be on the golf course, shows you just how unbelievably important this campaign is. He would not be here if we were not lucky enough to have someone there who knew how to use a defibrillator and perform CPR.”

‌



Ince has joined forces with Neil Ruddock, Julian Dicks, Iain Dowie and Roy Keane to form a “toughest-ever” five-a-side team that will urge supporters not to be scared of learning and administering life-saving CPR skills. The Every Minute Matters campaign - funded by Sky Bet and run in conjunction with the British Heart Foundation (BHF) - has been running for three years and Ince and his fellow hard men are launching the next phase after research showed that over two-thirds of football fans believe fear could stop them using a defibrillator.

Ince says: “When a heart stops, you don’t need to be the toughest person in the room to be a hero, you just need to feel empowered to act. A defibrillator is there to help you, not test you.

"It guides you every step of the way and there’s nothing to be afraid of. It’s impossible to hurt someone.

‌



View 3 Images Paul Ince was with Glenn Hoddle when the former England manager suffered a heart attack on his 61st birthday

“It takes just 15 minutes to learn how to use a defibrillator with the BHF’s free RevivR tool. Giving yourself that confidence could help you to help save a life.”

Ruddock also had a deeply personal reason to get involved in the Every Minute Matters campaign, explaining: “I was best friends with Justin Edinburgh. For his age (49), he was the fittest man you would ever see.

‌



"He collapsed in a gym that did not have a defibrillator and we lost him. It was so tragic.

"That is why this means a lot to me. And that’s why I’m calling on fans to face their fears and learn how to use a defibrillator.

View 3 Images Neil Ruddock is urging football fans to learn life-saving CPR skills

Article continues below

"The Sky Bet Every Minute Matters campaign has already had a monumental impact to bring together fans to learn CPR – and you just need to spend 15 minutes using the BHF’s free RevivR tool. Doing the training means that if a cardiac arrest happens at home, at work or beside a football pitch, you are ready to step up and help save a life.”

* First launched in May 2024, Sky Bet and the BHF’s Every Minute Matters campaign has already made a transformative impact, inspiring more than half a million fans to learn CPR. In September, the campaign is kicking off its next phase - a month-long push to tackle fear and get football fans ready to step up and use a defibrillator.

As part of helping as many fans to access lifesaving defibrillators as possible, the ‘Every Minute Matters’ campaign is asking fans to check their eligibility and apply for a free defibrillator for their local area through the BHF’s Community Defibrillator Funding Programme.

Sports.title: Red Bull's Hadjar to miss Spanish GP as injury absence continue
Sports.content:
Isack Hadjar will miss this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid as he continues to recover from a fractured wrist.

Liam Lawson will replace Hadjar for a third successive race as Max Verstappen's team-mate at Red Bull, while Yuki Tsunoda continues at Racing Bulls.

Hadjar suffered a hairline fracture in a bone in his wrist during the summer break in a routine workout that involved boxing which forced him to miss the Dutch, Italian and now Spanish Grands Prix.

"The decision has been taken as Isack's recovery continues to progress positively. While he is not yet ready to return to the cockpit, he will be in Madrid supporting the team.

"Everyone at Red Bull Racing looks forward to welcoming Isack back behind the wheel very soon."

Sports.title: Pakistan investigating 'discipline and conduct' in latest twist on crisis tour
Sports.content:
The Pakistan Cricket Board has launched an investigation into "media reports concerning discipline and conduct" amid the team's crisis tour of England.

Pakistan last week took the unprecedented step of sending seven players home and calling up seven after losing heavily at Headingley and Lord's to fall 2-0 down in the three-match series.

Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and assistant Umar Gul have also been replaced, with Mike Hesson, in charge of Pakistan's white-ball sides, and former Australia seamer Ashley Noffke overseeing the third Test at Edgbaston, which begins on Wednesday.

A statement read: "The Pakistan Cricket Board has initiated an internal disciplinary inquiry following media reports concerning discipline and conduct, which are currently being reviewed internally.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the best of day four at Lord's as England thumped Pakistan by 194 runs to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match Test series

"The PCB handles such matters in accordance with its standard procedures. The process is being conducted under PCB regulations, ensuring that all concerned individuals are given due consideration.

"At this stage, any speculative reports or unverified claims circulating on certain platforms, particularly those originating from hostile external sources, should not be regarded as credible."

The banished senior players included Salman Ali Agha - who captained Pakistan in the first Test before being dropped for the second - wicketkeeper Mohammad Rizwan and Imam-ul-Haq, who did not bat in either innings after suffering a low-grade calf strain in the field.

Former captain Shahid Afridi described the PCB's decision to make sweeping alterations to the travelling party as the "most shocking decision ever by a selection committee".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pakistan's Saud Shakeel missed out on a Lord's century, holing out off Josh Tongue to fall for 97 against England in the second Test

Of the seven replacements who have been called up, only batters Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal have Test experience.

The PCB's statement on Monday added: "The PCB will not comment further at this time. The board advises stakeholders and the public to rely on official PCB communications."

New Pakistan coaches in the dark over investigation

Noffke addressed the media in Birmingham on Monday, admitting he was unaware of the specifics of the probe.

"I can be really honest in that I don't know too much," he said. "I sit outside of that decision-making model, (which is) above us as coaches. We try and keep the players focused on what they need to worry about.

"One thing that I've learned about being in Pakistan and coaching for a period of time, nearly 15 months now with the white-ball team, is there's always something going on in the background.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at some funny moments from the England vs Pakistan Test series!

"I think most of the time it's out of the players' control. They need to focus on the cricket that they have in front of them and the opportunity they have in front of them.

"We're not really in the position to even know the outer workings of what's happening at PCB in that context."

Noffke also admitted that taking over mid-series as part of head coach Hesson's staff was "unusual".

He added: "It doesn't happen very often and I guess from Mike and my perspective is all we can do is come in and add positivity.

"We want to listen to the players as much as we can, so there's obviously a feeling of uncertainty but also they've just got back on the job."

Sports.title: Leicester have sunk to new low under Martin but can he turn it around?
Sports.content:
A decade ago in September 2016, Leicester City were getting ready to play in the Champions League.

Now? They sit 17th in League One, the lowest position in the club's history since they entered the Football League in 1894.

Russell Martin has led the Foxes to just one win in their first five games, and on Saturday they were battered 4-0 at home by Oxford United.

Leicester fans were chanting 'you're getting sacked in the morning' at Martin at the King Power Stadium, who would have been desperate for a good start to turn his reputation around after a dismal end to his time at Southampton, and then a gruelling spell at Rangers.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Sky Bet League One match between Leicester City and Oxford United.

But can he turn it around? Former Leicester City assistant manager Michael Appleton believes he can.

"It's a difficult moment, there's no doubt about it," Appleton told The EFL Show on Sky Sports News.

"Russell Martin is a very experienced guy now. It was always going to be a difficult job, with big expectations from a club that not too long ago was playing in the Premier League and winning the Premier League.

Martin's miserable record Russell Martin has managed just three league wins since the start of the 2024/25 season, with Southampton, Rangers and Leicester, in 28 attempts.

"With those expectations, you've got to deliver. It's still very early, but losing 4-0 at home, along with the results against Plymouth and Burton, makes it a very difficult start. They've got to start winning games very quickly to address it.

"What I would say is that he's got experience. He's been here before, at a big club with expectations in the league they were in, and he didn't get off to the start he wanted.

"He'll draw on those experiences and maybe use them behind the scenes with the players and staff, speaking about how they dealt with those situations and trying to keep everyone calm.

"It's still very early and there are some good games coming up for them. I always say that when you're in a difficult moment and you're losing games, it feels much worse when you're at home. I'm not saying losing 4-0 at Oxford would have been a good result in any stretch of the imagination, but when it happens at home, it feels so much worse.

"There's a big expectation to deal with, but I think he's more than comfortable doing it."

Meanwhile, Reading co-CEO Joe Jacobson believes the inexperience in the squad is hurting their progress this season.

"They've got a really young team at the minute," he said. "You look at the players they're bringing off the bench and they're taking off experienced players and bringing on younger ones.

"It's difficult for those young players, who will feel the pressure and feel the atmosphere in the stadium. The fans are waiting to turn because of what's happened over the last couple of years. It takes a long time for a fan base to turn and get right behind their team again.

"They have a really tough job on their hands and Russell Martin will know that. He knows exactly what he wants to do and how he wants his team to play. Sometimes that causes division within the fan base, but I'm sure he'll be knuckling down on exactly what he wants to do with his team.

"It reminds me of when he was at Southampton. They lost four games in a row in September and then didn't lose a league match until February. If he can turn the ship, he might start to get a tune out of some of those players."

Jacobson also feels that the disconnect between the club and the fans is also causing an issue, especially since the owners announced Leicester was up for sale, having had a similar recent experience at Reading.

"It's been difficult at Reading because of what happened previously with the ownership there. We've felt it as well. It has taken a long time to get the fans to buy into what you want to do, and the ownership have done amazing things there over the years," he added.

"But when they recently came out and talked about wanting to sell the club and actively looking for a buyer, straight away the fans almost say, 'Well, you don't care now. You just want out. That's your main focus.'

"If the ownership are openly saying they want to sell, it's really difficult for the fans to buy into that. But I still think they're going to have a really successful season.

"Once these players get time on the training field with the manager, I'm sure they'll come good. At the minute, there's that anxiousness and a divided fan base. They want to support their club, but they also want to feel that everyone is pulling in the right direction."

Next up for Martin and Leicester is a trip to Stockport County on Saturday, who are currently sat third in League One.

A decade ago, the Hatters were in National League North. Now they welcome the Foxes to Edgeley Park as favourites for victory.

Sports.title: The flap of a wing: How St Helens let success become stagnation
Sports.content:
The dust has settled on the fact that St Helens have missed out on play-off rugby for the first time after their seventh-placed finish in Super League.

The analytical dissection of how this happened has been ongoing by fans and pundits for the best part of two years. Some supporters would say longer.

The next 12 months will give an indication of how long those with power inside the four walls of the club have realised that their trajectory has been downwards.

The famous question posed by meteorologist Edward Lorenz back in the 1970s was 'can the flap of a butterfly's wing in Brazil set off a tornado in Texas?'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Leigh Leopards secured their Super League play-off place with a 48-10 victory over St Helens, who missed the play-offs for the first time in the club's history

Can the smallest of changes lead to significant outcomes in the most complex of systems?

If this low ebb for Saints is their tornado, what exactly was the flap of the wing? What exactly caused the chaos?

For that, we need to rewind to 2019, when they picked up their first Super League title in five years.

2019: The start of a run like never before

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2019 Super League Grand Final where St Helens beat Salford 23-6 at Old Trafford

Midway through 2017, St Helens were sitting mid-table and made the decision to part ways with head coach Keiron Cunningham and bring in Justin Holbrook.

After a Luke Gale drop goal saw Saints heartbreakingly fall in the semi-finals in 2017 and somehow miss out in 2018 despite the genius of Ben Barba, 2019 marked the year when they were simply the best team around.

The Saints obliterated the competition in 2019, losing just three matches and cantering to the top of the league.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Thompson was the first prop since 1992 to win the man-of-the-match award in the Super League Grand Final

Their 23-6 win over Salford Red Devils in the Grand Final was the moment that cemented that St Helens were here once again.

It was a star-studded team with the likes of Jonny Lomax, Tommy Makinson, Alex Walmsley and Lachlan Coote all in their mid-to-late 20s and in their prime. A mix of homegrown talent and hand-picked Australian superstars was running the show.

They had to then overcome a change of head coach but, under Kristian Woolf, success would continue...

2020-2023: Four in a row leads to climbing Everest

Woolf has spoken openly about the fact that the season shutting down due to Covid potentially saved his job.

Woolf's team had just lost to Huddersfield Giants and Castleford Tigers when the season went on hiatus.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player In the final moments of the game, Tommy Makinson hit the post when attempting a drop goal, only for Jack Welsby to follow up to grab a try

By the time it returned, he had spoken with his playing group about what more they wanted from him and how they wanted things to run. A collaboration between a stern coach and a group striving for success - and continuing to achieve it - was born.

Jack Welsby scored one of the best Grand Final tries ever seen in 2020 and then two more Super League wins followed. Not only that, they won a Challenge Cup and a League Leaders' Shield.

Then they do the unthinkable...

World Club Challenge: Everest complete

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player St Helens beat Penrith Panthers to win the World Club Challenge in dramatic fashion with an extra-time golden point winning drop goal!

When St Helens headed down under for the World Club Challenge in 2023, no one believed they could beat Penrith Panthers.

Hometown head coach Paul Wellens moved from captain and player to assistant coach, and after over 10 years in the coaching game at the club, he had stepped up to the top job.

Then, Lewis Dodd sent over a golden-point drop goal that is lauded as one of the most seismic moments in the sport in this country.

They had climbed to the top of Everest and planted the St Helens flag.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player St Helens captain James Roby analyses the incredible try that helped them beat Penrith Panthers to win the World Club Challenge

You have won it all, your players have provided every success you have asked for.

So what is the next task? Is it starting a transition period? Is it trusting this same group of players to provide once again? Is it a mix of both?

St Helens went for option B...

Salary cap bites

Big players were winning big and getting their reward, deservedly so. But in a salary-capped sport, there comes a time where that may start to bite.

By this point, the likes of Makinson, Lomax, Walmsley, Mark Percival, Louis McCarthy-Scarsbrook and Sione Mata'utia had brought unprecedented success. They were also now mostly in their 30s.

Naturally, with that, comes upgraded contracts. Simply put - you win more you deserve to earn more.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jon Wilkin and Sam Tomkins were shocked by the way St Helens lost to Hull FC and looked at the massive decline of the club

But, if contracts are being upgraded year on year, the space on a salary cap dwindles. Your chance to bring in big names dwindles. Your room for youngsters to be earning well dwindles.

A sum of £2.1m only stretches so far and you need to be ruthlessly pragmatic. Or players need to be willing to earn less than what they were receiving in their 20s. A tough sell!

Over the next three seasons under Wellens, St Helens would make just 11 signings to replace the likes of Regan Grace, James Roby, Will Hopoate, Makinson, Lewis Dodd and Mata'utia.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player St Helens lift their fourth Grand Final trophy in a row after a 24-12 victory over Leeds Rhinos

Those signings were Tee Ritson, Wesley Bruines, Daryl Clark, Waqa Blake, Kyle Feldt, Tristan Sailor, Lewis Murphy, Moses Mbye, Matt Whitley, Shane Wright and Deon Cross.

Wright and Cross only became available due to the financial collapse of Salford Red Devils.

Some would argue those big boots have still not been filled. Or if they have been filled, the successor has not matched up to their predecessor.

Moneyball gone wrong?

Back in 2025, former St Helens CEO Mike Rush described the club's recruitment strategy as 'Moneyball'.

Moneyball is a term coined from Michael Lewis' book which analysed how, in 2002, Oakland Athletics and their general manager Billy Beane used a statistical approach that saw them sign players whose skills might be being undervalued on traditional methods of scouting.

You sign players to fulfil particular roles, for example making lots of tackles or making metres, knowing they lack in other areas, so that you can still compete despite being hampered by a budget.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On The Bench podcast with Jenna Brooks and Jon Wilkin, St Helens CEO Mike Rush responds to recruitment criticisms around the club

"We're always going to get stuff wrong because whether it's an overseas player or not, you take risks and you gamble," Rush told Sky Sports.

"Context is, and without divulging personal business, it's a salary-cap sport. You're putting certain numbers on players' heads that you believe they're worth.

"Without people knowing the salary-cap value, it's very difficult. It's where that person sits on our cap [that determines] if we get value.

"It's much more detailed than just picking a certain player and saying, 'is he playing well?'

"Waqa Blake played in an NRL Grand Final. That doesn't make him a great player, but for what we had available in our cap or for what we valued the player at, it was worth a chance to do."

So, you gamble and sign what you think is value for money. But did that mean St Helens built a cost-effective squad of players who did not deliver what was asked of them?

One thing that is for sure is that they did not replace like for like.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jon Wilkin and Jamie Jones-Buchanan assess the problems facing St Helens after their 48-10 defeat at Leigh saw them miss the Super League play-offs for the first time in the club's history, with recruitment and squad balance coming under scrutiny

"I've said it a number of times but Saints' recruitment has been shocking," Sky Sports' Jon Wilkin said.

"It's been terrible. They've made convenient and short-term recruitment choices. They've not replaced like for like and they need to rethink their recruitment strategy.

"There's a lot of young guys who have gone out into Super League who aren't ready. I'm loving that, it is great for them and for their future.

"But the reason they're out there was because you had an old squad at the start of the year that wasn't durable enough to get through a year, and then you signed shoddy replacements for guys who moved on."

Not only that, St Helens are not the spending force they once were. It is not just the 'Super League giants' with cash to burn. Obviously, Wigan have got richer, but Wakefield now have money, as do York, Leigh and more.

More clubs are offering better and Saints are being outcompeted in the wage stakes.

Wellens to Rowley to Walters...

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jon Wilkin says St Helens were irresponsible to give Paul Wellens the top job at the club so early on in his coaching career

If quality drops, senior players age and suffer injuries, and more is asked of youngsters, then naturally, outcomes of seasons will change.

Lomax and Percival have managed just 14 games between them in 2026. They do not offer what they once did.

Wellens, Roby and Rush also all left the club in a quick span of time. That is three people who have had eyes on St Helens' successes and failures, consistently since the 1990s.

They lost stalwart and skipper Matty Lees to injury early in the season and have not had him as the enforcer on the pitch. They also lost their other enforcer in Morgan Knowles to the NRL.

St Helens fans did not enjoy the attritional approach to rugby under Wellens that brought them third, sixth and fifth-placed finishes that saw them make the play-off semi-finals twice in those three seasons.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sam Tomkins sends the Catalans Dragons to the Super League Grand Final with this last minute try!

The club decided that those results, with the roster available, were not good enough and change was needed. With that, they brought in Paul Rowley to turn the club's fortunes around on a three-year deal.

Rowley lasted less than a season at Saints before being sacked ahead of the fixture against rivals Wigan Warriors in Round 20 back in July.

It is unknown how the season in full would have shaped under Rowley given the raft of injuries that St Helens faced and the clear signs that his systems were not embedding into a club that has a very specific DNA.

What we do know is they finished seventh.

Now they have turned to Australia head coach Kevin Walters to get things back on track.

St Helens legend James Graham said on his podcast, The Bye Round, that he had sent Walters a YouTube video of all of Saints' greatest wins to show him just why they have the tagline 'Never write off the Saints'.

Walters is renowned for maintaining strong environments and being an advocate for his players. He is already teasing big signings he is making.

The noises from St Helens are that they are now reverting to splashing the cash to ensure the quality on the field matches the expectations off it.

Chaos theory...

The question posed was what was St Helens' 'flap of a wing'. What were the small, incremental changes made that ended in this tornado.

Frankly, it seems that what caused their tornado in 2026 is that they spent four years not flapping their wings at all.

They say in sport, if you are not evolving you are falling behind. Those at St Helens can say they could not see this outcome occurring.

But this is not a random outcome. It was predetermined when option B was chosen - the option of standing still and attempting to not cause disruption by flapping your wings.
