Sports.title: 'It's been wall-to-wall aggravation': F1 supremo Bernie Ecclestone, 95, speaks out after being stopped for illegally carrying shotgun on his jet 'to go clay-pigeon shooting'
Sports.content:
'It's been wall-to-wall aggravation': F1 supremo Bernie Ecclestone, 95, speaks out after being stopped for illegally carrying shotgun on his jet 'to go clay-pigeon shooting'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Bernie Ecclestone says Portuguese police subjected him to 'wall-to-wall aggravation' after he was stopped at an airport for illegally carrying a shotgun - which he claims was for clay-pigeon shooting.

Formula One supremo Ecclestone, 95, was reportedly arrested at Tires Aerodrome in the municipality of Cascais close to Lisbon after landing there in his private jet from Switzerland.

And speaking to Daily Mail Sport, Ecclestone admitted he had travelled with the gun without the correct documentation and was held up for 'hours'. His wife Fabiana Flosi, 49, is now trying to rectify the situation.

Ecclestone told the Daily Mail: 'I had a gun that I was bringing over from Switzerland to Portugal for clay-pigeon shooting. It's as simple as that. I have guns at home there that are licensed.

'We cleared customs on arriving here – I know the guys there – and they were fine with everything. No problems. Then a policeman afterwards asked to search the bag. It could have been [his six-year-old son] Ace's fishing tackle for all it looked like, but it wasn't.

'They asked if I had a "blue book", which is apparently the documentation you need, and I told them I never travel with documents like that, any documents at all practically. They said they would arrest me, but after what seemed like hours, we sorted it out, but it has been wall-to-wall aggravation.

Bernie Ecclestone, pictured with his wife Fabiana Flosi, was reportedly arrested in Portugal for illegally carrying a shotgun

'But it seems it can be put right. Fabi has gone to Lisbon to surrender the gun, or pay the tax or whatever you need to bring it in, or to hand it over in the end. I said I would go too but I didn't as it happened, and I am sitting at home waiting for it to be the situation to be put to bed.'

Flight radars today show a private jet having flown to Cascais, landing at 10.55pm, from Saanen in Switzerland, where Ecclestone has a £23million ski chalet. Private jet experts value Ecclestone's Dassault Falcon 7X plane at around £30million.

He was previously arrested in May 2022 in Brazil for illegally carrying a gun while boarding a private plane.

He acknowledged owning the gun but said at the time he was unaware it was in his luggage.

Ecclestone was freed and allowed to travel to Switzerland after paying bail. He described it afterwards as a 'silly, tiny little incident', saying it had caused a lot of aggravation as he and family tried to leave Sao Paulo by private plane.

He also denied he was formally arrested despite Sao Paulo state's public security office confirming in a statement a businessman it didn't name was arrested for possession of a firearm at Campinas' airport.

Ecclestone's arrest occurred after he landed at an airport to the west of Lisbon, in Cascais

Ecclestone said afterwards he had bought the handgun, a LW Seecamp .32, from a Formula One mechanic or tyre man in Brazil years ago without ammunition and purely as a deterrent.

He added: 'They said you need something like this. It might work if someone tried to mug you or something. So I bought it from the guy.

'I had it in the house and used to muck around with it if people came to visit me or something, we would joke around.'

In April it was reported Bernie Ecclestone's wife had bought a mansion in the prestigious resort area of Quinta da Marinha in Cascais for £35million.

Respected Portuguese daily Correio da Manha described the deal at the time as the 'largest private sale ever of a home' in the country.

It said Brazilian Fabiana, 46 years younger than Ecclestone, agreed the purchase of the property around 15 miles west of Lisbon in January after negotiations lasting half a year.

A spokesman for the PSP police force, which according to Portuguese media reports made the arrest, said: 'Our border control officers haven't made the arrest that's being attributed to them.'

The force said in response to a formal request for a statement or additional information about Mr Ecclestone's reported arrest: 'Regarding the questions raised, we inform you that this concerns an occurrence involving the Tax and Customs Authority – Lisbon Delegation (Customs), and you should therefore request clarification from that entity.'

Customs' officials couldn't be immediately reached for comment.

Sports.title: Inside Kevin Pietersen's shock England SOS: The figure who pushed for his appointment revealed, the ways he's expected to shake up the dressing room - and his added motivation to get close to key players
Sports.content:
Inside Kevin Pietersen's shock England SOS: The figure who pushed for his appointment revealed, the ways he's expected to shake up the dressing room - and his added motivation to get close to key players

Brendon McCullum instigated the extraordinary move to bring arch critic Kevin Pietersen into England’s coaching set-up.

It has been normal practice over the past decade for individuals with specialist local knowledge to be recruited by the ECB on consultancy terms ahead of major tours or global tournaments overseas, but the engagement of Pietersen carries extra shock value, coming as it does so soon after he lambasted McCullum’s white-ball regime.

However, Daily Mail Sport understands it was McCullum who proposed the role to Pietersen earlier this summer, around the time the New Zealander was relieved of his Test coaching responsibilities.

In the official press release, McCullum, 44, said he had ‘immense respect’ for former England captain Pietersen, who will join up for twin white-ball series against Sri Lanka starting next week and will remain around the environment until next year’s World Cup in southern Africa.

But he also clearly holds no grudges, after Pietersen’s scathing assessment of England’s preparation, or lack of it, on a limited-overs tour of India 18 months ago.

In his role as a broadcaster during that tour, he accused England of a slack approach to pre-match practice.

Kevin Pietersen has been appointed as a mentor to England's white-ball sides despite being a vocal critic of Brendon McCullum's set-up in the past

In fact it was McCullum (right) who instigated the appointment of his former critic

McCullum hit back, saying it was ‘factually incorrect’ of Pietersen and fellow commentator Ravi Shastri to say England had not done enough training during a tour which ended in two crushing series defeats.

It was true, however, that in trying to strike a balance between the intensity of a tour of India and a desire not to allow it to become all consuming, England had not netted ahead of the second and third one-day internationals.

One source close to McCullum said on Monday that contrary to a public image of being stubborn, he covets strong opinions within the dressing room culture he creates and views Pietersen as someone who will naturally increase energy levels.

Pietersen has never been shy of speaking his mind, of course. Or rubbing people up the wrong way in the process.

And even though he has softened since being sacked by England 12 years ago, briefly returning to do some coaching on the white-ball tour of South Africa three years ago, he was critical of Harry Brook in swerving an Indian Premier League deal in 2025 that would have seen the pair work together at Delhi Capitals.

In an interview with ESPN last year, he said: ‘I told him. I was like, "Dude, I'm gutted that I can't work with you for a few months". I think that he is a star… You don't hit one ball over extra cover and the next, same ball, over midwicket if you can't play.

‘So he can properly play, but he has technical flaws in the subcontinent – in India, in particular. I really wanted to work with him, but people make their own choices in life and you've got to respect them. He has a flaw playing spin in India – a real big flaw. Two months here, imagine what might have happened if he had fixed that?

‘I would've worked the same with him as I did with (Joe) Root and (Jonny) Bairstow at the start of their careers. Root turned out to be the greatest player of spin England's ever had. I'm not saying it's because of what we did when he was a youngster, but we spent hours together batting in the nets, going through drills and practising. I love that stuff.’

Pietersen (pictured celebrating victory in the 2013 Ashes) is one of England's finest ever batsmen

An explosive hitter in his playing days, he will be working with England's white-ball sides for 15 months

Intriguingly, Daily Mail Sport can reveal Pietersen has been pursuing England’s biggest stars this summer, as yet to no avail – keen for them to appear on episodes of his YouTube channel The Switch, which features challenges and interviews with leading players from around the world.

Now, he will don an England tracksuit and hook up with a side in Southampton next week who briefly reached No1 in the world T20 rankings this year, mentoring a group including many who idolised his flamboyant style as youngsters. By contrast, England lie down in seventh in the ODI rankings.

As part of a consultancy set to run 15 months, Pietersen, 46, will also be involved on the tours to Australia and South Africa this winter and then return next summer for series against Pakistan and New Zealand, which will finalise preparations for the 50-over World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia next autumn.

‘Putting on the England uniform again for the first time since 2014 is a profound honour and a deeply special moment,’ said Pietersen, whose 277-cap international career included being named man of the tournament during the 2010 Twenty20 World Cup win in the Caribbean.

‘We have an incredibly talented white-ball squad, and I am excited to get in the trenches and work relentlessly hard with these players to maximise their potential.

‘To be a part of Brendon’s think tank over the next 12 months is a fantastic opportunity, and I cannot wait to get started.’

Although McCullum planted the seed on this one, South African-raised Pietersen’s recruitment is the latest ‘specialist’ signed up during Rob Key’s tenure as director of England men’s cricket: Mike Hussey was part of the support staff during the Twenty20 World Cup triumph in Australia in 2022 while Kieron Pollard took up a similar position in the 2024 event in the Caribbean, which resulted in a semi-final exit.

As far back as 11 years ago, England turned to Sri Lankan Mahela Jayawardene to help them understand the challenges of playing on the pitches of Asia.

Pietersen worked with Joe Root on his batting against spin in the subcontinent early in his career

Of Pietersen, McCullum added: ‘I’m particularly excited for our batters to get the opportunity to work with him. KP has a unique understanding of what it takes to perform at the highest level, which will be hugely valuable to our players.’

His appointment comes hot on the heels of another high-profile former England player, Andrew Flintoff, leaving his role as England Lions coach.

Flintoff has been replaced for this week’s Lions fixtures against the touring Sri Lankans by another multi-Ashes winner Jonathan Trott.

Ravi Bopara and Graeme Swann are also in the coaching set-up while the 20-strong playing squad includes half a dozen full internationals, including Tom Banton and Jamie Overton.

Sports.title: Joey Barton to stay in jail for the rest of the year as he is denied bail over golf club 'assault' that could leave victim blind in one eye
Sports.content:
Former footballer Joey Barton will remain in custody until his trial next year after a bail application was refused.

The 44-year-old had been due to stand trial at Liverpool Crown Court last week accused of causing grievous bodily harm with intent to Kevin Lynch, 51, at £1,440-a-year Huyton and Prescot Golf Club in Merseyside on March 8.

But on Wednesday the case was adjourned and delayed until March next year.

Barton, wearing a grey zip-up fleece, appeared over videolink from HMP Liverpool at a hearing on Monday, when Judge David Potter refused a renewed bail application.

He nodded as the judge remanded him in custody ahead of a pre-trial hearing on December 11.

Joey Barton will remain in custody until his trial next year after a bail application was refused

Kevin Lynch, 51, was injured in the alleged assault at Huyton and Prescot Golf Club

Former footballer Barton appeared over videolink from HMP Liverpool (pictured)

His trial will take place exactly a year after the alleged assault, meaning the defendant, who was arrested shortly after the incident, will have spent 12 months on remand.

Barton is accused of carrying out the attack on Mr Lynch after they had been drinking together at the golf club.

Mr Lynch, a former non-league football manager and founder of special education school NexGen Academy, was said to have suffered serious injuries to his eye.

Last week at Liverpool Crown Court an application by Barton's counsel Tim Forte KC to have the case adjourned so potential new witnesses could be contacted was not opposed by prosecution counsel Alex Leach KC.

Judge Potter said that there were still 'intractable problems' which meant that the trial could not start on September 1 and set a new date for March 8, 2027.

Former Manchester City and QPR midfielder Barton, of Widnes, Cheshire, has one England cap and also played for Newcastle, Rangers, Burnley and Marseille.

He went on to manage Fleetwood Town and Bristol Rovers.

Sports.title: Red Star Belgrade fans unveil tifo of war criminal Ratko Mladic before Serbian derby
Sports.content:
Red Star Belgrade fans unveil tifo of war criminal Ratko Mladic before Serbian derby

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Red Star Belgrade fans unveiled a tifo of Ratko Mladic before their derby win with rivals Partizan, the day before the war criminal’s funeral in the city.

Mladic was given a life sentence for genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity in 2017. He died in prison last month aged 84.

Known as the ‘Butcher of Bosnia’, Mladic was the Bosnian Serb commander who orchestrated the massacre of more than 8,000 Muslim men and boys in Srebrenica in 1995, as well as the years-long siege of the Bosnian capital, Sarajevo, and setting up concentration camps for detained non-Serb civilians and enemy soldiers.

The club’s social media accounts published a video of the tifo and the two teams observing a minute's silence for Mladic.

Red Star were fined £77,000 this month after their fans unveiled a banner commemorating Mladic in a Europa League clash against Viktoria Plzen.

They were also banned from selling tickets to fans for their next away game in a UEFA competition. That will apply when the Serbian champion visits Swiss club Lugano in the third-tier Conference League.

Red Star Belgrade fans unveiled a tifo of Ratko Mladic, the day before the war criminal’s funeral in the city

Serbia defied EU warnings against allowing public homage to the man found guilty of genocide, with thousands of mourners arriving to attend his funeral

Mladic’s body lay in state on Monday as Serbia defied European Union warnings against allowing public homage to the man found guilty of the continent's first case of genocide since the Second World War.

Thousands of mourners arrived early at the small Serbian Orthodox Church of St. Luke in Belgrade to honour Mladic, who is still viewed as a hero by many Serbs. His military officer's cap and saber rested on the coffin, which was flanked by men in fatigues.

The head of the Serbian Orthodox Church, Patriarch Porfirije, led the funeral service while pro-government media in Serbia reported that Mladic will receive full military honours at the burial site.

Mladic had spent over a decade in hiding before he was arrested in 2011.

He was convicted at the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia in 2017, receiving a life sentence.

Mladic died at the age of 84 last month after suffering several strokes in prison.

Sports.title: Aston Villa's tricky start to the season unpacked: The Brian Madjo mystery, a transfer window scramble, the peculiar decision on Taylor Harwood-Bellis... and the one shining light
Sports.content:
If there is one thing Unai Emery really cannot stand, it is when he calls for a substitute only to find the player is still putting on his shirt or adjusting his boots.

Alejandro Garnacho has already found himself on the end of an Emery blast for touchline dawdling against Arsenal last week. At Hull, Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Tammy Abraham felt the full force of their manager’s fury.

Yet right now, that image of the unprepared sub sums up Villa in September 2026. They feel like that player who is just not quite ready when the manager beckons him over.

No team in the world could lose six players from their first-choice starting XI and bounce along as though nothing had happened. When the side in question is also severely restricted by punishing UEFA financial regulations, the rebuilding job becomes even tougher.

How clubs respond to those setbacks, however, tends to shape their future. These are early days for the new Aston Villa but for the second season in a row, they are without a win or a goal after three Premier League matches.

The team need to pull their socks up quickly, ideally in their Champions League opener at Club Bruges on Tuesday. Daily Mail Sport looks at what might come next for Villa as they begin their European campaign...

These are early days for the new Aston Villa but for the second season in a row, Unai Emery's team are without a win or a goal after three Premier League matches

Alejandro Garnacho has already found himself on the end of an Emery blast for not being ready to come on as a substitute against Arsenal last week

MISSING MADJO

Villa’s only goalscorer this season is Brian Madjo, who was chosen ahead of Tammy Abraham for the UEFA Super Cup and produced a barnstorming display against Paris Saint-Germain in Salzburg last month.

The 17-year-old is currently out with an ankle injury and Villa say they hope he will have recovered once the upcoming international break is over. If that is the case, it seems strange that Abraham has been preferred to Madjo in the Champions League squad. If he is back in October, Madjo would – in theory – be available for seven more European games.

Abraham joined Villa from Besiktas in January and it feels as though they have been trying to sell him ever since. They were desperate to send Abraham to Ipswich on loan just before deadline day and after the 1-0 defeat by Arsenal, Emery was pretty frank in his assessment of Abraham: ‘We opened the door for him but he’s decided to stay here with us.'

By Friday, he was more conciliatory – an understandable tactic given Abraham will be with Villa for four more months at least. ‘His challenge here is very important,’ said Emery.

Yet if Madjo’s injury really is minor, and Villa really were under no pressure from UEFA’s financial rules when they put together the squad, the choice looks curious.

Madjo has made only six senior appearances in his career, whereas Abraham has more than 400. Emery believes experience counts for plenty in European competition and Abraham has that, too, with 65 appearances.

But this did not stop Emery throwing in European novice Morgan Rogers for the 2024-25 Champions League campaign, nor will he hesitate to use academy product George Hemmings in this season’s. So why not Madjo?

Aston Villa's Brian Madjo scored against PSG in the Super Cup - but why is he not in their Champions League squad?

SIGNINGS WITH STRINGS ATTACHED

Villa’s record signing, Johan Manzambi, has an issue with his knee and Emery has admitted he must take great care with the Swiss playmaker.

Leon Goretzka, 31, arrived on a free transfer on August 27 but has yet to feature in a matchday squad. Garnacho has played only 31 competitive minutes.

We may see more of Matteo Ruggeri and Ibrahim Mbaye after the international break, as is the case with Manzambi and Joao Gomes when he completes his suspension. Of Villa’s new signings, only goalkeeper Zion Suzuki, midfielder Gomes – sent off on his debut – and Nicolas Jackson have gone straight into the starting line-up.

Some players have called the 2026-27 squad the ‘new Aston Villa’ and the more bullish online followers talk about ‘Villa 2.0’. Really, though, what we are watching right now is an inferior version of the ‘old’ Villa.

It takes time to integrate new players and those who have departed are not easily replaced. Still, it feels like Villa have been scrambling a little too much.

It was common knowledge across the club that Rogers would leave. Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne had exit clauses. Ezri Konsa was one of three key targets for Arsenal since last May – which Villa must surely have known.

Which brings us to Taylor Harwood-Bellis...

Villa’s record signing, Johan Manzambi, has an issue with his knee and Emery has admitted he must take great care with the Swiss playmaker

Joao Gomes is serving a suspension after being sent off against Brighton on the first weekend of the season

SNUBBING KONSA'S REPLACEMENT

If a club rate a player highly enough to pay £30million for him as a replacement for Konsa, one of the best centre backs around, it surely follows that they would have him available for all their fixtures.

Not Villa, who have omitted Harwood-Bellis from their European squad. Emery says he has opted for versatility by including Lamare Bogarde, who can also play at centre back but is primarily a midfielder. He also namechecked Boubacar Kamara as a possible centre-back option.

If you’re Harwood-Bellis, though, you may feel as though you’re not only fourth-choice centre back, but that the manager would rather play midfielders there in Europe if he has to.

Villa have form for this. They signed Donyell Malen in January 2025, only to axe him from the European squad when they made the high-profile loan signings of Marcus Rashford and Marco Asensio. Malen, it is safe to say, was not a happy chap.

Again, Villa say the exclusion of Harwood-Bellis is unrelated to their UEFA settlement agreement, which means there must not be a ‘negative balance’ in their Champions League squad. In layman’s terms, that means the transfer and wage outlay on their signings cannot exceed the fees they have received in sales, and the wages they have saved.

Equally, Emery demands a great deal from his players when Villa do not have the ball. It takes time to master his instructions and perhaps Emery believes it too risky to ask a player to learn on the job, especially in the Champions League.

The last time Emery made a major signing from the Championship, he went for Rogers – now one of the most expensive players in history after his £117m move to Chelsea.

Even so, the Harwood-Bellis call still seems an odd one, if it really is for football reasons alone.

Taylor Harwood-Bellis will have to make do with a seat in the stands during the Champions League as the £30m signing has been left out of the squad

HERO HEMMINGS

Amid the uncertainty of Villa’s start, they have unearthed a jewel from their youth system in Hemmings.

Madjo drew all the attention against PSG but Hemmings looked the more accomplished footballer and he looks ready-made for a coach like Emery.

There are still kinks to iron out – as there will generally be for a player with only eight senior appearances. But look at the many upsides.

Hemmings is technically strong, physically robust and tactically smart. This season, he more than held his own against Achraf Hakimi and Ben White.

Amid the uncertainty of Villa’s start to the season, they have unearthed a jewel from their youth system - George Hemmings

In the home defeat by Arsenal last Monday, Hemmings started on the left of a narrow attacking three.

He had to provide Villa with an attacking outlet, help Ian Maatsen deal with Bukayo Saka, and stay aware of White when he stepped into midfield from right back. He did all three difficult jobs in the ‘serious, mature, responsible’ fashion Emery demands from all those he coaches.

It sounds daft to say this of a 19-year-old novice, but Villa’s new boys can learn a great deal from Hemmings. A player can be as skilful as he likes but if he doesn’t do what Emery wants out of possession, he won’t play many games.

Mbaye is a double Champions League winner, Goretzka has 17 major trophies and Garnacho is closing in on 200 senior appearances at the age of 22 – but Hemmings is showing the way. All Villa fans hope the new men can be up to speed as quickly as him.

Sports.title: Inside Man City's summer of streamlining: Enzo Maresca's new strategy for squad depth, where Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez fit in and how Hugo Viana quickly fixed the mistakes of 2025
Sports.content:
Elliot Anderson had only been back in the country for 48 hours, still processing England's defeat by Argentina, when his day arrived. Going up to Manchester to officially sign the deal of a lifetime before enjoying deserved time off on two separate holidays with his brothers and girlfriend.

The interest had been heavily signposted, with Manchester City making relevant enquiries just before Christmas, and the 23-year-old was earmarked as the man to add much-needed punch into a midfield that felt light and yearned for the Rodri of old.

He had been anticipated to arrive, smiling with Hugo Viana and meeting Enzo Maresca, as the most expensive British footballer of all time - though that £116million fee paid to Nottingham Forest was eclipsed by Chelsea and Morgan Rogers within days of the agreement being reached during the World Cup.

And he didn’t even end the transfer window as City’s record signing either, Enzo Fernandez sourced from Chelsea for £125m in the nick of time on deadline day. So late – City threatened to pull out amid the posturing – that he was having a medical at almost 10pm and posing for photographs in complete darkness.

But irrespective of the finances and what ultimately transpired in City’s hectic window, the conversation around the dinner table at the Ivy Asia on July 22 between Anderson, his family and representatives would have circled to how he was one of the faces of this rebuild. A pillar of Maresca’s midfield, huge trust in somebody whose stock is rising rapidly yet will only taste the Champions League for the first time in Porto on Tuesday.

Midfield was clearly the area identified as the one requiring most surgery. Anderson’s early displays, powerful and authoritative, suggest he is picking up from where he left off in taking more responsibility in an England shirt. Next to him stands the divisive character of Fernandez, a proven winner, a signing Maresca pushed for personally, and who offers a nastiness that City have probably missed in the past two years.

Elliot Anderson will be a pillar of Enzo Maresca’s midfield - huge trust in somebody whose stock is rising rapidly yet will only taste the Champions League for the first time on Tuesday

Next to him stands the divisive Enzo Fernandez, a proven winner, a signing Maresca pushed for personally, and who offers a nastiness that City have probably missed in the past two years

Ironic, really, that City’s new-look engine room is on show in Europe for the first time at the Estadio do Dragao – the scene of the 2021 final defeat by Chelsea, when Pep Guardiola went without a conventional holding midfielder. The decision is still debated in the bars of Manchester to this day.

When taking deep breaths at 11pm last Tuesday, City were satisfied with their work, totalling a net spend of £145m following heavy sales, and there is an insistence that the squad is now in a significantly more advantageous position than a year ago.

That is largely because the two windows of 2025 have aged poorly, with Tijjani Reijnders, Omar Marmoush and Nico Gonzalez all having been let go less than 18 months after landing.

City rectified those mistakes by earning their money back on all three, with Tottenham owning an obligation to purchase Marmoush for £60m once his loan finishes. And not forgetting the astonishing £85m for two-goal Savinho, bought a year earlier.

Another 2025 signing, Rayan Ait-Nouri, cannot buy a game at left back and Manchester United even asked whether the Algerian was available for transfer. In truth, allowing Ait-Nouri to leave as well would have left City too short and that throws up an intriguing subplot to their summer.

It feels deeper, this squad. It feels more complete. But there are fewer players. Twenty-two senior outfielders last year plays 20 this. In the Treble season, there were 18.

With ten first-teamers departing since May, six coming in, this has been a streamlining. Is the thinking clearer now than it was a year ago, when Txiki Begiristain was handing over and Guardiola’s time began drawing to a close? The proof will be in the progression over the next three years and these past few months will likely define Viana’s tenure at the Etihad.

The idea on the squad’s make-up appears to have shifted slightly, with more emphasis placed upon individual players battling a team-mate in specific positions – much like how Thomas Tuchel ran the England team in the build-up to the World Cup – rather than demanding they are capable of performing in three or four different areas.

How that works or evolves will only become clear over time, as with much of this new era, and City’s idea that Antoine Semenyo is the alternative No9 to Erling Haaland suggests they will still be leaning on some versatility.

Rayan Ait-Nouri cannot buy a game at left back and Manchester United even asked whether the Algerian was available for transfer

City’s idea that Antoine Semenyo is the alternative No9 to Erling Haaland suggests they will still be leaning on some versatility

What follows over the next ten days – Porto, United at Old Trafford on Sunday and then the Carabao Cup against Norwich City – should provide clues as to what sort of City manager Maresca sees himself as.

Settled side or heavy rotation? There will have to be some caution – Porto have won all six of their games this season, conceding only once, and Guardiola found out how troubling the Champions League league phase can be.

With the derby on the horizon, Maresca must decide whether to go same again or mix things up in Portugal. Given it certainly looks as if the quality gap between individuals fighting for the same position has narrowed with the recent business, there could be more confidence in tweaking with the sort of regularity that Guardiola was famed for.

Maresca has talked up the need for Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye to be offered minutes, while Phil Foden didn’t start against Coventry City.

Before they flew out to Porto on Monday afternoon, Maresca had the music blaring during the early part of City's training session, as is customary under him. The Italian likes his house music and the fitness coaches are in control of the tracks for the warm-ups. Maresca is quietly convinced he will get a tune out of City’s reimagined squad.

Sports.title: Revealed: Why the Premier League and EFL will NOT mark 25th anniversary of 9/11 terror attacks this weekend
Sports.content:
Revealed: Why the Premier League and EFL will NOT mark 25th anniversary of 9/11 terror attacks this weekend

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The Premier League and EFL will not be asking clubs to mark the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terror attacks at this weekend’s matches.

A total of 67 Britons were killed 25 years ago on Friday following a series of atrocities in the United States.

However, Daily Mail Sport understands there are no plans to organise competition-wide tributes to those who perished at forthcoming matches.

Last year, it was announced that the Premier League and the rest of English football would no longer hold automatic minute’s silences for global disasters, after a working group concluded that such gestures were losing impact.

Instead, they decided that only international incidents with a direct link to football would trigger league-wide tributes.

Following the Manchester synagogue attack last year, only both Manchester clubs staged a minute’s silence.

Premier League and EFL clubs will not mark the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terror attacks

Two Premier League matches held on the 10th anniversary in 2011 saw a moment's silence held with players also wearing black armbands

The World Events Working Group (WEWG) was launched in 2024 in a bid to inform decision making for the Premier League, EFL and FA.

Criticism had been levelled at the FA after it failed to light up the Wembley arch following the October 7 terror attacks in Israel in 2023, having previously done so in solidarity with Ukraine following Russia’s invasion of the country.

As The Times reported at the time, the WEWG’s remit does not extend to player-led initiatives, such as taking the knee, which Daily Mail Sport revealed last month would be taking place at two Premier League match rounds this season.

While there are no top-flight games on Friday, in the Championship West Ham United host Wrexham at the London Stadium.

On the tenth anniversary of 9/11, in 2011, a moment’s silence was held before both Premier League matches held on the Sunday, with players wearing black armbands. The vast majority of Britons killed were in the World Trade Centre in New York, while one was onboard one of two hi-jacked airplanes that struck the iconic Twin Towers.

In the US, a series of commemorations will take place across sporting events. For the NFL’s opening week, end zones will feature the words ‘Never Forget’ while officials will use 9/11 branded coins for the coin toss, which will later be auctioned with funds raised going to the league’s September 11 charitable partners.

The Week One match in Australia will feature a pre-game ceremony in which Australian and US military members will parade.

At the New York Giants’ clash with the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday night, players, coaches and staff from both sides will wear commemorative NYPD, FDNY and PAPD hats on the sideline in recognition of first responders.

Meanwhile, at the baseball clash between New York’s Yankees and Mets on Friday there will be a series of pre-game ceremonies.

Sports.title: George Russell's title hopes in tatters as Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli wins Italian Grand Prix to extend his championship lead - despite starting 19th
Sports.content:
George Russell's title hopes in tatters as Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli wins Italian Grand Prix to extend his championship lead - despite starting 19th

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Kimi Antonelli galloped from 19th on the grid to win the Italian Grand Prix, all but ending the title hopes of George Russell, who started second and finished second.

‘Exceptionally challenging,’ admitted the Englishman of achieving his career ambition, almost resigned to be a smiling bridesmaid in someone else’s story.

As for Antonelli? What a drive. In triumphing on a strategy that clearly – and controversially – favoured him rather than his Mercedes team-mate Russell, the 20-year-old became the first Italian to win his home race since the black-and-white days of Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966.

The pivotal moment came on lap 28, when Lance Stroll’s Aston Martin broke down. A virtual safety car was deployed. Antonelli was called in, offered a cheap stop to move from hard tyres to mediums.

He came out flying, but 14 seconds behind race leader Russell, who had stayed out and was thus handed the uphill task of making his harder rubber last sufficiently well to the end with an ever-diminishing advantage.

At times, the to-be-winner Antonelli lapped nearly a second quicker than Russell and it grew into a matter of not if but when he would close the deficit to his senior before the 53rd and concluding lap.

Kimi Antonelli roared to victory in his home Grand Prix, becoming the first Italian to win it since 1966

It set up a grandstand finish. With 10 laps remaining, Antonelli was 4.7sec back. It looked bleak for Russell. It was going to come down to the last nervous moments. Or not quite as long as that, in fact.

Antonelli arrived on Russell’s gearbox on lap 49. They skirmished at the first corner. All fair. Russell went deep. Antonelli ran into the gravel, losing two seconds. Russell kept the lead, for now. But a lap later Antonelli did what the inevitable at Variante Ascari: he went into first place, and that was that.

His Mercedes was fast and Monza is an overtaking track, but this was also a scintillating drive, albeit helped by this strategy that was most useful to him.

An early red flag brought about by Charles Leclerc’s huge shunt on lap two got him on to hard tyres under the red-flag opportunity and bunched the field (a huge help after his engine change had condemned to start so far down the field).

Russell, arguably, should have been far enough up the road never to have been under threat. He had, after all, started 17 places ahead of Antonelli, who transported himself from further back on the grid to win than anyone since John Watson at Long Beach, California in 1983. Watson started 22nd that day.

The Mercedes garage hailed the win as you would expect – with unbridled emotion, and their motorhome was buzzing afterwards. Antonelli is their favoured son. Russell, who finished 3.8sec back from him, is not. He is also 66 points adrift from leader Antonelli in the standings and has precisely no momentum with 10 races remaining.

It is almost impossible to see a way back for Russell. He has won twice this season; Antonelli seven times.

George Russell, starting second and finishing second, could only congratulate his team-mate

But why did Mercedes not bring Russell, then leading, in for new tyres rather Antonelli? Their team boss Toto Wolff said: ‘We didn’t know what was the better strategy.

‘At that stage, the system said that the one-stop (Russell’s strategy) comes out ahead. That is what the software said.’

On whether Russell’s championship dream folded in the Royal Park at Monza, Wolff added: ‘It’s too early to say. It’s motor racing. It’s a technical sport. Things can break. Accidents can happen, and that’s why we have to do our best job for both drivers.’

If that sounds as if Wolff believes in and is backing Russell, I’m Mother Theresa. The Austrian said Antonelli is improving like an AI agent and that he had ‘walked on water’ here.

Russell was strangely sanguine afterwards, saying: ‘Kimi is definitely in charge of the championship, and he deserves to be. I am not even thinking about a fight or a comeback but focused on taking it race by race and maximising every weekend.

Early on the race was suspended following Charles Leclerc's 160mph smash into the barriers

‘It is going to be exceptionally challenging to overcome that gap, so I am sort of accepting what it is. I am going to try to enjoy it from here and win as many races as possible.’

Max Verstappen, for the record, finished third. Lando Norris was fourth and Oscar Piastri fifth. Lewis Hamilton was sixth for Ferrari.

It was a yo-yoing race, a good show in some ways but one that revealed not only the strengths but the frailties of the new regulations introduced this year that allow one car to pass with a boost button and then be repassed as their electric charge falls off.

Early, Leclerc was left sitting in pain after his dramatic 160mph crash.

The Ferrari favourite lost control of his car at the final bend, the Parabolica, as he duelled with Piastri for fourth place.

Leclerc’s impact with the wall was severe with only a short portion of gravel to slow his trajectory into the hoardings, which he thudded side-on.

Leclerc was left devastated on the grass after crashing out of the race

The Monegasque soon jumped out of the car but then sat disconsolately on the grass as he was comforted by a marshal before being taken away in the medical car. He was feeling his neck as he went for treatment. Ferrari said he had been released from the medical feeling ‘OK’.

The race was red-flagged for 30 minutes and some fans in the grandstands cried at the huge blow for their team.

By this point, Leclerc had already squeezed Hamilton on the second part of the opening chicane and was driving somewhat erratically. Hamilton was furious, saying: ‘Charles pushed me off.’ The seven-time world champion, who started fourth, fell down to 10th place.

Russell was leading the race for Mercedes at this point when the race was suspended after passing pole man Pierre Gasly, who was to finish seventh for Alpine, on the main straight at the end of the first lap.

Leclerc’s stricken car was taken away by crane and the ding-donging began again. And nobody was hit harder than Russell.

Sports.title: Edu's venture after Arsenal exit 'not what he envisaged' as Nottingham Forest errors prove costly
Sports.content:
Edu's time at Nottingham Forest is officially over, with the Brazilian leaving his role as Global Head of Football.

Almost two years on from leaving his role at Arsenal with his stock at an all-time high, Edu's gamble to move elsewhere for a broader remit has not quite paid off. The former Gunner had worked impressively in tandem with Mikel Arteta as the duo combined to make the north Londoners a force in the Premier League once more. But, shortly after a second successive season where Arsenal finished as runners-up to Manchester City, Edu left the Emirates.

He headed to the City Ground to work under Evangelos Marinakis, with a desire to work in a multi-club model seen as a huge pull, with Edu also overseeing Olympiacos and Rio Ave.

However his work in Nottingham failed to produce the necessary results and he's been removed from his role. The news has been a long time coming - The 48-year-old had been sidelined for months and hasn't attended a match since February or set foot in the City Ground or training facility since early March.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The Telegraph reports that the work assigned to Edu was not what he envisaged when he took on the job. Edu himself accepts that he struggled to foster relationships with key members of Marinakis' staff, which ultimately made his job more challenging.

The decline in his relationship with Nuno Espirito Santo was also well documented, leading to the Portuguese leaving the City Ground. Last year's disaster campaign saw Forest go through four managers - Nuno, Ange Postecoglou, Sean Dyche and Vitor Pereira as the club narrowly avoided the drop. Oliver Glasner is now at the helm.

The transfer decisions taken by Edu failed to push the club on, after they had finished seventh and qualified for Europe in 2025. The former Arsenal chief was responsible for several transfer calls that failed to pay dividends - he led the pursuit of Igor Jesus from Brazilian club Botafogo.

‌



View 3 Images Edu's difficult relationship with Nuno Espirito Santo was well documented (Image: Visionhaus, Visionhaus/Getty Images)

The £37.5million signing of Omari Hutchinson, plus loan deals for Douglas Luiz and Oleksandr Zinchenko, were all influenced by Edu, but only three of those four players remain at the club.

Adding James McAtee from Manchester City was seen as a real coup, but the young midfielder has struggled to push on, in part owing to the constant managerial upheaval that has impacted on a host of players. Being on the outer meant that the club's summer transfer business was conducted with other key figures.

When Edu quit Arsenal he claimed: "This was an incredibly hard decision to make. Now it is time to pursue a different challenge."

‌



View 3 Images Omari Hutchinson was one of several Nottingham Forest signings who have not delivered (Image: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

Whilst at the Emirates Edu, who was part of the Invincibles that won the title in 2004, helped assemble a huge bulk of the team that would go on to win the Premier League last season. He was responsible for signing Martin Odegaard, Ben White, Gabriel and the club-record capture Declan Rice.

But since leaving the Arsenal wheel has continued to turn and they've been able to add more star quality, which now leaves them with the best squad in the league by some distance. Andrea Berta, effectively Edu's replacement, has continued to conduct the club's business.

Edu's stint at the City Ground will leave him scarred and his upwardly mobile status was always going to be assessed after joining Forest, which in itself was by no means a step forward, if anything its set him back.

Sports.title: Askey proud of Tour of Britain efforts but admits he wanted more
Sports.content:
Askey proud of Tour of Britain efforts but admits he wanted more

Askey's hopes of matching 1989 winner Robert Millar evaporated in Saturday's stage around the Yorkshire Dales, meaning he came into yesterday's concluding dash around the Scottish Borders with twin ambitions - protecting his narrow advantage in the sprints standings and hanging on to second in the general classification.

View 2 Images Lewis Askey of NSN Cycling Team, wearing the points jersey, gives chase to Tim Wellens during the fifth stage of the 2026 Lloyds Tour of Britain Men in Earlston. (Image: © SWpix.com (t/a Photography Hub Ltd))

Lewis Askey produced the best Scottish result in the Lloyds Tour of Britain in nearly four decades but admitted he wanted more. Askey's hopes of matching 1989 winner Robert Millar evaporated in Saturday's stage around the Yorkshire Dales, meaning he came into yesterday's concluding dash around the Scottish Borders with twin ambitions - protecting his narrow advantage in the sprints standings and hanging on to second in the general classification.

‌



He missed the first target but hit the second, coming home 42 seconds behind Belgian Tim Wellens, who took overall honours in Earlston. However, Askey still looked a little downbeat, admitting frustration that he and his team allowed the breakaway to form, which cost him the points jersey, won by ten-time Grand Tour stage winner Filippo Ganna.

‌



View 2 Images Picture by Simon Wilkinson/SWpix.com - 06/09/2026 - Cycling - UCI ProSeries - 2026 Lloyds Tour of Britain Men - Stage 5: Earlston to Earlston (156.1km) - Tim Wellens (UAE Team Emirates XRG) comes in first, Lewis Askey (NSN Cycling Team) comes in second, Jasper Stuyven (Soudal Quick-Step) comes in third (Image: © SWpix.com (t/a Photography Hub Ltd))

‌



But with that jersey gone, he and fellow Brit Jake Stewart put in a shift to ensure the margin of the lead group didn't cost him his runner-up prize. "It doesn’t mean loads to me until I stand on the top step," he admitted. "I’m here because I enjoy winning races. I always say a second, or a top five, top ten — they’re all nice performances, and you’re obviously proud of how you’ve ridden and happy with it.

"We were going to prioritise the sprint and I would have enjoyed that, but one mistake, one lack of urgency, and that was gone. I need to say a big thanks to Jake. He kept our group moving and without him there is no way I'd have finished second."

Czech Michal Schuran won the climbers' jersey after getting himself embedded in the early breakaway, while another Scot, Elliot Rowe, was the best young rider after an attention-grabbing week on his home Tour.

‌



"I definitely didn't expect to win this. It's a great bonus at the end of a great week," said Rowe, who made his debut for Scotland at the recent Commonwealth Games. "It's been a really important few days for my development. Everyone wants to make the next step up to become pro, so getting a chance to race these guys and learn from them is so important.

"I’ve had a nice week with zero pressure and I've just enjoyed racing. You don't get the chance to race in Scotland often, so this was a fun day." Elsewhere, Ben Wiggins underlined why a name from cycling's past has a big future.

Wiggins, son of Tour de France winner and five-time Olympic champion Sir Bradley, mixed it with the best to earn a top-ten finish at the Lloyds Tour of Britain. The 21-year-old got himself in an eight-man breakaway on the final stage around the Scottish Borders, going pedal to pedal with a host of Grand Tour veterans and looking every bit the part.

‌



He was never bullied, but with the group bossed by five members of the same team, the odds were always against him winning a stage in a race won by his dad 13 years ago. "I was all-in to win the stage but maybe a bit of youth and inexperience came into it," said Wiggins, who came home sixth behind stage winner Nils Politt.

"It was great to be in the mix with all those big names. I had a moment when the group formed and I was like, ‘This is wicked.’ It was a mint day out. I didn’t expect that to happen at all. “I wouldn’t say I learned loads about myself from it. I know I’ve got the engine to compete with the best — I genuinely feel that. But when those boys are going flat-out, especially on the climbs, it takes some doing.

“We actually had a completely different plan for me being in the breakaway. It unfolded very differently from what I expected, but I took my chance. I’m currently without a job for next year as well, so hopefully that helps my case."

Sports.title: Ben Wiggins stamps his name on the Lloyds Tour of Britain with top ten finish
Sports.content:
Ben Wiggins stamps his name on the Lloyds Tour of Britain with top ten finish

Ben Wiggins, son of Tour de France winner and five-time Olympic champion Sir Bradley, earnt a top-ten finish at the Lloyds Tour of Britain.

View Image Ben Wiggins on stage at the Lloyds Tour of Britain (Image: © SWpix.com (t/a Photography Hub Ltd))

Ben Wiggins underlined why a name from cycling's past has a big future. Wiggins, son of Tour de France winner and five-time Olympic champion Sir Bradley, mixed it with the best to earn a top-ten finish at the Lloyds Tour of Britain.

‌



The 21-year-old got himself in an eight-man breakaway on the final stage around the Scottish Borders, going pedal to pedal with a host of Grand Tour winners and looking every bit the part. He was never bullied, but with the group bossed by five members of the same team, the odds were always against him winning a stage in a race won by his dad 13 years ago.

‌



"I was all-in to win the stage but maybe a bit of youth and inexperience came into it," said Wiggins. "It was great to be in the mix with all those big names. I had a moment when the group formed and I was like, ‘This is wicked.’ It was a mint day out. I didn’t expect that to happen at all.

‌



“I wouldn’t say I learned loads about myself from it. I know I’ve got the engine to compete with the best — I genuinely feel that. But when those boys are going flat-out, especially on the climbs, it takes some doing. We actually had a completely different plan for me being in the breakaway. It unfolded very differently from what I expected, but I took my chance. I’m currently without a job for next year as well, so hopefully that helps my case."

Belgian Tim Wellens took the winner's jersey, with Britain's Lewis Askey 42 seconds behind after a tough day in blustery conditions on roads that will host next year's Tour de France Grand Départ. If Wiggins was all smiles, Askey looked a little downbeat, admitting frustration that he and his team allowed the breakaway to form, which cost him the points jersey, won by ten-time Grand Tour winner Filippo Ganna.

‌



However, with that jersey gone, he and fellow Brit Jake Stewart put in a shift to ensure the margin of the lead group didn't cost him second place in the general classification. "It doesn’t mean loads to me until I stand on the top step," he said.

"I’m here because I enjoy winning races. I always say a second, or a top five, top ten — they’re all nice performances, and you’re obviously proud of how you’ve ridden and happy with it. We were going to prioritise the sprint and I would have enjoyed that, but one mistake, one lack of urgency, and that was gone. I need to say a big thanks to Jake. He kept our group moving and without him there is no way I'd have finished second."

Czech Michal Schuran won the climbers' jersey after getting himself embedded in the early breakaway, while Britain's Elliot Rowe was the best young rider. It's 298 days until the Tour de France starts on these undulating roads, as 'La Grande Boucle' rolls out of Edinburgh, across the Borders and finishes its first stage in the shadow of Carlisle's medieval castle. After this day in the saddle, though, some were left to ponder what's harder: battling punishing climbs in 30 °C at the ongoing Vuelta or tackling devilish crosswinds on twisty roads in the Scottish Borders?

Article continues below

British Cycling is inspiring riders and fans across the country through the Lloyds Tour of Britain, bringing the sport to life and celebrating the joy of cycling through Britain's biggest free-to-spectate cycling event. Visit britishcycling.org.uk

Sports.title: Gemma Stevens battles back from heartbreak to win Defender Burghley Horse Trials
Sports.content:
Gemma Stevens battles back from heartbreak to win Defender Burghley Horse Trials

After 25 years in elite sport, British Equestrian Gemma Stevens finally claims the Defender Burghley Horse Trials title.

View Image Gemma Stevens (GBR) and Chilli Knight winners of the Defender Burghley Horse Trials during the prize giving after the Defender Burghley Horse Trials held in the park land surrounding Burghley House near Stamford in Lincolnshire in the UK between 2nd - 6th September 2026 (Image: © Nixonphoto)

When life knocks you down, the only thing is to get back on your horse and win the biggest individual event of your career. That is exactly what Gemma Stevens did as she etched her name into British eventing royalty after winning the overall crown at the 2026 Defender Burghley Horse Trials.

The 41-year-old from Horsham has been the talk of the week following her heartbreaking outing at the World Championships in Aachen just last month, when she was dropped from the British Equestrian team event score after being eliminated in the cross-country. It was a knock she admitted was one of the lowest moments of her sporting career, despite still winning the gold alongside her teammates.

But fortunes can change very quickly in sport and from the lowest depths to the highest highs, Stevens' stars finally aligned to give her an emotional victory at the world's greatest 5* eventing competition. "I'm not sure I can sum this up quite yet if I am totally honest," said Stevens, who had never won at Burghley and Badminton Horse Trials before.

"I can't believe it. I have managed to stop crying now but I honestly cannot believe it. 25 years of work and finally I've managed to win a 'Big B', and I'm just chuffed. Obviously, it's always a dream to win, and I just knew that he had it in him.

"We so nearly won Badminton a couple of years ago, and I've just known in my heart of hearts there is a big win in this horse. We just needed our stars to align, and they have finally aligned this week."

Stevens jumped a double clear with 16-year-old stallion Chilli Knight in Stamford to overtake Switzerland's Nadja Minder after the dressage phase of the competition on the opening day. And she refused to add any more penalties to her score, making both the expected cross-country and showjumping times to finish on a score of 29.6.

It meant that she took victory a whole 13.4 points ahead of second-placed and fellow Briton Katie Magee, with the USA's Caroline Pamukcu completing the all-female podium in third.

It marked the sixth time in a row that a British rider has won at Burghley, not including the 2021 and 2020 years, which were not run due to Covid. And while this victory closes the door on what had previously been a difficult summer for the rider, she noted that the Championship title is still the one she wants after now finally conquering the famed Burghley course.

"This means more than a championship this time round because obviously I didn't contribute myself on a personal performance to the medal," she added. "My amazing teammates did that for me. But the Championships and the Big Bs are what it's all about for me."

Defender Burghley Horse Trials (3-6 September 2026) has been a major international sporting and social event for over 50 years. It attracts the world's top equestrians and is attended by vast and enthusiastic crowds. For more information visit www.burghley-horse.co.uk

Sports.title: Kylian Mbappe reveals why he might be ahead of Harry Kane in Ballon d’Or race
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappe reveals why he might be ahead of Harry Kane in Ballon d’Or race

Kylian Mbappe is among the favourites to claim this year’s Ballon d’Or but England and Bayern Munich star Harry Kane might have something to say about that claim

View 2 Images Kylian Mbappe is a contender for the Ballon d'Or (Image: Getty Images)

Kylian Mbappe has suggested that his World Cup record should see him among the favourites for the Ballon d’Or.

‌



The France and Real Madrid star scored 42 goals in all competitions for the Spanish giants last season and already has a further four to his name already this term. Mbappe also netted ten times at this summer’s World Cup to claim Miroslav Klose’s record of the tournament’s all-time top scorer.

‌



And he believes that - as well as representing his current employers - should stand him in good stead for the voting. He said: "I think when you play for Real Madrid, the best club in the world, people associate you with this award.

‌



"There are many people that speak about me and the Ballon d'Or. Of course I've made history in the most important competition. Maybe it's a good year for this but people can vote according to what they think."

He added: "I always think I'm the best [player in the world] but everyone has their own opinion. Maybe people think different ways. I don't think it's a discussion we need to have. Of course this year could be good for me to win the Ballon d'Or. But journalists vote."

‌



Mbappe might face some serious competition should he want to claim the Ballon d’Or this year. England’s Harry Kane is also a contender, having enjoyed another glittering season with Bayern Munich, as well as a stunning World Cup.

Asked if he has ambitions of claiming the award, he said: “I'm extremely proud of the season I put out for sure. I think it just fills me with pride because I know not long ago that I was that fan wanting to become a professional footballer.

View 2 Images Harry Kane has enjoyed a brilliant 12 months with Bayern Munich (Image: Getty Images)

‌



“I'm here now, and I'm winning awards like the Golden Shoe. And the Ballon d’Or is the same. Of course, now it's out of my hands in terms of it's down to the voters and the people who decide it. The season I had was my best season by far, and we have to wait and see this.

“It's a weird one because I'm already focused on this season now and the next season and thinking how can I be better, how can I improve. But also I want to appreciate what I did. Time will tell.

“I think the thing with football and opinions - there's so many opinions, so many arguments for different players and people love this player because of that. ‘He's fast, he's got a great IQ, he finishes great.’

Article continues below

“I think that's what makes football special is all those debates and the Ballon d’Or is definitely one of them. So I'm happy that I'm in contention, so we have to wait and see.”

Sports.title: 5 times Gabriel was 'lucky' to avoid red card as Arsenal star called out
Sports.content:
5 times Gabriel was 'lucky' to avoid red card as Arsenal star called out

Arsenal defender Gabriel escaped punishment during his team's weekend victory over Chelsea and it wasn't the first time

View 4 Images Gabriel avoided a red card when Arsenal beat Chelsea (Image: Getty Images)

The fallout from Arsenal's victory over Chelsea has brought plenty of debate over a number of flashpoints. In addition to moments involving England internationals Declan Rice and Cole Palmer at either end, Gunners defender Gabriel received scrutiny for an early challenge involving visiting goalkeeper Emi Martinez.

‌



Gabriel was attempting to find the net when his follow-through made contact with Martinez's head. Accidental or not, though, pundits Wayne Rooney and Ashley Young felt the centre-back was lucky to avoid a card – perhaps even a red one.

‌



"Martinez has got the ball in his hands and Gabriel boots him in the head, he swings a leg and goes way over the top. He's extremely lucky to stay on the pitch," Rooney said on Match of the Day.

‌



Young argued the Brazilian had "got away with one," expressing his surprise that VAR didn't get involved. It wasn't the first time Gabriel might consider himself fortunate to avoid a sending-off during an Arsenal game.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

David Raya reveals what now sets Arsenal apart from Premier League title rivals READ MORE :

Manchester City vs Arsenal, April 2026

Gabriel was involved in a heated exchange with Manchester City striker Erling Haaland during a match at the Etihad Stadium in April 2026. The defender appeared to move his head towards the Norwegian, but the on-field decision of yellow cards for both players was allowed to stand after a VAR check.

‌



Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher described it as a fair outcome but recognised it could have gone another way. "Gabriel is very unwise what he does, it is not the cleverest thing to do and he runs a risk, but if you look, he actually goes does the front of him and not through him, he does not headbutt him," Gallagher said on Ref Watch.

"But he is very, very lucky that Haaland was very, very responsible because if he hits the deck, the whole landscape changes and the referee has a different situation to deal with," he added. However, ex-Arsenal striker Jay Bothroyd saw things differently.

View 4 Images Gabriel escaped with a yellow after his clash with Erling Haaland (Image: Getty Images)

‌

"Gabriel was lucky - when we look at the rules, it is violent conduct if you put your head into someone's face, that was violent conduct and we have seen other people get sent off for that kind of movement towards someone's head,” Bothroyd said. What Haaland said is absolutely right - if he goes down holding his face there, he is going to get a red card and then he is banned for three matches."

Brentford vs Arsenal, February 2026

The trip to Brentford in February was another which brought a yellow card for Gabriel. However, he avoided a second booking for a foul on Dango Ouattara and Bees manager Keith Andrews made his feelings clear.

‌



"It was a definite yellow," Andrews told TNT Sports at the time. "I just feel like the first few fouls always set the bar for how they referee the game, there’s always that level isn’t there and then it felt a few times in the first half we weren’t getting quite the rub of it."

Former Arsenal defender Martin Keown also felt Gabriel was lucky, saying: "I'm not even going to argue with that. There were enough yellows given out... and it felt like that was another one."

Newcastle vs Arsenal, September 2025

View 4 Images Nick Woltemade thought referee Jarred Gillett should have shown Gabriel a red card (Image: Lee Parker - CameraSport via Getty Images)

‌



Early in the same season, Gabriel had another escape after a run-in with Newcastle forward Nick Woltemade. He swung an arm at the German but stayed on the pitch following the incident.

"He’s made the mistake for the goal, he’s fuming, and he’s obviously had a bit of a problem with [Woltemade], so he’s leaving a bit on him. You can’t do that," Jamie Redknapp said on Sky Sports.

"That should be a foul. It could be a sending off. It’s ridiculous, but everyone’s copying each other, all doing the same things, and it just causes a massive melee every single time."

‌



Woltemade was also asked about the incident and suggested he might have been better off going to ground. "I felt his elbow in my face and I'm two metres [tall] so his arm has to be really high," he said.

"I don't want to fall down but I think maybe in this situation... I just said to the referee I felt something in my face and I think it's not right to feel something in your face. I'm not the type of player who will fall down for this but it's hard because sometimes maybe you have to do it."

Leeds vs Arsenal, October 2022

View 4 Images Gabriel's red card against Leeds was later downgraded to yellow (Image: Getty Images)

‌



As was the case against Chelsea on Sunday, Chris Kavanagh was the referee when Arsenal travelled to Elland Road in October 2022. That's where the similarity ends on the red card front, though.

Kavanagh initially pointed to the penalty spot, showing Gabriel a red card after a clash with Leeds striker Patrick Bamford in the area. However, the decision was reversed after a VAR check, with Bamford ruled to have fouled his opponent first, and Gabriel's red was changed to a yellow.

The initial red card was believed to have been awarded for the denial of a clear goalscoring opportunity. That no longer applied with the penalty overturned, though some still wondered whether the kick out was worth a red on its own.

‌



Man Utd vs Arsenal, November 2020

Going even further back in time, we arrive at an incident from Gabriel's very first season in English football. The centre-back was booked against Manchester United but some argued he should have seen red after a foul on Mason Greenwood.

"How is that not a red card for Gabriel? He’s fouled Greenwood twice in the one play," one fan wrote. "Gabriel should have had a red and got spun by Greenwood," argued another.

While Gabriel escaped a red card on that occasion, he was dismissed for the first time in his Arsenal career the following month. He picked up two yellow cards in quick succession against Southampton, with Mikel Arteta suggesting he had intended to substitute the player before his second booking.

Sports.title: Ex-F1 boss Bernie Ecclestone, 95, arrested in Portugal for carrying shotgun
Sports.content:
Ex-F1 boss Bernie Ecclestone, 95, arrested in Portugal for carrying shotgun

Bernie Ecclestone was arrested at a Portuguese aerodrome for allegedly carrying a gun having previously been reprimanded for a similar incident back in 2020 but was released after paying bail

View 5 Images Bernie Ecclestone is now 95 years old (Image: Getty Images)

Billionaire ex F1 boss Bernie Ecclestone has reportedly been arrested at a Portuguese aerodrome for illegally carrying a shotgun.

‌



The 95-year-old is said to have been held at Tires Aerodrome in the municipality of Cascais close to Lisbon after landing there in his private jet.

‌



Airport police belonging to Portugal’s PSP force are understood to have made the arrest during a “routine operation.” The weapon Ecclestone was allegedly carrying has been described locally as a shotgun.

‌



He was arrested in May 2022 in Brazil for illegally carrying a gun while boarding a private plane. He acknowledged owning the gun but said at the time he was unaware it was in his luggage.

Lewis Hamilton takes swipe at Ferrari and concedes defeat in F1 title bid READ MORE :

F1 Italian GP suspended after huge Charles Leclerc crash and Lewis Hamilton battle READ MORE :

Ecclestone was freed and allowed to travel to Switzerland after paying bail. He described it afterwards as a “silly, tiny little incident”, saying it had caused a lot of aggravation as he and family tried to leave Sao Paulo by private plane.

He also denied he was formally arrested despite Sao Paulo state’s public security office confirming in a statement a businessman it didn’t name was arrested for possession of a firearm at Campinas’ airport.

‌



Ecclestone said afterwards he had bought the handgun, a LW Seecamp .32, from a Formula One mechanic or tyre man in Brazil years ago without ammunition and purely as a deterrent.

View 5 Images Bernie Ecclestone was arrested at a Portuguese aerodrome (Image: Getty Images)

He added: “They said you need something like this. It might work if someone tried to mug you or something. So I bought it from the guy. I had it in the house and used to muck around with it if people came to visit me or something, we would joke around."

‌



One of sport's most flamboyant characters Ecclestone has opened up on raising both his 71-year-old daughter and six-year-old son. The 95-year-old has four children, with Deborah his oldest from his first marriage to Ivy Bamford.

Tamara, 42, and Petra, 37, followed from second wife Slavica Radic. While he shares youngest kid Ace with Fabiana. Ecclestone told German newspaper Bild: “Ace is a wonderful boy. He’s bright, curious and interested in everything.”

View 5 Images Tamara Ecclestone - Bernie's daughter

‌



Wife Fabiana added: “It’s working very well. Bernie and I are a team and we’re raising Ace as a team. When I get a little impatient, Bernie explains to him in his usual calm and quiet way that he’s not allowed to watch TV for half an hour until he’s done his homework.”

On juggling raising a five-year-old while being father to a 70-year-old, Ecclestone noted: “It’s quite something. You look at your oldest and youngest and realise how much has happened in between.”

He has owned luxury properties in Britain and other countries throughout his career. He now spends much of his time in Gstaad, Switzerland. His daughter Tamara is a famous TV host, model and socialite who is particularly close to her dad.

‌



Last year he confirmed that he had sold his collection of 69 Formula 1 and Grand Prix cars to Mark Mateschitz, the son of late Red Bull co-founder Dietrich Mateschitz. The final price was not disclosed the collection was valued at £500 million.

View 5 Images Billionaire Bernie Ecclestone (Image: ITV)

The cars covered Formula 1 history dating back to the championship's inaugural 1950 season. They included vehicles associated with champions Alberto Ascari, Mike Hawthorn, Niki Lauda, Nelson Piquet and Michael Schumacher.

‌



Among the most famous cars were Lauda's Brabham BT46B "fan car," Ascari's 1951 Italian Grand Prix-winning Ferrari 375 F1 and the Ferrari Schumacher drove during his dominant 2002 championship season.

View 5 Images Bernie Ecclestone with Eddie Jordan (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Ecclestone saidthat finding an appropriate long-term home for the collection mattered more to him than simply accepting the highest offer. Mateschitz said the cars would be preserved and eventually displayed publicly.

Article continues below

In April it was reported Eccleston’s wife had bought a mansion in the prestigious resort area of Quinta da Marinha in Cascais for £35million. Respected Portuguese daily Correio da Manha described the deal at the time as the “largest private sale ever of a home” in the country.

It said Brazilian Fabiana Flosi, 46 years younger than Ecclestone, agreed the purchase of the property around 15 miles west of Lisbon in January after negotiations lasting six months.

There has not yet been any official comment from the PSP about today’s reported arrest which several Portuguese media outlets are now going public with.

Sports.title: Man Utd's four-year-old defence have kept just four clean sheets together in damning record
Sports.content:
Man Utd's four-year-old defence have kept just four clean sheets together in damning record

Manchester United have yet to keep a clean sheet this season and their back four has come under scrutiny

View 2 Images Lisandro Martinez and Harry Maguire started at centre-back against Everton (Image: News Images/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

Manchester United's results under Michael Carrick have been enough to take the Red Devils back into the Champions League, but there are still some doubts. There have been questions asked at the back, with worries arguably exacerbated by a lack of summer investment.

‌



The arrival of Carlos Baleba ought to help, with the Cameroon midfielder expected to provide protection for the back line when he's ready to make his debut after injury. However, the four men who started in defence at Everton on Sunday were also the four who began the painful 4-0 loss at Brentford some four years ago.

‌



Then-manager Erik ten Hag responded to that result by breaking the bank for Casemiro, with the Brazilian thriving in his first season at Old Trafford before fading in his second. That back four of Diogo Dalot, Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez and Luke Shaw have combined for some decent results but questions remain over their ability to shut out opponents.

‌



Carrick has used the combination in two games this season - against Ipswich and Everton - and they have played together 12 times in total. However, a return of four clean sheets in those 12 games isn't the best.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Michael Carrick points finger at Man Utd stars after late Everton draw READ MORE :

In 12 matches with a back four of Dalot-Maguire-Martinez-Shaw, United have won eight, drawn two and lost two. On the surface, that doesn't look like too much to worry about, but the goals conceded column for those games reads 17.

‌



Seven of those 12 encounters have ended with United's opponents scoring two or more goals. That includes two games this season and a trio of 3-2 wins last term, against Arsenal, Fulham and Nottingham Forest.

Spread over a whole season, 17 goals conceded in 12 games would equate to just under 54 goals conceded in 38 matches. Last season, only six teams in the league conceded more than 54 times and three of those were relegated.

If United want to improve on last season's third-place finish, they'll feel they need some improvement on that front. They have conceded 54 goals or more in just four of their Premier League seasons and their highest finish in any of those seasons is sixth.

‌



View 2 Images United played the same back four in a 4-0 defeat at Brentford in 2022 (Image: Getty Images)
