World.title: Jakarta airport extends closure after volcano eruption
World.content:
Jakarta – Indonesia’s main airport postponed reopening on Monday after halting operations following a volcanic eruption that left hundreds of thousands of passengers stranded.

Mount Anak Krakatau, about 150 kilometres (93 miles) from Indonesia’s capital, Jakarta, erupted on Saturday, spewing a fountain of lava and a plume of volcanic ash.

Eight airports halted operations over the weekend after ash was detected in their airspace, disrupting thousands of flights and leaving more than 270,000 passengers stranded, the transport ministry reported on Monday.

“These figures are the cumulative operational impact since 5 September 2026 and cover flights that have been cancelled, delayed, or diverted,” the ministry said in a statement.

Italian tourist Michel Miegge was on holiday with his girlfriend and due to fly home in time for work on Tuesday, but their flight was cancelled.

“We don’t have any news from the airline. We don’t know if we stay another day in Jakarta or find another flight,” the 32-year-old software engineer told AFP.

“I don’t think it’s possible now. We found a nearby hotel, but we saw that many hotels were fully booked.”

Another tourist, French painter Carol Odile, said she came with a group of friends to see Komodo dragons in Flores when she was notified that her flight was cancelled.

“We are disappointed, but our group is optimistic. We hope we can go to Flores Island very soon,” the 60-year-old told AFP.

– Airports closed –

Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport, extended its closure from Monday morning to midnight.

“Due to increased eruption activity at Mount Anak Krakatau, Soekarno-Hatta International Airport has suspended flight operations until 11:59 PM Western Indonesia Time,” the airport said in a social media post.

Halim Perdanakusuma, a smaller airport that caters to both civil and military flights, will also remain closed.

Another small airport in south Sumatra resumed operations on Monday morning, the transport ministry said.

More than 240 domestic and international flights were cancelled or delayed due to volcanic ash on Monday morning alone, Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport said, adding that nearly 30,000 passengers were affected.

The Transport Ministry has prepared six alternative airports — including airports in East Java, Central Java, and Yogyakarta — as options for aircraft that were originally scheduled to land in Jakarta.

“We are encouraging airlines to use these airports to avoid passenger congestion, both for arrivals and departures,” Transport Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said in a statement.

Airport operators would provide free bus services for passengers who wish to fly from other airports.

Dudy said that the Indonesian government also relaxed rules for foreign passengers who may have overstayed as a result of flight cancellations.

– Threat remains high –

Benjamin Foatelli, 48, a perfumer based in Jakarta for a French company, left Italy on Sunday evening for Jakarta on an Etihad flight via Abu Dhabi.

However, his connecting flight from the United Arab Emirates was delayed.

“I don’t know yet if I’ll be able to get back tonight, but I have everything I need to keep working so I can wait calmly for the situation to resolve,” he told AFP by phone.

The probability of an eruption remained high, the country’s geology agency warned.

“The threat from an eruption comes from the ejection of incandescent rocks accompanied by heavy ashfall. Another potential hazard arises from lava flows if the eruption resumes and continues,” agency head Lana Saria said.

Anak Krakatau, which means Child of Krakatau, sits in a strait that separates the islands of Java and Sumatra.

The volcano has been sporadically active since it emerged from the sea at the beginning of last century in the caldera that formed after the 1883 eruption of Mount Krakatau.

A 2018 tsunami triggered by a collapse of parts of Anak Krakatau killed 429 people and displaced thousands.

World.title: Zidan and U.S. envoy discuss plan on state monopoly on arms

Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The President of the Supreme Judicial Council, Judge Dr. Faiq Zidan, met on Monday, September 7, 2026, with the newly appointed Chargé d’Affaires of the United States Embassy in Iraq, Stephen Fagin.

Judicial and Political Framework on Arms Control

Judicial Enforcement Backing: Judge Dr. Faiq Zidan reiterated the judiciary’s constitutional mandate to support executive security operations aimed at curbing unauthorized weapons, holding illicit armed groups accountable, and upholding statutory penalties.

Coordination Committee Formulation: The arms-monopoly strategy is being drafted under a phased plan adopted by the Coordination Framework via a specialized committee.

Timing & Implementation Strategy: The committee will formally publish the terms and operational guidelines of the arms-control initiative once consultations are finalized and designated milestones are met.

Constitutional Compliance & Foreign Relations: Discussions underscored that enforcing state authority over weaponry aligns directly with the Iraqi Constitution and statutory law, while safeguarding sovereign diplomatic ties with Washington and multilateral partners.

Strategic Dimensions of the Engagement

Focus Area Operational Track Intended Outcome Monopoly on Arms Specialized judicial enforcement alongside interior security forces Consolidates federal authority and reins in unregulated armed actors. Coordination Framework Committee Drafting policy roadmaps and phased surrender/licensing criteria Ensures domestic political consensus behind executive disarmament actions. U.S.-Iraq Bilateral Relations Diplomatic engagement with Chargé d’Affaires Stephen Fagin Reassures international partners on sovereign security and institutional stability. The meeting reflects deliberate alignment between Iraq’s highest judicial leadership and governing political coalitions on the weapons file, directly addressing long-standing international and domestic concerns over unregulated arms.

By integrating judicial oversight into the security and legislative frameworks managed by the government, Iraqi authorities aim to demonstrate substantive progress in institutional discipline, public safety, and statutory sovereignty.

World.title: Jaguar Land Rover to cut 4,000 jobs as European car sector hits skids
World.content:
London – Jaguar Land Rover said Monday that it would cut “around 4,000 roles over the next two years”, or about ten percent of its global workforce, in a further blow to Europe’s automobile industry.

The company revealed its voluntary redundancy scheme just days after the German car giant Volkswagen announced 50,000 new job cuts.

It follows months of turmoil caused by a cyberattack on the British luxury carmaker and US President Donald Trump’s sector-wide tariffs.

The world’s biggest carmakers across Europe, the United States and Japan are also facing strong competition from Chinese manufacturers, as well as the need to invest heavily as the industry shifts toward electric vehicles.

“The automotive industry faces significant challenges, with technological change amidst intense competition and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty,” JLR’s chief executive PB Balaji said in the statement, which also said it would target cost savings of £1.7 billion ($2.3 billion).

“Over the next 12 months, we will launch five new products, continue to leverage the strength of our brands and renew our focus on North America, amongst other markets, to help us deliver double digit revenue growth,” Balaji added.

The vast majority of JLR employees — around 34,000 people — are based in the UK.

In an earlier statement Monday, JLR identified management roles as those at risk, while local media reports said most of the cuts would be in the UK.

– Cyberattack –

UK Business minister Jonathan Reynolds is scheduled to meet with JLR executives this week to discuss the job losses.

“We recognise this will be difficult news for colleagues affected, and are committed to supporting everyone with care, fairness and respect,” Balaji said.

“Together, these actions will help build a stronger, more competitive JLR for all our stakeholders.”

The restructuring comes a year after a major cyberattack halted JLR’s production in Britain and severely affected its finances.

Owned by India’s Tata Motors, JLR was forced to halt production for more than a month, costing the company £260 million, according to its latest estimate.

Hit also by US tariffs, the carmaker posted a loss of £244 million for its fiscal year ending in March, compared with a net profit of £1.8 billion in 2024-25.

“We must further simplify our organisation, improve efficiency, and build greater resilience,” JLR said Monday.

Seeking to move on from the cyberattack, the company last week opened orders for its new fully electric Range Rover.

Last week, Volkswagen said its management and unions had agreed to axe a a total of 100,000 jobs by the end of the decade, the biggest-ever restructuring in the global auto industry.

The company said it had approved a plan involving the reduction of around 50,000 jobs, on top of 50,000 already agreed earlier this year.

World.title: US average diesel price rises to record $5.90 a gallon: AAA
World.content:
London – Average diesel prices in the United States climbed to a new record Monday, the motorists’ association AAA said, as damage to Gulf refineries during the war against Iran disrupted supplies.

The price of the fuel largely used in road hauling, agriculture and construction hit $5.9015, the AAA said, around 30 cents higher than the average just one week earlier.

Steep fuel price increases since the US and Israel launched attacks on Iran six months ago are putting pressure on President Donald Trump ahead of midterm congressional elections in November.

He has vowed to tackle higher costs of living but the ongoing war against Tehran has severely impacted tanker shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, sending fuel prices higher across the board.

Diesel cost just $3.71 on average a year ago, and the higher prices are squeezing farmers and truckers, which could be forced to pass on the increases to consumers.

Average prices for regulator gasoline stood at $4.15 a gallon on Monday — when millions of Americans typically travel by car for the Labor Day holiday.

That is up from $3.20 on average a year ago. In western US states prices are even higher, with regular gas costing $5.86 in California and $4.54 in Arizona, the AAA said.

World.title: Ford names Shamal Al Jazeera (SAT) official distributor in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Ford Middle East and Africa has officially appointed Shamal Al-Jazeera for Automotive and Commercial Agencies (SAT) as its new authorized distributor in the Republic of Iraq, with operations formally commencing on October 1, 2026, the automaker announced on Monday, September 7, 2026.

Under the partnership agreement, SAT will assume responsibility for the nationwide importation and retail distribution of Ford passenger and commercial vehicles, genuine motor parts supply, and comprehensive aftersales and maintenance operations across the Iraqi market.

Shamal Al-Jazeera (SAT) is formed through a joint venture combining corporate capital and automotive retail expertise:

March Holding: A regional investment conglomerate managing over ten operational subsidiaries in Iraq spanning financial technology, digital payment processing, software solutions, and e-commerce logistics.

Olayan Group (Automotive Division): A regional distributor with over 50 years of automotive representation across the Middle East, managing franchised distribution networks for brands such as Hyundai, Kia, BYD, Isuzu, Geely, and GAC.

Executive Leadership: The venture is led by Chief Executive Officer Mohammed Olayan alongside General Manager Yassin Al-Saati.

Ford outlined a structured handover framework with outgoing distributor Al-Kasid Group, which has represented the American brand in Iraq for the past nine years:

Transition Window (Through September 30, 2026): Customers will continue to purchase vehicles, source OEM components, and access certified routine maintenance at existing Al-Kasid service centers and showrooms without disruption.

Transfer Date (October 1, 2026): SAT assumes sole commercial responsibility for new vehicle orders, dealership networks, and technical service points.

Warranty and Service Continuity: Factory vehicle warranties, extended coverage programs, and existing service contracts will remain valid and fully honored following the operational handover to SAT.

Strategic Partnership Overview

Feature / Dimension Current Setup (Through Sept 30, 2026) New Operating Framework (From Oct 1, 2026) Official Distributor Al-Kasid Group (9-year tenure) Shamal Al-Jazeera (SAT) Strategic Shareholders Automotive trading group March Holding (Fintech/E-commerce) + Olayan Group (Automotive) Operational Scope Nationwide sales, parts, and service Showroom expansion, digital retail, logistics, and certified workshops Warranty & Parts Coverage Active under official terms Full continuity; honors all active warranties and OEM supply Regional Leadership Ravi Ravichandran, President of Ford Middle East & North Africa

Ravi Ravichandran, President of Ford Middle East and North Africa, stated that Iraq remains a central growth market for the company’s regional strategy, noting that SAT’s combination of local commercial expertise and dealership infrastructure will support customer engagement through the purchase and ownership cycle.

Mohammed Olayan, CEO of SAT, affirmed that the company is establishing upgraded retail showrooms and modern diagnostic service facilities across Iraqi governorates to support Ford’s lineup, which includes internal combustion, hybrid, and electric models across the Ford Blue, Ford Pro, and Ford Model e divisions.

World.title: ‘Will reduce UP to Orwellian Dystopia’: Allahabad HC raps Noida DM over student’s NSA detention
World.content:
Akriti Chaudhary, a 24-year-old Delhi University history graduate and student activist, was arrested in connection with cases arising from a workersâ protest in Noida in April 2026

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Allahabad High Court has ordered recovery of Rs 5 lakh from the salaries of the Gautam Buddha Nagar district magistrate and other officials after quashing the National Security Act (NSA) detention of Delhi University student and activist Akriti Chaudhary.The division bench of Justices Atul Sreedharan and Achal Sachdev held that Chaudhary's detention violated her fundamental right to life and personal liberty under Article 21, finding that the material relied upon by authorities did not justify invoking the stringent preventive detention law.The court directed that Rs 5 lakh be paid to Chaudhary as compensation and recovered from the salary of Gautam Buddha Nagar DM Medha Roopam and other officers found responsible, including the SHO who prepared the initial report backing her detention. It also directed that the court's displeasure with the officials be entered in their service records.In a strongly worded September 2 order, the court criticised the manner in which the detention order was passed and warned that continued "despotic" conduct by "errant" bureaucrats could reduce Uttar Pradesh to an "Orwellian Dystopia", reported PTI.Chaudhary, a 24-year-old history graduate, was arrested in connection with cases arising from a workers' protest in Noida in April 2026.The UP Police invoked the NSA against her and activist-journalist Satya Verma on May 13. They were among activists arrested in cases related to the protest seeking higher wages.The court said the police dossier against Chaudhary contained allegations but lacked credible supporting material. It said the DM was required to independently examine the record before deciding whether preventive detention was warranted."The conduct of the Gautam Buddha Nagar DM who passed the impugned order is worthy of derision," the court said.The bench noted that Chaudhary had no previous criminal record and that there was no material showing she had incited violence. It said the circumstances suggested that the detention was intended to make an example of her and discourage others from exercising their right to freedom of speech and expression in support of labourers.The court also questioned the state's version of when Chaudhary was arrested. It recorded that she was taken into custody around 5.30 pm on April 11 at Botanical Garden Metro Station, although the state claimed her arrest took place on April 12.A notice issued under Section 130 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) was cited by the state. However, the notice carried General Diary Entry No. 37, which was generated only at 10.20 am on April 12."Mentioning the GD number in the notice under section 130 of the BNSS reveals that the petitioner was already arrested and the procedure of giving a notice under section 130 of the BNSS was ex post facto the arrest and nothing more than a sham," Justice Sreedharan said."I agree with the view of brother Justice Achal Sachdev that the notice u/s. 130 of the BNSS was prepared after the arrest of the Petitioner and that is the reason why the time of issuance is not mentioned in the notice and its omission is deliberate," he added.The court said preventive detention under the NSA is an exception and cannot be used in place of ordinary criminal law. It described the grounds of Chaudhary's detention as "repetitive, speculative and are only opinion-based", noting the absence of material supporting those conclusions.It also cautioned authorities against treating peaceful public protests as a threat merely because they could potentially lead to a breach of peace."Preventing people from gathering in public spaces or agitating for their rights on the grounds of assumed breach of peace would be throwing the baby out of the bath water," the court said.The bench said the constitutional protection of freedom of speech and expression extends to peaceful gatherings and collective action, and cannot be curtailed merely on the basis of the state's subjective assessment.The court also reminded bureaucrats and police officers that their duty is to the Constitution rather than the political executive, saying that people are the masters in a democracy.It warned that officials who disregard their constitutional oath could come to be seen as an "oppressive vestige of the British Empire", creating an environment of civil unrest.The court said the judiciary could pass "harsh orders" to compensate citizens where official excesses or illegalities infringe upon civil liberties without adequate cause or due process.

World.title: Fake encounter case: Allahabad HC seeks UP, Rajasthan Police reports over conflicting arrest versions
World.content:
Allahabad HC has sought police reports after conflicting accounts emerged over the accusedâs arrest in Jaipur and subsequent encounter in Firozabad

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The Allahabad high court has sought reports from senior officers of the Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan Police after conflicting accounts emerged over the arrest of a theft accused from Jaipur and his subsequent involvement in a police encounter in Firozabad, news agency PTI reported.A division bench of Justice Ajay Bhanot and Justice Divesh Kumar Samant passed the order while hearing a writ petition filed by Riya Gautam, wife of the accused, Awadhesh. The court directed the additional director general of police (ADGP), Agra Zone, to file his personal affidavit regarding the encounter and asked the commissioner of police (CP), Jaipur, to submit a report on the arrest.Gautam had alleged that on December 5, 2025, around 10pm, police personnel reached the company in Jaipur where her husband worked and took him away without informing the family. A subsequent Rajasthan Police inquiry stated that Awadhesh was wanted in a theft case registered in Firozabad and that he was later sent to judicial custody there, with Jaipur police personnel accompanying the UP Police team.The high court, however, noted that the Rajasthan Police account was at variance with the FIR. According to the prosecution's version, an informer had tipped off the police about Awadhesh's whereabouts in Firozabad, where he and a co-accused were allegedly found near a cold storage.The FIR states that the accused challenged the police and attacked them with firearms, following which Awadhesh sustained a gunshot injury in the ensuing encounter.The petitioner's counsel alleged before the court that Awadhesh had been injured in a fake encounter allegedly carried out by police authorities to burnish their credentials. In view of the contrasting accounts, the court directed the ADGP, Agra Zone and CP, Jaipur, to place their reports before it. The order, dated September 2, also directed that a copy be sent to the CP, Jaipur, through the registrar general of the Rajasthan high court. The matter has been listed for September 17.

World.title: Lucknow tops clean air survey 2026 for taking air pollution control measures, none of the big metros met the acceptable limit of PM10 levels in 2025-26
World.content:
Lucknow tops Swachh Vayu Survekshan 2026; Indore, Jabalpur follow

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Lucknow is ranked at the top followed by Indore and Jabalpur as second and third, respectively, in the list of million-plus population cities in the âSwachh Vayu Survekshanâ (clean air survey) 2026 for implementing air pollution mitigation measures under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP).The survey report, released by the Union environment ministry on the International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies on Monday, shows that though the levels of the average PM10 (particulate matter 10), a key pollutant, continue to be high in these cities compared to others in 2025-26, they still figured as the top three cities in the list due to scoring high on other parameters whose weightage is higher than the reduction in PM10 concentration level.The average annual PM10 concentration in Lucknow was 135 micrograms per cubic metre (Î¼g/m3) during 2025-26, whereas it was 76 Î¼g/m3 in Indore and 78 Î¼g/m3 in Jabalpur. Last year, Indore was at the top, followed by Jabalpur in second position, and Agra and Surat in joint third position for their performance during 2024-25.Delhi with PM10 concentration of 200 Î¼g/m3 is ranked 21st in the survey list, whereas Pune (97 Î¼g/m3) is placed at 12th rank, Hyderabad (80 Î¼g/m3) at 19th, Jaipur (143 Î¼g/m3) at 20th, Mumbai (81 Î¼g/m3) at 28th rank, Bangalore (76 Î¼g/m3) at 32nd, Varanasi (75 Î¼g/m3) at 34th, Chennai (69 Î¼g/m3) at 35th and Kolkata (87 Î¼g/m3) at 38th.Except in Delhi and Jaipur, the level of PM10 is less in these big cities than in Lucknow, which topped the list as reduction in PM10 concentration level has low weightage in the overall score. None of these big metros, however, met the national ambient air quality standards (NAAQS) by reporting annual average PM10 concentrations of less than 60 Î¼g/m3.âDevelopment and environmental conservation are not at cross purposes but can go together while maintaining the quality of life for the citizens. It is the responsibility of each citizen to ensure that generations to come are able to live in a clean environment,â said chairperson, National Green Tribunal (NGT), Justice Prakash Shrivastava, who was the chief guest at the event to award the cities for their performance.The survey has ranked 130 cities on the basis of real action on the ground to deal with different polluting activities, considering eight parameters including measures taken by cities on road dust, solid waste management, vehicular emissions, industrial pollution, construction and demolition waste management and other emissions (such as DG sets and commercial establishments).The ministry, on the occasion, shared that 108 out of 130 cities have shown improvement in PM10 levels in 2025-26 with respect to the levels of 2017-18, whereas 26 cities recorded reductions in PM10 concentration of more than 40% during the period and 14 cities met the NAAQS.

World.content:

CHANDIGARH: Admissions to Punjab government-run de-addiction centres rose by more than 164 percent in a year, with 25,290 people admitted in 2025 compared with 9,577 in 2024, according to data released by the state government on Monday.The Punjab government said the figures indicate growing public confidence in its treatment and rehabilitation network under its anti-drug campaign, âYudh Nashean Virudhâ, launched in March 2025. More than 14,000 people had already been admitted to government de-addiction centres by July 2026.The government said the increase in admissions suggested that more individuals and families were approaching formal treatment instead of allowing stigma around addiction to prevent them from seeking help.Admissions to government rehabilitation centres also recorded a sharp increase, rising from 2,644 in 2024 to 8,574 in 2025 â a jump of more than 224 percent. By July 2026, over 5,800 people had been admitted, nearly 68 percent of the total admissions recorded in 2025.The stateâs outpatient opioid-assisted treatment (OOAT) network has also seen an increase in registrations. New registrations rose from 13,033 in 2024 to 17,702 in 2025, while more than 12,500 new patients had registered by August 2026, the government said.Punjab has also invoked provisions under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act to facilitate treatment. As of August 27, more than 11,000 individuals had been granted immunity under Section 64A of the Act, which provides legal immunity to people suffering from drug addiction who are charged with consumption or possession, subject to its conditions.Health and family welfare minister Balbir Singh said the rise in admissions was among the most encouraging indicators of the anti-drug campaign, as more people were seeking institutional support and entering the formal treatment system.âYudh Nashean Virudh stands on three pillars: strict enforcement against smugglers, treatment and rehabilitation for the affected, and prevention to protect our children before drugs ever reach them,â Singh said.He added that the governmentâs focus was to help people recover from addiction, restore families and provide those struggling with substance abuse a pathway to recovery.

World.title: 'I apologise': Bengal CM Adhikari after govt ad sparks row over 'distorted' Durga image
World.content:
NEW DELHI: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Monday apologised over a government  that showed Goddess Durga with 11 arms instead of the traditional 10, saying those responsible had been cautioned and promising greater care in future.

The  appeared in newspapers ahead of a coordination meeting on Durga Puja preparations at Milan Mela Prangan. It carried an image of Durga with an extra arm holding an indistinct object, triggering criticism from opposition leaders.

"First of all, as the chief minister of the state, I apologise. A defective  was published this morning. I apologise for that. Those who issued the defective  have been cautioned.

The government will be more careful about such matters in future," he said.

Opposition targets BJP government

The  was issued to announce the meeting organised by Kolkata Police and the Kolkata Municipal Corporation in collaboration with the state information and cultural affairs department.

CPIM leader Shatarup Ghosh was among those who criticised the depiction and took a swipe at the BJP government.

"Gods gave Durga ten hands and weapons to kill the demon. The BJP government has given her an extra hand," Ghosh said.





TMC MLA and spokesperson Kunal Ghosh also objected to the image and raised the issue with the chief minister on X.

"Honourable chief minister, in the government , Maa Durga, who is traditionally depicted as 'doshobhuja' (ten-armed), has become 'ekadoshbhuja' (eleven-armed). According to the scriptures, one hand needs to be removed," wrote TMC spokesperson Kunal Ghosh on X.

He posted a picture of the , which also featured photographs of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Adhikari alongside the image of Goddess Durga.

"We hear about various codes of conduct every day. If the number of the Mother's arms increases in 2026, the matter could become complicated. Please immediately instruct the department concerned not to distort the original depiction of the Mother Goddess," he added.

"It can be corrected. The matter should not be politicised," Bhattacharya said when asked about the controversy.

in West Bengal, with the administration stressing the traditional character of the festival.

Theme-based Puja celebrations were also discussed at Monday's meeting. Adhikari said organisers would be free to use themes but warned them against choosing concepts that could hurt religious or cultural sentiments or undermine Sanatan traditions.

The government has said the coordination meeting was intended to help ensure that Durga Puja, West Bengal's biggest annual cultural celebration, is conducted safely and peacefully.

World.title: Karan Rajendra Darda elected INS president for 2026-27

The INS, the apex body of publishers of newspapers, magazines and periodicals in the country, said Darda succeeds Vivek Gupta of Sanmarg as president.

Darda, executive director of Lokmat Media Group, said he would work towards protecting press freedom, strengthening the newspaper industry, encouraging innovation and ensuring that all members, irrespective of their size, have an equal voice.

âTogether, we will make Indian journalism stronger and future-ready,â Darda said.

Darda joined the family business in 2005 and has contributed to the growth, transformation and diversification of Lokmat Media Group, with a focus on innovation, technology, operational efficiency and new business opportunities. He has also championed Project Butterfly, aimed at paperless workflows, and Project Sky, focused on automation and organisational efficiency.

World.title: From ancient Gurukuls to AI frontiers: CM Yogi unveils education blueprint for UP's youth
World.content:
LUCKNOW: Chief Minister

has written a letter to the people of Uttar Pradesh on the occasion of Teacherâs Day and ahead of International Literacy Day, stressing the need to combine traditional education with modern technology and skills.

In his letter, Yogi said teachers are âthe lamps who spread the light of knowledgeâ and play a key role in shaping future generations. He said the government had honoured 81 teachers on September 5 for their contribution to nation-building.

Yogi said education should go beyond reading and writing and equip children with knowledge, values, discipline, self-confidence and an understanding that gives the right direction to their lives.

Referring to the ancient Gurukul tradition, he said holistic education should remain the foundation of the modern education system.

The chief minister said rapid technological changes had made AI literacy as important as digital literacy. He said AI, deep-tech and emerging technologies were opening opportunities in education, healthcare, agriculture, industry and employment. He added that the AI City in Lucknow and the developing drone and UAV technology ecosystem in Kanpur were laying the foundation for new technological possibilities in Uttar Pradesh.





Yogi highlighted Operation Kayakalp, Mission Prerna, Mukhyamantri Abhyudaya Yojana and skill development programmes, saying the state government had focused on improving education quality and school facilities, preparing students for competitive examinations and developing youth skills.

He said these efforts had helped achieve significant success in minimising the school dropout rate across the state, with more children joining the mainstream of education.

Calling teachers the most important link in the education journey, Yogi said they instil values, curiosity, discipline, self-confidence and a sense of responsibility among students while connecting Indiaâs knowledge tradition with modern knowledge and innovation.

World.title: CPI(M) leader P. Shanmugam condemns Vijay for ‘body shaming’ Stalin
World.content:
CPI(M) State secretary P. Shanmugam on Monday (September 7, 2026) took strong exception to Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s remarks in the Assembly on DMK president M.K. Stalin, accusing him of body-shaming the DMK president over the broken jaw he suffered during his detention under the MISA, when Emergency was imposed in India.

“The country knows the history of the struggles to protect democracy and the repressive measures and excesses unleashed during the Emergency. Mr. Stalin was brutally attacked by the police, and his jaw was broken. It is condemnable, however great they may be, to ridicule him. The act of the Chief Minister is irresponsible,” Mr. Shanmugam said in a post on X.

Mr. Shanmugam, whose party provides outside support to the ruling TVK, said though Mr. Vijay had replied to the demands for grants for the Police and Fire and Rescue Services Departments, his reply had failed to answer the questions raised by the MLAs.

“Instead of speaking about issues concerning the people, his reply targeted the principal Opposition party. When all democratic organisations are under the clutches of the Enforcement Directorate, levelling allegations made by the agency is not appropriate,” Mr. Shanmugam said.

He said it was against the ethics of the Assembly to use the House to eulogise individuals and launch personal attacks. “Harsh personal attacks should be kept for meetings outside the Assembly. Wasting the time of the Assembly, which is run on taxpayers’ money, is unacceptable,” he added.

World.title: U.K. government condemns protests against small boat arrivals
World.content:
The U.K. government and Ministers condemned protests by hundreds of people in Portsmouth, who had gathered until the early hours of Monday (September 7, 2026) morning to protest the arrival of illegal migrants on a dinghy from France. Protesters faced off with police holding riot shields, as they sought to block buses carrying migrants for processing in Kent.

“We condemn the intimidating and thuggish behaviour we saw in Portsmouth last night,” a Home Office spokesperson said in a statement emailed to The Hindu and other news organisations.

The words were echoed by government Ministers. The way the protesters behaved “crosses a line”, Treasury Secretary Emma Reynolds said.

Police and Crime Commissioner for Hampshire and the Isle of White, Donna Jones, who is affiliated to the Conservative Party, said 140 migrants arrived in one boat early Sunday (September 6) morning from France and arrived in the U.K. around midday on Sunday.

The boat had reportedly been followed by French authorities for about 10 hours, halfway across the English Channel. The Home Office declined to comment on whether any of the migrants who had arrived in Portsmouth on Sunday were Indian nationals.

A day earlier, some 200 protesters took to the streets in the coastal port town of Dover, with visuals of masked men boarding trains and marching along the road chanting , “Whose streets? Our streets.”

Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said: “I condemn it. I mean, peaceful protest – essential part of British life, but that’s not dressing up in costumes like this and disrupting people’s lives.”

‘Lack of border control’

Commissioner Jones said the U.K. government had “lost control” of the 100s of miles of British coastline in an interview with Sky News. In another interview, she said that her constituency did not have the processing facilities for migrants and that there would be “significant” issues if traffickers shift their routes from Dover to Portsmouth, which is farther west than where dinghies carrying migrants from France typically enter the U.K.

The number of protestors had grown to 400-500 by midnight on Sunday, and they stayed on till about 3 a.m. in Eastney, in Portsmouth, Ms. Jones said “when a legal position was agreed” and protesters agreed they had made their point.

Ms. Jones called the protests “a very worrying escalation” of the situation but said “most” protesters were lawfully protesting. She said the incidents were a “real wake up call” for the U.K. government over the lack of border control.

Since the July 2024 election of the Labour government under Keir Starmer, 48,000 crossing attempts had been prevented as per government data. The French and U.K. governments have signed two agreements, since the election, to control irregular crossings through the English Channel.

World.title: No special treatment for unruly customers claiming political links, says Cyberabad top cop
World.content:
Cyberabad Police Commissioner M. Ramesh on Monday directed owners of hotels, bars, restaurants, pubs and hookah centres to strictly comply with licensing and operating norms, warning that legal action would be taken against establishments found violating the rules.

At a review meeting with business owners and officials at the Cyberabad police commissioner’s office auditorium, Commissioner Ramesh said establishments must possess all required permits and licences, including clearances from the Fire Department, CMC, Chief Medical and Health Officer and Town Planning Department. Licences issued through the CPPMS portal should also be renewed on time, he said.

The Commissioner said the number of officially licensed establishments within the Cyberabad commissionerate appeared low despite a large number of hotels, restaurants, pubs and similar businesses operating in the area. He said instances of establishments functioning without proper licences had come to the police’s notice and warned that legal action would follow.

Business owners raised concerns over different departments having varying timelines for licences and permits. Mr Ramesh directed officials to coordinate with the concerned departments to address the issues while ensuring compliance with regulations.

He made it clear that pubs, bars and similar establishments must close at the permitted time and that no activities, including sale of alcohol, would be allowed after closing hours. Minors must not be permitted into bars and restaurants, he said.

The Commissioner also directed managements to ensure that staff had valid Aadhaar verification, identification documents and proof of age, and warned against employing minors.

The officer also told business owners to monitor customer behaviour and said no special treatment would be given to people claiming to be relatives of politicians or other prominent persons if they violated rules or behaved rudely with staff. The law would apply equally to everyone, he said.

He also asked establishments to prevent altercations and clashes between groups in bars and pubs, noting that such incidents could lead to law-and-order problems and inconvenience to the public. Owners were asked to cooperate with police in curbing the use and sale of narcotics and other banned substances.

On hookah centres, the Commissioner said such establishments could not operate in view of the ban on hookah activities in Telangana. He warned that violations of COTPA provisions could attract strict action, including penalties of up to seven years’ imprisonment and fines of up to ₹2 lakh.

Mr Ramesh said the Cyberabad police did not intend to hinder businesses operating legally, but would take strict action against establishments that violated laws and regulations.

World.title: Ganesh idols that grow after immersion
World.content:
When Swarajit Alakananda was passing by Flower Market around Ganesh Chaturthi in 2017, the colourful clay idols for sale by the roadside made him pause. “They looked beautiful, but I wondered if there was danger lurking behind, as the Tamil proverb goes,” recalls the 32-year-old. Swarajit has always been a Nature lover and was involved in lake clean-ups even back then. “I wondered what the idols might do to our waterbodies once they were submerged,” he says.

What if the idols were made of nothing but pure earth? What if they came to life once they touched water? Thus was born the idea of ‘seed Ganesha’, one that took the city by storm in 2017. Swarajit, who runs an NGO called So Aware, worked with potters in places such as Edayarpalayam, Selvapuram, and Sundakkamuthur to come up with eco-friendly variations of Ganesha idols. The best part: they could be submerged at home in a bucket of water and once they dissolved, the vegetable seeds in them sprouted forth. If cared for, they yielded vegetables for the entire family.

Swarajit’s idea was welcomed by consumers and the city corporation alike, and he and his team worked round the clock to deliver the idols themselves. He recalls that the K Vijayakarthikeyan, who served as the Commissioner of the Coimbatore Corporation back then, was especially supportive. “We made idols with two tonnes of clay,” he says. The following year, they set up a distribution network in the city and have been popularising seed Ganeshas ever since. Today, their idols are available at around 15 shops in Coimbatore.

The making of a seed Ganesha begins with convincing potters to refrain from using harsh chemicals to paint the finished product. Swarajit says that most of them have been following a particular style for years and were at first hesitant to venture into something new. Today though, many of them are embracing the trend. “I work with artisans who are able to offer a nice finish,” says Swarajit, pointing to the features of the Ganesha idols. “Since they cannot be accentuated by paint, they have to be shaped well by hand,” he says.

Once the idols are made and dried in shade for over 30 days, they are ready for the next step. All of them are hollow, and come with a small opening at the back, through which seeds are dropped. For this, Swarajit employs student volunteers from the city. They gather at his office in Ramnagar — he runs a company called Fix Your Gadgets — a few days before the festival to do so.

Volunteers drop a pinch of the seeds — there is ladiesfinger, tomato, beans, brinjal, radish, tulsi, and cucumber — into the opening, along with a small pinch of seeds of greens. The team also adds a handful of red soil and manure before sealing the opening with a small amount of clay. The greens, explains Swarajit, go into every idol by default. “This is to remind people to water the plants a few days after the idol is submerged,” he explains. Greens will automatically sprout, signalling the presence of a lifeform inside, in case people forget they exist. The seeds, Swarajit says, are native varieties that he sources from farmers in Thiruvannamalai.

“The core philosophy is to send back to the soil what was taken from it,” he says, speaking about the clay that goes into the idols, adding, “Hopefully, reducing substances such as Plaster of Paris from polluting our waterbodies.” Swarajit offers seed Ganeshas ranging from four inches onwards to those as tall as two and a half feet.

The taller ones are filled with wheat, rava, corn and aval inside, and can be submerged with a clean conscience in lakes. “The grains will be eaten by fish and birds,” says Swarajit.

The initiative is not driven by profit. Swarajit says the idols are priced such that the potters who crafted them get up to 60% of the profit. Even as the city prepares itself for Ganesh Chaturthi, Swarajit is readying seeds and calling for volunteers, who will soon get to work. Ganeshas the colour of earth will start arriving from potter colonies, ready to carry a beating heart that will sprout forth with life.

For details, call 9655667775. Visit soaware.org.in

Idols with water-based colours

Rajavalli Shanmugam Arts’ 40,000 sqft godown is filled with Ganesha idols in various sizes and colours. While the tall idols — those ranging from three and a half to 10 feet — are made of paper mache, the smaller ones are made with clay. “We’ve made 20,000 clay idols this year,” says S Saravana Kumar, who owns the crafts venture in Selvapuram.

Saravana Kumar knows that the chemicals from the paint he uses on the idols can pollute our waterbodies. “Five years ago, I made the switch to water-based paints,” says the 56-year-old, adding that until then, his team used enamel-based paint. “Water-based paints are mainly composed of limestone and hence will not cause much harm to our lakes once the idols are submerged,” he says.

Ganesha idols, unlike golu dolls, are not fired at the kiln. “They are made with pachai mann [raw soil] and are painted once they are completely dry,” says Saravana Kumar. He also makes idols that are brown in colour bearing a coating of varnish. Idols made by Rajavalli Shanmugam Arts’ team are available at Poompuhar and Gandhi Sarvodaya Sangh in the city. Saravana Kumar is packing bulk orders for customers as we speak. “I send idols to wholesale dealers in Tiruppur, Mettupalayam, Pollachi and Udumalpet,” he says.

For details, call 9894395589

World.title: Funeral of convicted war criminal Mladic draws thousands, opens old wounds
World.content:
Thousands of people gathered in Belgrade on ‌Monday (September) for the funeral of the former Bosnian Serb General Ratko Mladic, who died ​last week while serving a life sentence for genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity.

Crowds ⁠carrying Serbian flags and pictures of Mladic wearing a traditional Serbian military cap gathered outside the church in a Belgrade suburb where the head of the country’s Orthodox church, Serbian Patriarch Porfirije, presided over the service.

Mladic’s coffin, surrounded by armed ‌soldiers in fatigues and accompanied by a brass band, was then paraded through streets thronged with onlookers, who chanted his name. He was buried at a nearby cemetery next to his ‌daughter, who died in 1994.

Also read | Judges uphold conviction of Serb military chief Ratko Mladic

It was one of the biggest public funerals in Serbia since the fall ‌of ⁠communism in 1990 and showed how revered Mladic remains among many in Serbia and in ⁠Bosnia’s autonomous Serb Republic, despite his convictions linked to his role in the 1995 Srebrenica massacre and in the siege of Sarajevo — two of the bloodiest events in post-war Europe.

“He is a hero,” Djordje, a 34-year-old man who came from Prijepolje to pay respects ​to Mladic, said. “He was a great military strategist.”

CONFLICTS ‌TRIGGERED BY BREAK-UP OF YUGOSLAVIA

Mladic’s death has stirred up strong feelings linking back to the break-up of Yugoslavia and the ethnic conflicts that ensued in the Balkans.

Mladic was found guilty by the United Nations International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia of genocide for his role in the 1995 Srebrenica massacre, ‌in which about 8,000 Bosniak Muslim men and boys were killed after Bosnian Serb forces overran ​the UN-designated enclave.

He was also convicted over the 43-month siege of Sarajevo, during which about 10,000 people were killed.

Last week, EU enlargement commissioner Marta Kos postponed her visit to ⁠Serbia, which is a candidate country to join the bloc, because of what she said was the “glorification” of Mladic after his death, including the use of a government plane to return him to Serbia.

“The Western Balkan armed ‌conflicts of the 1990s were among Europe’s darkest moments in its recent history,” an EU spokesperson said in a statement on Monday (September 7).

“Any glorification of war criminals, genocide denial and revisionism contradict the most fundamental European values and have no place in the EU or in EU candidate countries.”

Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic, who dismissed Kos’ statement last week, did not attend the funeral. However, his son Danilo attended, along with Defence Minister Bratislav Gasic and Justice Minister Nenad Vujic.

PAINFUL REMINDER FOR THOUSANDS

In Sarajevo, meanwhile, the funeral rekindled painful memories of the war. ‌Telecom companies in Bosnia’s Bosniak-Croat federation blocked the signal of the two Bosnian Serb TV stations that carried live broadcast of ​the funeral and procession.

Bosnia’s Foreign Minister Elmedin Konakovic said the country will withdraw all staff from its embassy in Belgrade except for the ambassador and consul in protest at Serbia’s handling ⁠of the funeral, including the military escort of the body and the attendance of government officials.

“It is really horrible ⁠that this is taking place there [in Belgrade] because I know there are normal people who are against it,” said Zdravka Gvozdjar, a retired pharmacist whose 9-year-old son was killed during the Sarajevo ‌siege by a grenade fired by the Mladic-led forces, one among more than 1,000 children killed in the city.

“Mladic ... only deserved to be erased from memory for good, not to be ... promoted as a ​hero,” she said. “He should be remembered only as a butcher.”

World.title: West Bengal recorded 60,000 underage institutional deliveries in first six months of 2026: CM
World.content:
Expressing grave concern over the high prevalence of child marriages resulting in underage pregnancies and deliveries in the State, West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Monday (September 7, 2026) said that the State had recorded nearly 60,000 underage institutional deliveries in the first six months of 2026.

Details of underage institutional deliveries from January 1, 2026 to June 30, 2026 had been obtained from the State Health Department, and the numbers were alarming, Mr. Adhikari said.

“As a result of the previous government, we are now number one in two criteria across the country — marriage of girls below 18 years of age, and deliveries before 18 years of age. These numbers are so high that there aren’t enough jails in which to put these people,” the Chief Minister said, addressing media persons at the State Secretariat.

Mr. Adhikari read out the provisions of the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, adding that the law prohibited marriage with a child below 18 years of age. In such cases, “Police action will be initiated and arrests will be made,” he said.

The Chief Minister emphasised that the practice of child marriage could not be allowed to prevail, and the State Health Department would issue a show-cause notice to the offenders, especially the husband, who would have to provide documentary evidence within a month that both he and his ‘wife’ were adults in accordance with the law.

“If he fails to do so, the DGP (Director General of Police), who is sitting right next to me, will take action as per the law,” Mr. Adhikari said. The State government would stop delivering benefits under all Central and State government welfare schemes to these families, he said. Action would be taken against the priest and qazi who solemnised the marriage, and against other family members, he added.

Sharing district-wise details of cases of underage pregnancies, the Chief Minister said 12,847 institutional childbirths by underage girls were recorded in Murshidabad district alone, followed by South 24 Parganas at 4,178.

West Bengal has recorded the highest number of child marriages over the past few years, despite schemes rolled out to keep girls in schools. According to the Sample Registration Survey report published in September 2025, West Bengal recorded 6.3% of females getting married before the age of 18 years, whereas at the national level, 2.1% of females got married before the age of 18 years. Murshidabad remains a hotspot for child marriages. About 55.4% women in the district aged 20 to 24 years said they were married before the age of 18 years, according to the National Family Health Survey-5.

Experts working on the ground, however, say that child marriage is a complex issue involving not only parental or social pressure but also cases of elopement, and minor grooms. They warn that the arrest of husbands may result in placing a strain on already marginalised families, and impact marital relations adversely.

World.title: U.S-India space ties move from cooperation to co-creation: Ambassador Gor
World.content:
The India-U.S. space partnership is moving beyond traditional cooperation and towards joint development of technologies, missions and commercial opportunities, U.S. Ambassador to India Sergio Gor said at the opening of the ninth Bengaluru Space Expo (BSX) 2026 here on Monday.

Launching the U.S. pavilion at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (BIEC), Mr. Gor said the partnership was entering a new phase driven by co-creation between governments, space agencies, start-ups, and private industry.

“Our partnership with India is no longer just about cooperation. It is about co-creation. We are no longer just sharing data. We are co-designing instruments, co-funding start-ups, and co-authoring the future of human discovery,” he said.

The Ambassador also reiterated NASA’s invitation to ISRO to participate in the Moon base programme, saying the U.S. wanted India “by its side on the lunar surface.” He also emphasised the need for open and rules-based governance of space amid growing international competition.

The U.S. delegation included several major commercial space companies, including Amazon Leo, BlackSky, IONQ (Capella Space), L3 Harris, Pellucere Technologies, Vantor Inc., VAST Space, Viasat, and Voyager Technologies. Their participation is expecte to provide an opportunity for Indian start-ups and companies to explore partnerships, investment and access to international markets.

The expo also saw strong participation from other space-faring nations. Australian High Commissioner to India Philp Green highlighted the complementary strengths of Australia and India in the space sector and the potential for closer bilateral collaboration. He emphasised the unique chemistry of partnership between the countries, noting that while other nations bring heavyweights like NASA or Galileo to the table, Australia and India have complementary, contrasting strengths. “We have the things you don’t, and you have the things we don’t,’’ High Commissioner Green added.

Italian Ambassador Antonio Bartoli highlighted Italy’s expertise in advanced manufacturing and Europe’s long experience in space, with a large Italian delegation attending the expo to explore partnerships with India’s growing private space industry.

On the domestic front, Secretary, Department of Space, and ISRO chairman V. Narayanan, and IN-SPACe chairman Pawan Goenka outlined the policy and institutional priorities for expanding commercial space activity in India.

A key theme of the discussions was the shift from technology transfer to deeper joint development and joint ventures. The focus was also on enabling Indian space companies to access global markets and build international partnerships.

“Karnataka has a strong and vibrant innovation ecosystem with start-ups, industry, accademic institutions, and research centres working across a range of emerging technologies,” said N. Manjula, Secretary, Department of Electronics, IT, Biotechnology, and Science and Technology, Karnataka.

Later, a technical session chaired by Anupam Sharma of the Ministry of Defence and DRDO examined opportunities for private space companies to develop surveillance, intelligence and secure communication capabilities for defence applications. Bellatrix Aerospace co-founder Yash Karanam was among the industry participants.

The exhibition floor showcased the widening space ecosystem in India. The Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology (IIST) presented its research, student innovations and start-ups incubated through its ecosystem.

Industrial bodies were also pitching manufacturing opportunities. For instance: The Tamil Nadu Industrial Development Corporation (TIDCO), among others, showcased aerospace clusters and investment opportunities aimed at attracting global companies to establish manufacturing bases in India.

With international delegations, private space companies, start-ups, and government agencies converging at BSX 2026, the first day highlighted India’s transition from being primarily a space-service provider to an increasingly important partner in the global commercial space economy.

World.title: North Chennai residents seek Metro Rail connectivity via Perambur, better sanitation, and water supply facilities
World.content:
A new Metro Rail route connecting several parts of North Chennai, abandoning the proposed 2,100-tonne waste-to-energy plant at Kodungaiyur, reviving micro-compost and material recovery facilities, improving drinking water and sewerage infrastructure, preventing flooding, widening roads and improving transport, resolving housing and patta issues, strengthening healthcare, developing sports and green spaces, and creating better employment opportunities were among the demands made by residents of Perambur constituency.

These demands were consolidated into a study report at a public meeting organised by Federation of North Chennai Residents’ Welfare Associations on Sunday. Federation president T.K. Shanmugam said the demands should become a government action plan.

Tamil Nadu Housing Board Chairman V. Siva received the study report, Eriyum Manitha Urimaigal (Burning Human Rights) and assured action when he addressed the gathering.

The master plan seeks to permanently close the existing 50-tonne waste-to-energy plant, abandon the proposed new plant, and complete biomining of the Kodungaiyur dumpyard. It also calls for the revival of 168 micro-compost centres and 88 material recovery facilities and implementation of the federation’s ‘Green Chennai Initiative’ as an alternative waste management plan.

The plan proposed a new Metro Rail route connecting areas, including Basin Bridge, Vyasarpadi, Sathyamurthy Nagar, M.K.B. Nagar, Erukkancheri, Moolakadai, and Madhavaram. It also sought a constituency-level master plan for drinking water and sewerage, comprehensive flood mitigation measures, housing patta and registration solutions, primary healthcare facilities in every ward, improved sports facilities and green spaces, and welfare facilities for workers.

Federation’s Senthamizh Pari spoke on areas affected by the dumpyard and the 50-tonne plant, and described it as an evidence-based document.

World.title: Govt jacks up petrol price by Rs12.90, HSD by Rs3.72
World.content:
The government on Monday jacked up the price of petrol by Rs12.90 per litre while increasing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.72 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs358.77 per litre while HSD will cost Rs381.77 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on Sept 8 (Tuesday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Senate panel passes bill proposing death penalty for perpetrators of acid attacks
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Senate Standing Committee on Interior on Monday passed a series of key criminal law amendments, including a bill proposing the death penalty for acid attacks, as it moved to strengthen protections for vulnerable groups and public safety.

Chaired by Senator Faisal Saleem Rehman, the committee considered private members’ bills relating to acid crimes, protection of domestic workers, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) safety, anti-rape legislation and consumer protection.

The bills were passed despite opposition from State Minister for Interior Tallal Chaudhry, with PPP lawmakers also voting in favour.

The Criminal Law (Amendment) Bill moved by Senator Muhammad Abdul Qadir, seeking to amend Section 336B of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) relating to hurt caused by corrosive substances, was passed in the absence of the mover.

Citing “the recent incident of acid attack on a lady doctor in Quetta”, the bill states that despite the 2011 amendment, acid attacks continue to cause lifelong disfigurement and trauma.

It proposes the punishment of “death or imprisonment for life or imprisonment of not less than 14 years and a fine of Rs2 million” to serve as a strong deterrent.

The committee also unanimously passed the Criminal Laws (Amendment) Bill moved by Senator Sarmad Ali, proposing to criminalise the abuse of domestic workers.

The Statement of Objects and Reasons notes that “domestic workers constitute one of the most vulnerable segments of society, often subjected to physical violence, sexual abuse, forced labour, and other forms of mistreatment by employers.”

It adds that “existing provisions… do not specifically address the abuse arising from dependency and control inherent in domestic work settings”.

The proposed section covers physical violence, sexual harassment, threats, forced labour, wage theft, confiscation of identity documents, denial of food or medical care, and humiliating treatment.

The proposed penalties are “imprisonment for a term which may extend to 10 years and fine which may extend to Rs100,000” and “imprisonment for life and fine which may extend to Rs500,000” if the offence causes serious injury or death.

The bill also makes employers liable if abuse is committed by household members, “unless the employer took reasonable steps to prevent such abuse”.

Schedule II of the Criminal Procedure Code has also been amended to make the offence non-bailable and triable by a court of session.

In a move to address public safety hazards, the committee passed the Criminal Laws (Amendment) Act, moved by Senator Shahadat Awan, to amend Sections 286 and 286A of the PPC to criminalise the unauthorised transfer of LPG into smaller cylinders.

Noting that such decanting in residential areas and roadside setups poses severe risks, the bill increases the punishment under Section 286 from six months to two years and the fine from Rs1,000 to Rs100,000. Under Section 286A, imprisonment is increased from two to five years and the fine from Rs10,000 to Rs500,000.

The Statement of Objects and Reasons notes that “the decanting of LPG from larger cylinders into smaller domestic cylinders without proper safety measures has become a widespread practice in many parts of Pakistan.” It adds that “these unauthorised decanting operations are often conducted in residential areas, workshops, or roadside setups without adherence to safety standards, posing severe risks to public life and property.”

The bill proposes raising the punishment under Section 286 from six months to two years and the fine from Rs1,000 to Rs100,000. Under Section 286A, it proposes increasing the term of imprisonment from two to five years and the fine from Rs10,000 to Rs500,000.

“The proposed amendments aim to deter negligent and reckless conduct in the handling of explosive and hazardous substances, ensuring greater public safety and accountability.”

The committee also unanimously passed the Criminal Laws (Amendment) Bill, moved by Senator Samina Mumtaz Zehri, proposing to insert a new Section 338CA to make “Wrongful Detention of Dead Body” a punishable offence.

The Statement of Objects and Reasons highlights that “there have been numerous reports of private hospitals and clinics detaining the dead bodies of patients until their families settle outstanding medical bills”.

It cites examples of hospitals that “demand exorbitant advance deposits, sometimes as high as Rs2m to Rs4m” and “withhold dead bodies even when outstanding dues are as low as Rs100,000.”

The statement argues that this “not only causes immense psychological harm to grieving families but also denies the deceased the right to timely burial and dignified last rites, which is a fundamental religious obligation in Islam and other religions.” It adds that “the inviolability of human dignity does not cease upon death.”

The new section proposes a punishment of up to two years’ imprisonment and/or a fine of Rs500,000 for a first offence, and up to three years’ imprisonment and/or a fine of Rs1m for a second offence or detention beyond 24 hours. Exceptions are provided for autopsies or police investigations. The offence has been made compoundable by the legal heirs.

The Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) (Amendment) Bill, moved by Bushra Anjum Butt, was also passed, with the committee observing that legislation aimed at strengthening the legal framework against rape should receive appropriate government support.

On the consumer side, the committee passed the Islamabad Consumers Protection (Amendment) Bill, also moved by Senator Zehri, to bring private healthcare under the 1995 Act. The bill targets undisclosed fees, non-itemised billing and demands for advance deposits before emergency treatment, and requires hospitals to publicly display fee schedules and provide itemised bills.

The committee expressed serious concern over reports that former parliamentarians were being required to obtain a no-objection certificate (NOC) from the Ministry of Interior for the issuance of official passports and that their validity had been reduced from five years to one year. The minister of state for interior said only the internal approval procedure had been changed.

The chairman directed that existing law must not be violated and that official passports be issued with five-year validity in accordance with the law. Further deliberation was deferred.

The Ministry of Interior also briefed the committee on concerns regarding the unregulated use of social media by minors, stating that a high-powered committee was working on proposals to regulate its use by children.

Last week, a 35-year-old woman suffered burns when a man threw acid on her in Karachi’s Upper Gizri area.

Earlier in June, 29-year-old Mahnoor Nasir was seriously injured at the Quetta Civil Hospital when another employee threw acid on her. The attacker, later identified by police as Humayun Shah, was said to have been kil­led in an encounter after law enforcers tra­ced him as he attempted to flee on a bus.

Meanwhile, Dr Nasir was shifted to Karachi after receiving initial treatment in Quetta.

World.title: Interpol Pakistan issues 286 red notices in 7 months, 53 fugitives repatriated
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Interpol’s National Central Bureau (NCB) in Pakistan issued 286 Red Notices in the last seven months as part of efforts to track fugitives involved in murder, fraud, terrorism and human trafficking, according to Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) Director General Dr Usman Anwar.

A Red Notice is a request to law enforcement agencies by Interpol to locate and provisionally arrest a person pending extradition, surrender or similar legal action.

Anwar, who also heads NCB-Interpol Pakistan, reaffirmed the agency’s resolve on World Day of International Police Cooperation, adding that Islamabad would continue to strengthen collaboration with Interpol and global partners.

NCBs serve as each country’s focal point for all Interpol activities. They connect national law enforcement agencies with those in other countries and with the Interpol General Secretariat through a secure global police communications network known as I-24/7, allowing real-time access to databases and services.

Anwar said NCB-Interpol Pakistan issued a total of 290 Interpol notices during the period, including two Blue Notices and two Yellow Notices.

Yellow Notices are meant to help locate missing persons, often minors, or identify people who are unable to identify themselves, while Blue Notices are issued to collect additional information.

Of the 286 Red Notices, 225 were issued for suspects wanted in murder and attempted murder cases, while another 33 were issued for individuals wanted in kidnapping, corruption, robbery and cybercrime cases.

The bureau also issued 19 Red Notices for financial fraud and deception, six for human trafficking and three for terrorism.

Through international cooperation, 53 fugitives wanted in Pakistan for serious crimes were arrested in different countries and extradited to Pakistan during the same seven-month period.

“Today’s crimes are increasingly international. Cybercrime, fugitives and stolen goods driven by organised groups — none of these respect borders,” Anwar told Dawn.

“We seek information from other NCBs to help investigations in Pakistan, and we share our criminal data to assist other countries.”

He added that NCBs were critical because they could trigger law enforcement action in their respective countries and work directly with counterparts, even between states without diplomatic relations.

“When a crime goes beyond our national jurisdiction, we need international support to solve it. Interpol provides that platform,” he stated.

According to Interpol’s framework, NCBs contribute national crime data to global databases in accordance with national laws. Red Notices, for example, alert police in all 196 member countries to wanted persons.

NCB Pakistan works with domestic law enforcement agencies, other NCBs and sub-bureaus worldwide, as well as the General Secretariat’s offices, to coordinate cross-border investigations, operations and arrests. The FIA director general noted that regional cooperation was growing as countries combined resources to tackle shared threats.

“We are also building capacity at home. NCBs develop training programmes for national police to raise awareness of Interpol’s tools and databases so that our officers can use them effectively on the ground,” Anwar said.

“FIA NCB-Interpol Pakistan remains committed to ensuring that no fugitive finds safe haven abroad. Through I-24/7 and our network of partners, we will keep pursuing criminals and bringing them to justice.”

In April this year, Interpol issued Red Notices against Bahria Town owner Malik Riaz and his son Ali Riaz, Nat­i­onal Accountability Bur­eau (NAB) Chairman Lt General (retired) Nazir Ahmed said.

Last month, the National Cybercrime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) arrested two suspects and initiated the process for obtaining Red Notices for the remaining four alleged members of the “Tycoon2FA Cybercrime Network”.

World.title: Pakistan at ‘very start’ of Test rebuilding process, says bowling coach Noffke
World.content:
Pakistan are at the “very start” of rebuilding their Test side, bowling coach Ashley Noffke said on Monday, as the team attempts to move past a tumultuous week that has seen sweeping changes to the squad and a shake-up of its coaching staff.

“Every nation has a life cycle, and there’ll be moments where they play really great cricket for long periods and then older players will move out and younger players will come in. And we’re at the very start of that process,” Noffke told reporters at Edgbaston.

The contrast with England, who are attempting to complete a 3-0 series sweep after emphatic victories at Headingley and Lord’s, could hardly be starker.

While Pakistan have brought in a new interim head coach in Mike Hesson, made wholesale changes to their squad and sent Noffke to England at short notice, the hosts have been able to build on a settled pace attack led by Jofra Archer, who says he is finally enjoying a period of stability after years of injury.

Pakistan’s changes have opened the door for young fast bowlers Razaullah and Mohammad Imran Jr, with Noffke viewing their presence in England as part of a longer-term plan rather than simply an emergency response to two defeats.

“They’re young guys. They haven’t experienced England conditions and they’re over here to learn and grow,” he said. “I think with any life cycle of any cricket team, you need to take a forward-thinking approach to what we might need in the future. I think other teams have been doing that and it’s now our turn to bring young guys over, make sure they get accustomed to conditions that are different to theirs at home.”

Both bowlers offer Pakistan something that has been missing from their attack during the series — pace. Noffke said they were “certainly closer to the 140 mark” than some of the quicks Pakistan had previously used.

Imran Jr, a left-armer, and Razaullah, a right-armer with a different action, could also provide variety to an attack that has relied heavily on veteran seamer Mohammad Abbas.

“Abbas has obviously bowled amazingly through this series and we need to support him as best we can,” Noffke said.

Noffke himself was thrust into the Test set-up at short notice, saying he received a message “at 3am” informing him that management was sending him to England.

Asked whether he had been given an explanation for the sweeping changes to the squad, he said: “Not really.”

“It’s not my job to be in consultation with where they see who’s in and who’s out. That’s obviously the selection panel,” he said.

“As we’ve already asked Mike [Hesson] in previous interviews, he’s only just come into that phase. So, like we said before, it’s unsettling, but it’s about getting on with it, focusing on what’s ahead of us as a Test-playing squad and trying to develop in all areas.”

The uncertainty surrounding Pakistan has also been compounded by an internal PCB disciplinary inquiry into the conduct of some players announced on Monday.

Noffke said he knew no more about the matter than the media did.

“As much as you do. And I can be really honest in that — I don’t know too much,” he said. “I sit outside of that decision-making model above us as coaches.”

He said the coaching staff had attempted to keep the players focused on the cricket rather than the developments surrounding them.

“There’s obviously a feeling of uncertainty, but they’ve just got back on the job,” Noffke said. “I’ve been really impressed with the level of calmness that they’ve taken over the last couple of days once we’ve given them time to talk.”

The Australian said Pakistan’s immediate strategy was straightforward: “good Test cricket”, discipline, bowling in good areas and building long partnerships with the bat.

Asked whether Pakistan risked becoming a laughing stock following the events on and off the field and whether the team needed to restore some pride, Noffke said performances were the only meaningful answer.

“Well, you only install pride with really good cricket, don’t you?” he said. “There’s no question that we need to develop our game. Our Test game needs to improve. But that doesn’t mean that we should be worried about that.”

England, meanwhile, are preparing for the possibility of completing a clean sweep with a fast-bowling unit that has been one of the defining features of the series.

Archer, who returned to Test cricket in July last year after more than four years away, believes he is now in a “good place” following a succession of career-threatening injuries.

The Barbados-born quick arrived in England in 2015 and four years later spearheaded the attack during England’s dramatic World Cup triumph at Lord’s, while also starring in the 2019 Ashes.

But an elbow problem subsequently developed, followed by back injuries, and Archer was sidelined from Test cricket from February 2021 until July 2025.

The 31-year-old, who continues to play all three international formats, said his long periods away from the game had also brought unexpected benefits.

“The time when I was injured, I really got away from cricket,” he told the BBC on Monday. “It’s all been a blur. I didn’t realise how long the time out was, either.”

Archer said the enforced breaks allowed him to spend more time at home in Barbados after moving to England.

“I got to spend some time at home, because, moving over, I never really got more than a couple of weeks,” he said. “To spend a month here and there, it was really nice.”

“I’d be lying if I didn’t say I had a good time away from everything. Now, everything is really nice. My body is in a good place, the team is in a good place and everyone is in a good place. I just want to play cricket.”

Archer has played a key role in England’s two victories over Pakistan and will be central to their bid for a 3-0 result at Edgbaston.

His presence has also added further weight to an England pace attack featuring Ollie Robinson, Josh Tongue and Gus Atkinson, with the group beginning to draw comparisons with England’s celebrated “Fab Four” of Matthew Hoggard, Steve Harmison, Simon Jones and Andrew Flintoff, who helped secure the 2005 Ashes.

Pakistan, by contrast, are still deciding whether to field four seamers or retain a spinner, with Noffke saying the decision would depend on the pitch and weather.

“We’ve got some really good options now to select in terms of the four seamers, our spinner that can bat. There are some great selection dilemmas, which is nice,” he said.

The Edgbaston pitch has plenty of grass, but Noffke expects it to be a good surface.

“It looks a good surface. There’s plenty of grass on it, though,” he said.

For Pakistan, however, the significance of Wednesday’s Test extends beyond avoiding a series whitewash.

With new faces being introduced amid considerable upheaval, Edgbaston could offer an early glimpse of the side Noffke believes is only now beginning the process of rebuilding.

World.title: Karachi police briefly detain protesting family members of Pakistani sailors held hostage by Somali pirates
World.content:
